# Changelog

All notable product changes. Format: [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com). Design-side changes live in `04-docs/CHANGELOG.md`.

## [Unreleased]

## [2.614.0] — 2026-10-31

Field app (new APK) plus server and web. The field-app bug round FB-022, 023, 028, 029, 030, 031, 033.

### Fixed
- **FB-022 · a reading that would not sync.** The server no longer fails a whole batch when it refuses a reading that has a photo; it answers with the reason. A reading lower than the meter's last is accepted with a "Lower than last" warning and is not billed until a clerk checks it; the next bill counts from the last good reading (4,812 → 4,790 → 4,900 bills 88). Several readings in one cycle are all kept and the latest good one bills. The Sync screen lists items that keep failing under "Needs attention", with a reference DevOps can search for and "Send again".
- **FB-023 · money on field jobs.** Employees see the balance; contractors never do. The balance is checked when a money screen opens, the last figure is kept offline with its age, payments say Posted or Cleared correctly, and a disconnect stops when a posted payment clears the balance. New "Balance & payments" tick on the work-order template; the template's other four ticks are now honoured on the phone; disconnect jobs show the payment plan and the latest notice. "Partly done" from the web phone screen no longer fails.
- **FB-028 · work orders raised on site.** A raised job is the technician's at once and on their Today list, with "Send now". New "Reconnect limit" on the work-order template (default $25.00): a raised reconnect is allowed at or under it, otherwise "Still owes $… Leave it off." A raised disconnect stops on a cleared balance, a running notice or a protected account. The office is told each time.
- **FB-029 · jobs further ahead.** The job list has Today · two next days · Later · All; tab counts match their cards.
- **FB-030 · history.** A technician sees their own last 14 days: Completed (Today · This week · Earlier) opens the full record on phones, jobs closed on the web or another phone appear, and My reads opens each reading. A new or reset phone is refilled with 14 days. Photos stay on the device 3 days, then load from the server on tap.
- **FB-031 · help documents.** A job's document downloads, stays for offline use and opens in the phone's own app ("Open with…"). Empty rows say "No file attached." or "No number."; a template cannot be published with them; help added later reaches open jobs.
- **FB-033 · availability.** Available / On break / Off duty on the phone reaches the office with a "since" time; the office's "Unavailable" wins; the assign picker and schedule board warn about an off-duty technician.

### Added
- Phone: `expo-intent-launcher`, `expo-sharing` (document opening).
- New phone wording in all eleven languages.

## [2.613.0] — 2026-10-31

Server and web. Field-app fixes of the current round (FB-022, FB-023) are partly in this build; their APK follows when the round is done.

### Payments
- Statement lines show whose cheque was matched ("RET1029-01 CHK 4102 → Clara Castillo · AC-…"); Match to payment opens searching the cheque number and lets the clerk edit the Bank memo.
- Match to payment and Bank fee also work from the Reconciliation page, so a bounce reversed by hand later still lines up with the bank (never reversed twice).
- Plans & Rates charges have an "NSF fee" tick (one per plan).
- The counter warns when the same card/ACH reference repeats on one account and day.
- "Force close" is greyed out for non-administrators.
- After recording a payment: "Recorded. Receipt # PY-…" plus at most one warning.
- A file already loaded is refused in plain words on every import, never "HTTP 409".

## [2.612.0] — 2026-10-30

Server and web only — no field-app change, no APK.

### Payments
- **Pay for several accounts:** Record payment's "Pay for" switch splits one cheque across a landlord's units' bills (Left to allocate must reach $0.00; leftover becomes the landlord's credit); "Pay units" on a master account.
- **Match to several deposits** on Reconcile a bank statement: tick deposits until they equal the bank line exactly.
- A Finance Executive may reverse a bounced payment from the statement's Match to payment (only there); the Match form shows the NSF fee first.
- The statement import asks for the opening and closing balance, so the statement shows bank vs books.
- A receipt for an account in credit prints "Credit on account $X".
- Payments files may carry a **Network** column: each store network banks in its own daily deposit batch and reads "Store · <network>".
- Imports: "Save mapping as template" with a name; a later file with the same columns is mapped automatically.
- Walk fixes: money columns right-aligned on the several-deposits dialog; payment History allow-list names the ruled bounce fields.

## [2.611.0] — 2026-10-30

Server and web only — no field-app change, no APK.

### Templates (CR-199)
- Templates screen redesigned from the PO's drawing: list with channel chips, languages, variants, status and row actions; one action bar; editor beside a live preview; + New variant / Duplicate as variant (channel × language × customer type); History with Make live again (legal notices go for approval); Rich / Plain email with a branded header and logo link (Settings › Company › Brand); Pay now / View bill buttons; messages go in the customer's preferred language.
- Walk fixes: the utility's own edited wording reaches customers; all 87 templates reachable; dialogs return focus; preview links open a new tab.

### Notifications and reconnection
- Visit messages by email when one is on file; past-due reminder print only when nothing digital reaches the customer; reminder rule off skips and carries on; "Retried to a new address"; every message type named in Already sent.
- Put service back on = a reconnect request; a reconnecting case reads "Reconnecting"; a restored account returns to Active.

### Address search (CR-200)
- Portal Start service and Ask us for something suggest addresses; pick the apartment in a building (an apartment in Premises is a move-in); staff searches match word by word ("12 Oak 2B"); the request head and Approve window show the apartment.

### Payments (lockbox audit and payments audit by level)
- A $0.00 deposit batch reconciles in one click and its payments clear; returned cheques and bank fees on the statement post to the books (books match the bank); future-dated statement lines refused; "Matched · off by $X".
- NSF penalty from Account › Unit › Plan › charge code, one per bounced payment, untick with a reason; Bank memo on a reversal; a bounce on a closed account still reverses; proper bounce email and letter.
- Lockbox imports carry the Lockbox method; CSV only; duplicate cheques and receipts held; imports add up; risky rows held, warned or refused; plain messages; a file loaded twice refused at upload.
- Counter: Main office opens; a counter lists its own payments; duplicate warning on any tender when the bill is already paid; Receipt #, Taken by, Print receipt; no raw codes.
- Account held credit shown (−$5.00) with Refund and Apply now; late fee refused at sign-off when a payment landed after drafting; late-fee list loads and searches by name.
- Guest pay lockout uses the trusted address (security); bill number accepted with spaces or lower case.
- Master pays units on the server (screen awaits the PO's mock-up approval); Payments list bulk Send receipts and Reapply.

## [2.610.0] — 2026-10-29

Server and web only — no field-app change, no APK.

### Changed — Settings › Accounting
- **A used GL account's code can be changed** by a System Admin (`CR-196-BRC10`): a confirmation shows how many bills and payments use it, and the new code shows everywhere, past reports included, with "formerly 4150" kept on the account. The type stays locked.
- **GL mapping is one list** (`CR-197-BRC10`): Billing and Payments & balances, with search, filters, a "not mapped" count, Add / Edit / Disable. A service can post revenue to a different account per customer class; refunds can post to their own account; a discount now posts to its own account (`DEF-BIL-10648`). Issued bills never change.

### Added — customer messages
- **Service disconnected / Service restored** email and text when a cut is committed or service is restored, with the reading, balance, reconnection fee, total to restore, pay link and safety advice (`DEF-NOT-10649`).
- **Work order logged** when a job is raised without a date, and **preparation instructions** per work-order template in the logged, booked and moved messages; disconnect templates send no visit messages (`DEF-WRK-10652`).
- **Past-due reminder** goes by email and text under its Settings rule, a printed letter only when nothing digital reaches the customer; history records "Sent" only for real sends (`DEF-PAY-10651`).

### Added — text messages (`CR-198-BRC10`)
- **SMS through one shared platform Twilio account** — signed delivery reports, STOP replies block the number and turn off the account's text tick. ⚠ Live only once each server has the Twilio secrets, `PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` and A2P 10DLC registration.

### Changed — Messages needing attention (`DEF-NOT-10650`)
- Opens on what needs attention, bulk re-queue (up to 500), error details, and "Fix address and retry" for one message.

## [2.609.0] — 2026-10-28

### Fixed — photos reach the office on any connection (`DEF-FLD-10640`, FB-015, PO option A)
- **Photos upload on mobile data and wi-fi** by default (the old switch was saved as `1` and read as `true`, so it never worked). The setting is now *Photos on wi-fi only*, off by default; *"Photos wait for wi-fi."* shows only while it is on.
- **A completed work order shows every photo** — job-level ones, all of a step's, and readings' — on the Checklist tab.

### Added — payment check before a step, and a paid close (`DEF-WRK-10641`, `DEF-FLD-10642`, FB-013, PO 2026-10-28)
- **Template editor:** *Check payment* per step, with fresh minutes (default 5) and an optional fee code; the editor no longer erases it on save.
- **Phone:** a fresh read showing the balance cleared stops the step — *"Balance cleared. Do not disconnect."* — with *Close — payment received* or *Hand back to office*. A stale balance only warns, as before.
- **New close outcome *Not done — payment received*** with an editable remark; the server refuses it without a fresh cleared balance and stores what the phone saw and its own read. The office sees the outcome, remark and money, can filter for it on the Field desk results, and gets a notice.

### Fixed — found in the web walkthrough
- *+ Filter* no longer opens behind the sidebar (`DEF-SHL-10643`).
- The web phone's close screen offers the paid close exactly when the phone does, without a photo warning (`DEF-WRK-10644`).
- The payment-check boxes keep their labels once filled (`DEF-WRK-10645`); the outcome panel uses the utility's own date and time format (`DEF-WRK-10646`).

## [2.608.0] — 2026-10-28

### Changed — field app: certificate pinning dropped as a go-live requirement (`CR-195-BRC10`, PO "start A1")
- **The extra pinning check is off in every build**, beta and store; the phone relies on Android's standard certificate check, which still refuses a fake server. The pinning code stays, dormant — switching it on is configuration only.
- Settings › About no longer says *Beta build — certificate check off*. A build's server must be `https://`.
- **Staff portal:** Settings › Security no longer shows *Field app certificates*; the stored lists are kept and return with `SBH_FIELD_APP_PINNING_ENABLED`.

## [2.607.0] — 2026-10-28

### Fixed — field app: a photo added to a saved reading is no longer refused (`DEF-FLD-10637`, FB-019)
- *Add photo* on a saved reading sends one item — the photo, naming its reading — instead of an empty extra item the server refused as *"This photo is damaged. Take it again."* Old refused items of that kind clear at the next sync.
- The office reading lists the photo, marked *Added after saving*.

### Fixed — field app: a phone clock that is wrong never refuses work (`DEF-FLD-10639`, FB-014, PO 2026-10-28)
- Every send carries the phone's clock; the server moves every time in it onto its own clock — a job finished at 12:07 on a phone 5 minutes fast is stored as 12:02. Labour minutes are unchanged.
- Over 5 minutes out, the Sync screen says *"Phone clock is 5 min fast. Fix the time."* and the office job shows *Phone clock — Was 5 min fast*; the work still goes.
- A refused item no longer holds back the rest of its job, so a close reaches the office at once.

### Deferred
- **Asset history on the phone** stays empty (`DEF-FLD-10638`, FB-011) — deferred by the PO; when built: the last 10 visits, at most 24 months.

## [2.606.0] — 2026-10-27

### Fixed — field app: reading photos (`DEF-FLD-10630` FB-002, `DEF-FLD-10631` FB-003)
- **The camera screen shows the live camera** with the stamp over it; *Take the photo* takes it from that view, and the stamp is still burned in.
- **Every photo shows as a thumbnail** on the reading. Before saving: open it full size, **Retake** or **Remove**. After saving: view and **Add photo** only (PO 2026-10-27).
- **The photo count is right** — a photo added after saving, or a reading changed and saved again, no longer reads *"0 photos"*.

### Fixed — field app: the position is captured automatically (`DEF-FLD-10632`, `DEF-MET-10633`, FB-003, PO 2026-10-27)
- Opening the route or the camera asks Android for location, or to turn Location on; refused for good, *"Location is off for this app."* with *Open settings*.
- Saving waits up to 10 seconds for a position, then saves without. A position arriving within 5 minutes is added as its own record — *"Position added at 18:35 ±10 m"* — never as if it were there at save.
- A photo keeps the position of the moment it was taken. The office reading shows **Where it was read**, with *added at* for a late one.

### Fixed — field app: Scan finds any meter of the utility (`DEF-FLD-10634`, FB-009, MQ-046)
- Scan and *Enter manually* look on the phone, then — with a signal — across the whole utility, and open the meter on an exact serial or asset number. Offline: *"Not on this phone. A signal searches the whole utility."*

### Fixed — office (web)
- **A refusal's door-hanger photo shows on the Signature panel** — *Photo uploading*, then the picture with View (`DEF-WRK-10635`).
- **Settings › Company logo** reads *"On file: PNG, 2 KB."* — no database id (`DEF-TEN-10636`).

## [2.605.0] — 2026-10-27

### Fixed — field app: sync that sends nothing (`DEF-FLD-10624`, PO "start A to F")
- **The phone renews its one-hour sign-in whenever it has signal.** The renewal was never called, so an hour after sign-in every call was refused on the phone and nothing reached the server, while the screen said ONLINE.
- **The Sync screen says why nothing went** — *Could not reach the server.*, *Sign in again.*, *The server had a problem. Trying again.*, *Run timed out. Try again.*
- *Last reached the server* moves on a successful send; **Sync now** retries at once; one late item no longer holds back its whole job; every sync step has a time limit, so a stuck step cannot block the next press.

### Fixed — field app: route readings that never left the phone (`DEF-FLD-10629`, FB-004)
- **The reader's sending pass is renewed before sending**; when it cannot be, *Sign in again to send.* with a button, never silence.
- **Sync now shows *Sending…*, then *Sent 12.*** or the reason; photos read *Waiting for readings* until their readings are sent; *On this phone* counts routes.

### Fixed — signature and close (`DEF-WRK-10625`, `DEF-FLD-10626..10628`, PO 2026-10-27)
- **A refusal with its door-hanger photo is accepted**; the office sees the photo once it uploads.
- **A signing pad** — the customer signs on the phone, and the mark travels like a photo.
- **Close shows Arrived and Finished**, pre-filled and adjustable in 5-minute steps; Arrived defaults to the first work on the job when it was never tapped.
- *Captured by* shows the technician's name, never an id.
- ⚠ The signing pad is a new native module: this needs a new APK.

## [2.604.0] — 2026-10-27

### Security — the VAPT round, code side (PO rulings of 2026-10-27; `09-infra/06-vapt-remediation-2026-10.md` step 1)
- **Company logos are PNG or JPG only** (`DEF-TEN-10618`): Settings › Company › Brand offers PNG and JPG, refuses an SVG before upload with *"SVG files aren't accepted. Use PNG or JPG."*, and the server refuses it again. A file whose contents are not what its name says is refused (*"File contents don't match its type."*). The placeholder reads *"Logo — PNG or JPG, max 2 MB"*. A JPG logo prints on bills. A utility that already had an SVG logo keeps it: screens and bills now show its cleaned PNG copy.
- **A firewall block says so** (`DEF-SHL-10619`): *"This request was blocked for security. Contact support."* instead of *"We couldn't reach SMART360 Next"* — once DevOps adds the firewall's custom response (step 1-A).
- **A locked sign-in says how long to wait** (`DEF-IDN-10620`): *"Too many wrong attempts. Try again in 15 minutes."* — the minutes are the utility's own Settings › Security value, on the web and the field app. The web no longer shows a fixed "5 attempts / 15 minutes" line.
- **Rate limits in the app** (`DEF-SHL-10621`): per person 300 calls a minute, per utility 3,000, heavy actions (exports, imports, bill-run steps, bulk actions, report and runbook runs) 10 a minute per person, field-app syncs 120 a minute per phone — each changeable on the server without a release (`RATE_USER_PER_MIN`, `RATE_TENANT_PER_MIN`, `RATE_HEAVY_PER_MIN`, `RATE_DEVICE_PER_MIN`). Past a limit: *"Too many requests. Wait a moment."*; the web retries a read once, and the field app holds its sync and sends it again — nothing is lost. ⚠ The counters are shared between servers only when `CACHE_URL` points at Redis.
- **Evidence for the HTTP-methods finding** (`DEF-SHL-10622`): `pytest tests/test_vapt_http_methods.py -v -s` — every API address refuses every method it does not offer with 405, and a page on another site gets no permission to call the API.

## [2.603.1] — 2026-10-26

### Fixed — field app: "No signal" while online (`DEF-FLD-10617`, PO "B. Switch the check off for the beta")
- **The beta APK no longer checks the server's certificate**, so activation and sign-in work whatever the live server's issuer is. Settings › About says *Beta build — certificate check off*. The store build keeps the check on and cannot be built with it off.
- **Each failure says what it is**: a refused certificate reads *Can't verify the server. Contact the office.*; a server missing the door, or answering something that is not its JSON, reads *The server needs an update.*; only a real dropped connection reads *No signal* — on Activate, Sign in and the first-sync screen.
- **Before go-live**: confirm the real issuer from the browser padlock, put it and one backup in the build and in Settings › Security, and ship the store build with the check on.

## [2.603.0] — 2026-10-26

### Added — refused field work is kept on both the phone and the server (`CR-194-BRC10`, PO "store on both")
- **The office keeps a copy of every field item the server refuses** — a reading on a job given to someone else, a tick on a cancelled job, a route reading with no unit. The phone still keeps it to fix and resend, and the fixed resend still posts once; the office's copy then reads *Sent again*.
- **Work → From the field → Refused work**: Technician · Job · What · Reason · When · Status, filters and search by job number; open one to see the work as sent (a reading's value and unit, the photographs, the note), **Mark reviewed** or **Apply to job**.
- **The phone says so**: a refused row on the Sync screen adds *The office will review this.* — only when the server actually kept the copy.

## [2.598.0] — 2026-10-23

### Added
- **Portal application fee paid online at submission** (`CR-191-BRC10`). A portal application whose fee is above $0.00 is paid by card on its last step ("Pay $10.00 and submit"); the request exists only once the card is approved. The customer sees "Your card is charged $10.00 now." and "The fee is not refunded." before paying. The fee is posted as a card counter receipt to fee revenue at submission; approval asks for nothing more. $0.00 means no card step. A utility with a fee and no card provider connected shows "Card payment is not available." One charge per application even across a reload, a double press or a failed save (`DEF-PAY-10554`).
- **Accessible customer PDFs** (`DEF-BIL-10546`, portal accessibility F-06): bills, final bills, statements and agreements are tagged PDF/UA-1 files with language, title, headings, table headers and embedded Liberation Sans. veraPDF: 24 of 24 samples pass (was 0). Money and wording are identical to the previous PDF. New documents only.

### Changed (accessibility work in progress, groups still building)
- Secondary grey text is darker (`#6b6767`, 5.58:1) and input borders clearer (`#8c8888`, 3.50:1) across the product; text on a too-light brand colour turns dark, and Company → Profile refuses a brand colour no text can be read on (`DEF-CWP-10544`, `DEF-CWP-10545`).
- My details refuses a malformed phone or ZIP and removes an emptied phone (`DEF-CWP-10549`, server half).

### Deploy
- Rebuild the backend image: it adds WeasyPrint, Pango/HarfBuzz and the Liberation Sans fonts (`09-infra/05-tagged-customer-pdfs.md`). Migration `portal/0019` adds three draft columns.

With no rule, the technician taps *Create work order* on the phone, or the office does it from *Work › From the field › Route findings*. A finding becomes a job only once. ## [2.590.0] — 2026-10-21

- **Undoing a bank reconciliation puts its payments back to Posted** (PO 2026-10-21, *"Allow, back to Posted"*). Example: the 14 Oct $800 batch reconciled on 16 Oct and then undone reads Posted with no clearing date; reconciled again on 17 Oct it reads Cleared, 17 Oct. The balance does not move at any step. The database allows Cleared → Posted only during that undo, for that batch.
- **Payment reports now use the posting date** (PO 2026-10-21): *Payments by method*, the payments download, tax collected and the Payments summary mix. A card payment taken 14 Oct and reconciled 16 Oct shows on 14 Oct, before and after reconciliation (`DEF-PAY-10321`, `DEF-PAY-10342`).
- **Customer portal:** a Posted or Cleared payment reads *Received*; a cancelled one reads *Canceled* instead of *Processing* (`DEF-CWP-10341`).
- **Move-in, new account and new connection** no longer ask for a clearing date or say the deposit reads $0.00 until it clears; the deposit is Posted when taken (`DEF-CUS-10324`).
- **Payment page:** a deposit matched to a single bank line now reads Reconciled, not *Banked, not matched* (`DEF-PAY-10323`).
- **Field technician app** (`CR-187-BRC10`, new `field-app/`, React Native): Phase 0 and Phase 1 — shared design values, three themes, the component kit, the phone database and sync engine, sign-in for several technicians on one phone, navigation for all 92 screens, 11 languages, crash and usage reporting with a privacy filter. Not yet released to any store.
- **Work server:** the technician's phone is now told when a job is reassigned, unassigned or cancelled (`DEF-WRK-10347`); a cancelled job no longer shows in the technician's day (`DEF-WRK-10348`); one sync request can carry many jobs.

## [2.589.0] — 2026-10-21

- **Every payment is Posted when taken and Cleared when the bank is reconciled** (`CR-186-BRC10`; PO 2026-10-21). Counter, lockbox, card, bank transfer, providers and Invoice Cloud: a payment is saved **Posted** with its posting date, applied to the bill and journalled at once. It becomes **Cleared**, with the clearing date, when its deposit batch is reconciled with the bank statement. A Posted payment can be cancelled; a Cleared one is refused with "Issue a refund or credit". A payment dated in a closed month is accepted, keeps its own date for late fees, and its accounting entry goes into the first open month.
- **One deposit batch per till or per provider per day, all payment types together**, stamped the moment the payment is posted. Example: Dana's cash $300 + cheques $500 = one batch of $800. Invoice Cloud and Paymentus each get their own daily batch. The batch page shows totals by payment type.
- **The balance counts only Posted and Cleared payments** (plus the minus row a bounce writes), refunds and credits. Failed, cancelled and processing payments never count (`DEF-PAY-10340`, which made a cancelled or failed payment lower the balance). A $150 bill less $120 posted reads **$30.00** everywhere, including Invoice Cloud's Consumer Info, and a $20 refund makes it **$50.00**.
- **Invoice Cloud:** Make Payment saves the payment as Posted and replies **"posted"**, with the payment number and its batch ID. The "not cleared" note is gone. A payment naming a bill already paid in full becomes account credit instead of being refused.
- The payments status filter now lists Cancelled.

## [2.588.2] — 2026-10-21

- **New World / Logos receipt file now in New World's own format** (`DEF-INT-10304`; PO 2026-10-21): root `<ROOT>`, every field an attribute, VoidedFlag `0`/`1`, dates MM/DD/YYYY, every required attribute always present (`""` when empty), the four card fields always present and always empty, and no ProjectCode on the transaction line. The partner receipts API serves the same shape. Every file is checked against the template before it reaches the SFTP folder or the API; a failing file is not sent, the run is marked failed with the reasons, and an alert goes out. A day with no payments still sends an empty file. Test file for 20 Oct validated; it needs a fresh SFTP test (the earlier test used the old format).

## [2.585.0] — 2026-10-17

**Late fee** (PO 2026-10-17).
- **The bill run now adds the late fee** (`DEF-BIL-10200`): once per account per billing period, when $25.00 or more is still unpaid after the due date plus grace (judged by the date the money arrived). Shown in the Check step ("3 accounts · late fees $23.13"), waivable one account at a time, never taxed, never charged twice. Accounts on a live payment plan get no late fee (supersedes BR-BIL-073's fee clause).
- **A late fee can be a flat amount** as well as a percentage with a minimum (`DEF-BIL-10201`): flat $10.00 on $900 overdue → $10.00; 1.5% min $5 on $542.10 → $8.13 (unchanged). A 0% penalty with no minimum is refused.
- The late-fee pane no longer shows a decision pill or dead checkboxes (`DEF-BIL-10202`).

**Move-in searches all units** (PO 2026-10-17, `DEF-CUS-10190`): step 1 searches every unit with its status. Vacant or closed → move in. Active, vacation hold or marked for disconnect → *Start move-out* first (dated the day before the move-in); disconnected → *Start close-out*; then *Back to move-in* with the opening readings carried over. Move-out in progress and pending activation are shown but blocked; removed units are not listed. A move-out now ends a vacation hold (cancelling its jobs) and stops an open disconnect case as "customer left"; debt stays on the old account. A move-in onto a cut unit raises a reconnect job. Six walk bugs fixed (`DEF-CUS-10191`–`10196`).

**Solar and battery bill the sum of installed kW** (PO 2026-10-17, `DEF-RAT-10220`): every size class carries its capacity as data (built-in sizes filled in automatically; sizes a utility adds take their own, up to 4 decimals). Units compare without regard to capitals (`KW` = `kW`). Worked: 47.84 kW + 10 kW at $14.00/kW = **$809.76** (was 2 × $14 = $28.00). A size with no capacity is refused naming the asset; a FLAT rate priced per kW shows a warning. The one-time bill's Services row shows the kW billed (`DEF-BIL-10221`).
- **After deploying:** check each solar/battery size a utility added under Settings → Size classes has its capacity.

## [2.583.0] — 2026-10-15

- **Usage tab, Month by month, now shows each month's readings** (`DEF-CUS-10162`, `DEF-CUS-5146`; PO 2026-10-15): Previous reading, Current reading, Read on, Source and a Check chip (High, Low, Flagged, Estimated, Zero, OK). An account with two or more services gets one row per service per month. A month with no reading says *No reading* and nothing else; a month with several readings says so. Walk: A-10432 Jul 2026 Electric · 842 kWh · 14,612 · 15,454 · 07/31/2026 · Manual entry (AMI) · **High**.
- Logged: a bill-run estimate dated before a later actual reading is counted twice in monthly usage (`DEF-MET-10163`), the likely reason two months can show the same figure.

## [2.573.0] — 2026-10-13

_Fix a bill, revamped (CR-180-BRC10): Bills · Fix · Check · Send._

**Look in build 2.573.0**:
- **Billing → Fix a bill, step Bills**:
  - choose **One customer** (one bill or several months) or **Bulk** (a billing run or a price mistake);
  - find the account by name, number or address;
  - tick the bills;
  - drafts and bills already in a case are listed as left out.
- **Fix**: one *What was wrong* table.
  - Add a row for each correction: wrong reading, plan, rate, tax, a charge missed or billed in error, discount, deposit, period or service, theft, goodwill, or a reprint of name, address, unit, meter or template.
  - Pick what it should be and which bills it applies to.
  - *What happens* is worked out from all the rows (re-price > credit only > reprint only).
  - The old and new bill sit side by side, by service and rate type, line by line.
- **Check**: what the customer owes now, the existing bills (paid, moves to the new bill, still owed) and, for finance, the entries, the change per account and the posting month. A closed month posts to the earliest open one.
- **Send**: tick *I checked the amounts*, then *Send for approval*. Nothing is saved before this. The approver presses *Approve and issue*, which writes the credit note and the new bill, two balanced entries per bill, the payment moved to the new bill (any leftover is account credit), the delivery queued and the audit rows.

### Changed
- `CR-180-BRC10` Fix a bill revamp. It was walked on 19 of 20 scenarios (J-FIX-TWENTY, `05-prototype/fix-a-bill-walk-2026-10-12/`) and checked against bills, ledger, payments, delivery and audit.

### Fixed during the walk
- `DEF-BIL-10077`…`10090`, `10096`…`10103` (22 defects; see the walk README).

### Known
- `DEF-BIL-10091` **Bulk is slow.** Each step takes about 3 minutes on 38 bills, and production cuts a request off at 60 s, so a bulk fix over a large run will fail there until it runs in the background. One-customer fixes are unaffected.
- A run of 100 bills (S17) was not walked; no such run exists on the demo data.

## [2.566.0] — 2026-10-11

_Fourteen PO-reported issues across New request, Approve, New connect, the Accounts list, Move-in and Move-out — every one reported from a screenshot on 2026-10-11 and fixed the same day._

**Look in build 2.566.0**:
- **New request** → step 2: type an address with no match — City, State and ZIP can be typed, and *Check address* appears (*City map not connected.* without a City map). Step 3: *Payment details* — Pay now or Pay later; Pay now lists your utility's methods and asks each one's own details (Cash shows the change due). Step 4: *What the customer is told* has *Add a message*.

Type `101 Silver Creek Rd, Silver Creek, TX 78611` on a utility that already has it: *This address already exists.* names it by number with *Open it* and *Add it anyway*. Press *Check address*: without a City map it says *City map not connected.*; with one, a match offers *Use these details*. Open *Owner*, search a master account and press *Link this account*.

## [2.562.0] — 2026-10-08

_Settings → Security now does what it says: an expired password sends the person to change it, the last five passwords really are blocked, and a page that refreshes itself no longer keeps someone signed in._

### Fixed
- `DEF-IDN-10022`: *Password expires after* was saved and never read, so no password ever expired. A successful sign-in with a password older than the setting (90-day policy: day 91, not day 89) now lands on the existing forced change. *Never* still expires nobody; temporary passwords are unchanged; a *Keep me signed in* session is not renewed past the expiry.
- `DEF-IDN-10023`: *"The last 5 passwords are blocked"* was false — nothing stored them. A new password matching the current one or any of the five before it is now refused, on the ordinary and the forced change; the sixth-oldest is allowed. Hashes only, in a new `password_history` table with row-level security (`identity/0010`), five per person.
- `DEF-IDN-10024`: every request slid the idle clock, so a polling page (the bill run every 30 seconds) was never signed out. Requests sent while nobody has touched the page for a minute now carry `X-Background-Refresh: 1`; the server checks them fully and does not count them as activity.

## [2.561.5] — 2026-10-07

_US Payments now calls three addresses with no utility and no vendor in them — `/api/partner/v1/account-lookup`, `/add-payment`, `/add-return` — and the key in its `password` header says which utility it is._

**Look in build 2.561.5**: Settings → Connectors → USPayments. The API table reads `/api/partner/v1/add-payment`, `/api/partner/v1/account-lookup` and `/api/partner/v1/add-return` under Payments, Account lookup and Returns. Those are the three addresses to hand to US Payments, after `https://` and our API host, with the key from *Generate a key*.

### Fixed
- `DEF-INT-10020`: US Payments (built in 2.560.0) was served only at `/api/{utility}/integrations/inbound/pay_uspayments/…`. US Payments sends neither a utility nor our connector's name in any URL, so it could not reach us. Its three calls are now at `GET /api/partner/v1/account-lookup`, `POST /api/partner/v1/add-payment` and `POST /api/partner/v1/add-return`, each also with a trailing `/`. The utility is found from the key in the `password` header, sent exactly as issued with no `Bearer`, before anything else runs. `username` is a label and is not checked. Every check is unchanged: the key must be live, the enterprise and company IDs must match when sent, and the allowed addresses, rate limits and tender mapping all apply. A repeated `paymentId` still answers `409`. A wrong, unknown or revoked key gets the usual single refusal, after the same wait as every other partner address. The old per-utility address now refuses US Payments' three calls and logs where they moved. The generic kiosk connector is unchanged. Every other partner address still reads `Authorization: Bearer` exactly as before, and `/api/partner/v1/payments` and `make-payment` are unchanged.
- The API table on every partner connector now shows the address a partner actually dials, with `/api` in front. It used to show `/partner/v1/bills`, which answers nothing.
- New: `manage.py check_key_directory` lists every live issued key that has no utility-lookup row and changes nothing; `--fix` writes the missing rows through the same function that issuing a key uses.

### Rollback
- Redeploy 2.561.4. No migration and no setting. US Payments would then again be unable to reach us. Nothing it posted in the meantime is affected.

## [2.561.4] — 2026-10-07

_Every request we send to a city's map service now names us — `SMARTBillHub-GIS/2.561.4 (support@bynry.io)` — and a city firewall that blocks us is said as that, not as a bad key._

**Look in build 2.561.4**: with the City GIS connected, Add a property → type an address. A city whose firewall refuses us shows the amber box *The city's firewall blocked us.* (it read *The city rejected our key.*). Parcel check → Preview says the same. Settings → Connectors → the City GIS → the run's detail shows the city's own answer, e.g. *403, error code: 1010*.

### Fixed
- `DEF-INT-10019`: our server asked the city's map service, the Census geocoder and the premises geocoder with Python's default identity (`Python-urllib/3.x`), and Ann Arbor's Cloudflare refuses that with `403 error code: 1010`. One function (`core/gis_http.py`) now sends every such request with `User-Agent: SMARTBillHub-GIS/<product version> (support@bynry.io)` — our own name, never a browser's. A 403 whose body is not ArcGIS's own answer now reads *The city's firewall blocked us.* in all eleven languages; a 401, 498 or 499 is still the key, a 400, 404 or 410 still the moved layer, and a 403 in ArcGIS's own words still the key. The run row keeps the status and the first 200 characters of the answer (*403, error code: 1010*). A refusal still never counts towards the breaker.

### Rollback
- Redeploy 2.561.3. No migration, no setting. Runs recorded meanwhile keep their provider error text.

## [2.560.1] — 2026-10-07

_The City parcel check can now be run by hand two ways and finishes: the Preview reads the first few pages of the City's register and says how many it read, and the GIS reconciliation runbook now actually asks the City instead of stopping with "Nothing has landed yet."_

**Look in build 2.560.1**: Settings → Integrations → Esri ArcGIS → *Nightly parcel check* → **Preview** — when the City has more than three pages the result reads *"Stopped after 3 of 70 pages."* Then Runbooks → Templates → add *GIS reconciliation* → **Run ▶** (dry): the result says *"The city sent N rows over M pages."* and lists every difference, each one *Never touched* for an address field.

### Fixed
- `DEF-INT-9848`: with a working Esri ArcGIS connection, the GIS reconciliation runbook stopped at its first step every time with *"Nothing has landed yet."* — it never asked the City. It now runs the same parcel check the Integrations screen's *Preview* runs (no second copy of it), lists matches, differences and our properties no City parcel matched, and changes nothing. A City that refuses us stops the runbook with the reason (*rejected our key*, *map layer has moved*, *service had an error*, *this sync is switched off*), never an error page.
- `DEF-INT-9849`: the parcel check's *Preview* read the City's whole register inside a 60-second web request — about seven minutes at Ann Arbor's size — so it was cut off and showed nothing. It now reads 3 pages unless asked for a number (`?pages=N`), and says *"Stopped after 3 of 70 pages."* whenever it did not read everything. *Apply* still reads the whole register and refuses a page limit.
- `DEF-INT-9850`: pressing *Apply* on the parcel check at a utility that had added the GIS reconciliation runbook answered an internal error. It now completes and starts the runbook.

### Added
- The GIS reconciliation runbook has one new input, *City pages to read* (empty = the whole register). A utility whose copy of the runbook already has a saved version is offered *Template updated · Review →* once, and its runs wait for that press.

### Not changed
- No nightly or scheduled parcel run exists; what one should do is still the Product Owner's open choice. No address field is ever written by either path (R28).

### Rollback
- Redeploy 2.560.0. No migration. The runbook's new input disappears with it; a copy that accepted the template update shows *Template updated · Review →* again until reviewed.
## [2.560.0] — 2026-10-07

_A utility can now take payments through US Payments (Prime) — their kiosks, call centre, web page and phone line. A payment is posted the moment it arrives, so the next balance a customer sees is already right; a bounced payment is reversed the same way._

**Look in build 2.560.0**: Settings → Connectors → **USPayments** (now live). *Map their words →* opens the method list — map **OTHER** first, then *Connect* and *Generate a key*. Hand US Payments that key and the three addresses below. Then Payments → a US Payments payment shows **Source: Payment agent · Kiosk · 4471**, and a returned one shows **Bank code R01**.

### Added
- `CR-174-BRC10` (PO D1–D4, 2026-10-07): the USPayments card is the connector for the three calls US Payments makes to us — **account lookup** (`GET …/inbound/pay_uspayments/account_lookup?accountId=`, always 200, `{"accountValid": false}` for an account we cannot show), **payment** (`POST …/payments`: 200 posted · 409 duplicate · 400 bad body · 500 nothing kept, resend) and **return** (`POST …/returns`: also 503 when the payment has not arrived yet). The key travels in the `password` header; `enterpriseId` / `companyId`, when sent, must match the utility.
- The lookup answers the same live balance the customer portal shows (one read, now `payments/account_balance.py`), negative when the account is in credit, with the overdue part, the cash-only restriction and whether the account is residential.
- A payment meets the oldest bills first and any overpayment is held as credit. Its origin is the new **Payment agent**, so it never enters the New World receipts file.
- A return reverses through the existing reversal (the original stays, the bills are due again from their own due dates) and stores the bank's code beside the reason.
- The connector cannot be switched on until **OTHER** is mapped; on switching on, the obvious words (cash, check, ACH, card, wallets) are mapped to the utility's own methods where it has them. Nothing is created.
- *Map their words →* on the connector's page and its set-up page.

### Changed
- `payments/0049`: three new nullable columns on payments (`return_code`, `channel`, `terminal`) and a fourth origin, `agent`. 🔒 human review pending.

### Rollback
- Redeploy 2.559.1, then reverse `payments/0049`. The reverse refuses while any payment carries the `agent` origin — on purpose: posted money is never deleted to make a rollback fit. With US Payments payments already posted, roll forward instead.

## [2.559.0] — 2026-10-07

_A utility on New World / Logos can now have each day's online receipts placed in the City's SFTP folder as one file — set up on its own screen, tested with one button, run by hand first and then on a schedule it chooses._

**Look in build 2.559.0**: Settings → Integrations → New World / Logos → *Set up*. Under *Connection details* there is now a **Send to City folder** section: Server, Port, User name, Password, Folder, Server key, with **Save ✓** and **Test connection**. Then Runbooks → add *New World receipt push* → **Run ▶**.

### Added
- `CR-173-BRC10`: the **Send to City folder** section on the New World connection (PO approved 2026-10-07). The password is typed once, stored encrypted, and shown afterwards only as `••••` and its last four. **Test connection** signs in and writes a clearly named test file (`SMART360-connection-test-….txt`), then deletes it if the folder allows; the first successful test stores and shows the server's key, and every later connection checks it.
- `CR-173-BRC10`: runbook **New World receipt push** — build → upload → record for one day (yesterday on the utility's clock unless a day is typed), as ONE `Receipt_YYYYMMDD.xml` with one `<Receipts>` block. A dry run builds and counts and sends nothing. A day already sent is refused; a person may resend a day, with a reason, from the Send to City folder section. An empty day sends an empty file and alerts the System Admins; any failure alerts them too.
- `CR-173-BRC10`: **Run ▶** on every runbook's page now runs it (dry, or for real where the runbook allows it) — it said *Not connected yet.* until today.
- Every attempt is a row in the New World connection's run history: file name, folder, receipt count, the not-balanced and no-GL-number counts, and the result.

### Not changed
- The City's two read addresses (`/partner/v1/receipts`, `/partner/v1/ledger`) are exactly as before, and the key the City uses to read them stays valid when the password is saved.
- No card number, type, expiry or CVV exists anywhere in the file. No Ledger/JV file is sent.
- No other runbook can run for real.

### DevOps
- Allow outbound TCP 22 from our servers to `sftp.a2gov.org`. Get the server's host-key fingerprint from the City and compare it with the one the screen shows after the first **Test connection**.
- New dependency: `paramiko` (`06-backend/pyproject.toml`) — rebuild the image.

### Rollback
- Redeploy 2.558.4. Migration `integrations/0015` must be reversed first (`migrate integrations 0014`); it refuses to reverse while a connection holds a saved City password beside its key — delete that password first. Nothing is sent by 2.558.4.
## [2.558.5] — 2026-10-07

_When the City's map service refuses us, a clerk now sees the amber box with the reason in words instead of an internal error; and a parcel number that another property already has is refused with that property's address._

**Look in build 2.558.5**: on *Add a property*, with the City's key wrong, type `1408 Pec` — the amber box reads *"The City's records are unreachable. The city rejected our key. Type the address to continue."* On *Edit premise*, type a Parcel number another property already holds and press Save — the field reads *"This parcel already belongs to 101 Silver Creek Rd, Silver Creek."*

### Fixed
- `DEF-INT-9846` / `DEF-INT-5620`: a City answering "wrong key" (401/403), "not found" (404) or "server error" (5xx) reached the clerk as our own 500; an ArcGIS answer of `200 OK` with an error inside it was shown as "not answering" and counted towards switching the connection off. All four now show the amber box with one of three reasons — *rejected our key*, *map layer has moved*, *service had an error* — and none of them counts towards switching the connection off. The same refusal on the parcel check (*Run now* on the City connection) stops the run with the same reason instead of an error page.
- `DEF-MET-9847`: a parcel number already on another property could produce an internal error (two people saving at once), was accepted silently when typed on *Add a property*, and was otherwise refused without saying which property. It is now always one sentence naming the other property's address. Imports and the City parcel check can still put two properties on one parcel, as before.

### Rollback
- Redeploy 2.558.4. No migration and no data written by this change.

## [2.558.4] — 2026-10-07

_The address search now asks the City's map service the question it actually understands — the one the PO checked by hand against Ann Arbor — so what a clerk types is what the City searches for._

**Look in build 2.558.4**: on *Add a property*, type `2670 Sequoia` with a City address service connected. The request the product sends is `…/FeatureServer/0/query?where=UPPER(Street) LIKE UPPER('%2670 Sequoia%')&outFields=*&outSR=4326&returnGeometry=true&f=json&resultRecordCount=9` (plus `token=` when the City issued a key), and the City answers with *2670 Sequoia Pkwy, Ann Arbor*.

### Fixed
- `DEF-INT-9843`: the search sent `q=`, `limit=` and `key=` — words an ArcGIS map service ignores — so the City never filtered by what was typed. It now sends `where=` on the street field the utility mapped (default `Street`), asks for nine rows, and sends the key as `token=`. The nightly parcel pull and the search now build their requests in one place.
- `DEF-INT-9844`: the search did not ask for latitude/longitude (`outSR=4326`), so a City whose map is stored in State Plane feet would have sent feet as if they were degrees. It now always asks, and if a City still answers in another grid the search is refused and the clerk reads *"The city sent unusable map coordinates."* No coordinate from that answer is shown or saved.
- `DEF-INT-9845`: the City's unit label (`Unit`) was read and then dropped. It now travels with each address, so a building and its units can be told apart.

### Not changed
- The list a clerk sees is still a flat list of up to eight addresses. Grouping it by building is now possible but is a screen change, not taken here.
- Nothing is written until a person picks an address, as before.

### Rollback
- Redeploy 2.558.3. No migration, no data written by this change.

## [2.558.2] — 2026-10-06

_The PO's base-charge chain, with no fallback (PO ruling 2026-10-06, restating 2026-09-30): the base is the code the rate schedule NAMES, at its price. If the schedule names no base code, the base is $0.00 and the bill carries a warning — for every account on it, residential and commercial alike. Nothing is ever taken from the charge-code list by customer class._

**Look in build 2.558.2**: give a water rate schedule no base code while W-ALL ($8.00, every class) and W-COM ($15.00, Commercial) exist. A residential account's bill now shows a water base of $0.00 (it was $8.00), and a commercial account's bill now completes at $0.00 (before, it was refused with *"2 base charge codes for water"*). Both carry *"No base charge for Water. Billed $0.00."* Name W-COM on the schedule and a commercial account pays $15.00, as before. Open the plan, or New Connect step 2's *This plan* block: the water row of *Base charges* reads *Not chosen · $0.00*, with *"Water: its rate schedule names no base code."* and a *Choose a base code* link to the schedule. The plan list's base total counts it as $0.00. The rate schedule's Rates tab and list show only the code the schedule names.

### Fixed
- `DEF-RAT-9832`: a schedule naming no base code still took a code from the charge-code list by customer class. That billed W-ALL's $8.00 to residential accounts and refused commercial accounts. Now the base is $0.00 with the warning, on the bill, the first bill, the one-time bill, the R1–R7 chain, the rate-change impact, the plan screens and the plan list.
- `DEF-RAT-9829`: commercial accounts on such a schedule were refused. They now bill $0.00 with the warning. (Closed by the fix above.)

### Deploy note — read before deploying
**A live utility whose rate schedules name no base code will bill a $0.00 base on those schedules from this version** until a System Admin names a code on each schedule. Those schedules are already listed under *Rate schedules* as *"Base code needed on N schedules"* / *Choose a base code*. Measured on PostgreSQL 16 against the seeded demo utility (Brazos Bend): **8 of its 8 live schedules name no base code.** Of the 71 accounts on a plan, 50 lose a priced base — residential water $8.00 → $0.00 (40 accounts) and $10.00 → $0.00 (6), residential electric $12.00 → $0.00 (40) and $18.00 → $0.00 (6), commercial water $45.00 and $63.75, industrial water $195.00, municipal water $68.00, commercial electric $96.00 and $120.00, industrial electric $1,710.00, municipal electric $42.00, all → $0.00. That is **about $3,307.75 a month of base charges**. The other 21, refused before because no meter size was recorded, now bill $0.00 with the warning. The sample-utility seeders create schedules like these for every new sample world. That is filed as `DEF-RAT-9842`; it needs per-class schedules or plans in the sample data, because one schedule can name only one base code.

### Left open
- `DEF-RAT-9842`: the sample-utility seeders (above).
- `DEF-RAT-9841`: the one-off `migrate_base_to_charge_codes` command still measures the retired pool; three of its tests are marked expected-to-fail naming it.

### Rollback
- Redeploy the previous version. No migration and no stored row changed, so a rollback restores the earlier base-charge behaviour at once. Bills drafted on this version keep the $0.00 base they were drafted with.

## [2.549.14] — 2026-10-06

_Maintenance: one utility's plan screens no longer list other utilities' charge codes, and a production server refuses to start when tenant isolation is not in force._

**Look in build 2.549.14** — open Plans & Rates › a plan with a Solar service › Edit. *Name and details*, *Change from a date* step 1 and step 4 show this utility's ONE solar base code (e.g. `BASE-SOL`), never "Several base codes" listing BASE-SOL many times; the Charges step's dropdown lists each of this utility's codes once.

### Fixed
- `DEF-RAT-9791` (code half) — the plan read and the plan form's options read the charges, taxes and discounts tables without naming the utility, and relied on the database's row security alone; where that was not in force, every utility's codes appeared. Every read in the plan, plan-selector and discount read modules now names the utility itself. The production cause (which of the two ways row security was not in force) is the investigator's and the row stays open for it.
- `DEF-TEN-9794` — under `config.settings.production` a server now **refuses to start** when its database role bypasses row security, even with `SBH_ALLOW_RLS_BYPASSING_ROLE=1` (it says the setting was ignored), and when any tenant table lacks ENABLE or FORCE row security or its tenant policy (it names each table). A healthy boot prints two lines: `rls-guard: RLS is enforced on this connection: role '<role>' …` and `rls-guard: 284 tenant table(s) carry ENABLE + FORCE row-level security and a tenant policy (3 exempt by name: integration_key_directory, sessions, tenants).` Outside production an unprotected table is one `⚠` warning line.

### Added
- Gate `G143` — a read module (`*_reads.py`, `*_read.py`, `selectors.py`) may not query a tenant table without naming the tenant; it prints what it skipped.

### Rollback
- Redeploy `2.549.13`. No migration. ⚠ If a production deploy of this build refuses to start, the message names the role or the tables; fix the database (`ALTER ROLE … NOBYPASSRLS`, or `ALTER TABLE … ENABLE/FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` and re-apply its policy) rather than rolling back — rolling back restores the leak.

## [2.531.0] — 2026-10-05

_Move-in redesign (CR-171-BRC10) P1.17–P1.25, lane MVI-FLOW: step 1's unit and meter reads, the Messaging table and *What happened* at Complete, and the doors a clerk presses on a move-in that is not finished — Cancel, Change move-in date, Enter opening read, Add a work order._

**Look in build 2.531.0** — nothing on screen changes yet (the details view is P2). New routes for the screens to call, all keyed by the `MVI-` number:

### Added
- `GET /moves/{ref}/cancel-preview` and `POST /moves/{ref}/cancel` 🔒 — a not-started move-in's job is cancelled; a committed one (refused once a bill has issued) closes its account the day before the move-in date, ends its services that day, turns any credit into a refund request for Finance, calls off its open work orders, keeps its readings, and the unit reads Vacant. A move-in holding a deposit waits on a PO question (`OQ-CUS-12790`) and the preview says so.
- `POST /moves/{ref}/move-in-date` — moves the account's start and its services' start; refused once billed or onto the previous occupant's last day. Open visits are listed for the clerk to move.
- `POST /moves/{ref}/opening-reads` — readings after Complete, through metering's event door, dated the move-in date.
- `POST /moves/{ref}/work-orders` — add a visit to a move-in; refused when nothing is raised.
- `GET /units/{id}/move-in-facts` — the unit card on step 1: building (type, city limits, area, parcel, routes and cycles), unit, owner and history (first occupant or the previous one, plan changes).
- `GET /units/{id}/move-in-meters` and `POST …/check` — *Services and meters*: each service the unit offers with its meters, sub-meters and devices nested, how each reads and its last reading with its unit; *Below the last read* answered per row before Complete.
- Complete takes `extra_messages` (the Messaging table's added rows): an on-complete message to the customer is queued; the rest are kept as planned and say why. Complete now answers *What happened* and the request's `SR-` number.
- Twenty refusal sentences, each in all eleven languages.

### Fixed
- `DEF-CUS-9702` — a finished move-in no longer says *"The table that holds an account's plan does not exist"*, and *"No deposit was carried forward"* no longer gives a false reason.

### Rollback
- Redeploy 2.530.0. Cancels, date changes and readings already made stay: each is an ordinary account close, a date, a metering read or a refund request, and refunds are never reversed by a rollback (hard rule 4).

## [2.500.0] — 2026-10-04

_Work back office (CR-168-BRC10), round 3, lane SRV-2: what the redrawn raise and the assign dialogs read and write._

**Look in build 2.500.0** — open a job that needs *Meter I* and choose *Assign*: every technician, crew and contractor is listed with the skill, the area, the jobs that day and any lapsed certificate beside the name, and the one best fit marked; give it to somebody without the skill and it saves (the order's history marks that line). Move a job from D. Ortiz to R. Patel and you are asked why. Raise a job on six units of 301 Mill Pond Ln in one press: six jobs, one answer per unit.

### Added
- **Assign advice, never a block** (ruling 2; `BR-WRK-029` and `BR-WRK-030` superseded): `GET /work-orders/{id}/candidates` and `GET /work/candidates` (before the job exists) serve every technician, crew and contractor, paged and with no maximum, each with `advice {skill, has_skill, area_match, off_that_day, jobs_that_day, certifications_lapsed}` and one `best_fit`. An assignment against the advice is recorded (`work.order.assigned_against_advice`). Fixes `DEF-WRK-9531` (the 201st holder was never offered) and `DEF-WRK-9533` (a skill mismatch was refused).
- **Reassign with a reason** (P4.4): `act: reassign` on `POST …/assignments` and `reason` on `PATCH …/edit` — two history rows sharing the reason, one line on the order's history; a move off somebody without a reason is refused.
- **Raise in bulk** (ruling 19): `POST /work-orders/bulk-raise` — one job per ticked unit, or per ticked asset when an asset type is chosen (ruling 20); an answer per job; a repeated press returns the first answer.
- **Assign at the raise** (ruling 25): `POST /work-orders` and the bulk raise take `assignee`, a visit window and a due day.
- **The raise's reads**: `GET /work/raise/assets` (the assets on the ticked units, searchable by asset no, serial and where, with the last reading), `f.job_type` / `f.asset_type` / `f.scope` / `f.raisable` on `GET /work/templates`, and an asset's templates filtered by its service.
- **Send back** (P4.14): `POST /work-orders/{id}/send-back` returns a finished job to the field with a reason, only before it is accepted.

### Fixed
- `DEF-WRK-9527` — a unit of another building is refused on a premises job.
- `DEF-WRK-9528` — a template's scope and service reach the job; a water template on an electric job or meter is refused.

## [2.491.0] — 2026-10-04

_Discounts (CR-166-BRC10 follow-up): yearly caps and budgets count down from real bills; a bill is never held for a discount._

**Look in build 2.491.0** — open a discount on Plans & Rates › Discounts: *Granted this month* and each account's *This month* show what issued bills recorded (`$25.00`, or `$0.00`), not a dash. A customer with a $35.00 credit under a $300.00 yearly cap gets $35.00 a month to August, $20.00 in September, $0.00 to December and $35.00 again in January.

### Fixed
- **DEF-2430 / DEF-BIL-5341** · Every issued discount line now records what it granted, so a yearly cap, a lifetime cap and a programme budget count down. A yearly cap counts the calendar year of the bill's period end (PO 2026-10-04). Correcting a bill gives its discount back before the replacement is priced; replaying an issue or a correction counts nothing twice.
- **DEF-RAT-9366** · A yearly cap or budget no longer counts the next year's (or month's) grants against an earlier period's re-priced bill.
- **DEF-BIL-9501** · A bill with a discount on it can be corrected again: its credit note balances (it was refused, e.g. "debits 88.00 ≠ credits 72.00" on an $80.00 bill with $8.00 off).

### Changed
- **A bill is never held for a discount** (PO 2026-10-04, *"we cannot stop the billing"*; `BR-RAT-075` "suspend" superseded). When a programme's budget is used up the discount gives $0.00 (or what is left, on the bill that crosses it) and the bill goes out as normal — for every setting. Until now a used-up budget on *Suspend the discount* held every enrolled customer's bill.

### Rollback
- Redeploy 2.490.6, then roll back the two migrations (`rating 0064`, `billing 0039`). ⚠ Rolling back after a bill has been corrected fails on the restored constraint, on purpose: roll the code back and leave the migrations applied instead. Grants already written stay in `discount_grants` and are simply not read by 2.490.6.

## [2.484.0] — 2026-10-03

_Plans redesign (CR-167-BRC10) round 2 task 3: the plan server — dated plan versions, the §7.3 contract, deposits on a plan._

**Look in build 2.484.0** — Plans & Rates › Plans › **+ New plan**: the dropdowns are filled (`GET /plans/form-options`), *Save as draft* and *Publish plan* save in one call, and a new plan carries the late fee only when its row is on the Charges step. On the server: `GET /plans/{id}?as_of=` answers the plan as of a date; `GET /plans/{id}/units` searches, filters by occupancy and downloads CSV; `GET /plans/{id}/audit` reads in words.

### Added
- **Plan versions have dates (`BR-RAT-1066`, `OQ-324` closed as B).** A version owns its services, schedules, charge codes, taxes, discounts, deposits and terms; billing reads the version in force on the service date and splits a period at a version start. `POST /plans/{id}/versions` (*Change from a date*; *Save new version* / *Publish new version*) ends the version in force the day before. Worked: v1 from 09/01/2026, v2 from 01/01/2027 → 12/31/2026 prices by v1, 01/01/2027 by v2. Migrations `rating/0062`–`0064`; database lock `ex_plan_versions_no_overlap`.
- **Name and details on the same version (`BR-RAT-1067`).** Renaming a live plan keeps its version; a price change on `PATCH` is refused by name.
- **Deposits named on a plan** (ruling 9): refundable charge codes, by customer class. By meter size is `OQ-RAT-12786` (open).
- `GET /plans/form-options`, `GET /plans/{id}/audit`, list columns *Version · Schedules · Units · From · To*, the shared `ref` (version and from-date) on every referenced item; 20 refusal sentences in all eleven languages.

### Fixed
- **DEF-RAT-9337** · A base charge code is refused as a plan charge code; stored ones removed by `rating/0063`.
- **DEF-RAT-9330** · Publishing a plan that is already published answers *already published* instead of failing.
- **DEF-RAT-9328** (server half) · The plan's charge codes are one list with the late fee in it once; a body's `charge_codes: []` charges no late fee and is never filled with `LATE`.

### Not moved
- Golden suite 25 passed + 1 xfailed before and after; every account of the seeded utility priced before and after on PostgreSQL: 124 account-periods, $39,721.23, 0 differences.

### Rollback
- Redeploy 2.482.1 after `manage.py migrate rating 0061_cr166_discount_lock_and_rls`. `0064` down drops the lock and makes `plan_version_id` nullable; `0063` down is a no-op (base codes it removed from plans are not restored — they billed nothing); `0062` down drops the version columns, which FAILS while a plan holds two versions' rows for one service — retire the extra version first. Versions written by *Change from a date* lose their dates on the way down.

Measured on the New Connection walk's database: master `AC-2026-00066` (and `-00063`, `-00064`, `-00065`), whose only issued bill is the quote dated 2026-10-03, was asked *"billed through 2026-10-03 … 28 day(s) 2026-10-04 to 2026-10-31 no issued bill covers"* on its November run, and an October run would have started its bill on 10-04. Now the quote is not a billed-through date: the account's first cycle bill is a first bill, no question is asked, and the bill opens on the period's first day. The same holds for any fee bill (a $75.00 reconnection fee after a cycle bill no longer moves where the next bill starts) — the rule the move-out cut already used (`DEF-CUS-6086`). One rule on every read the run makes: the continuity question, the bill's opening day, the register anchor, and the bulk Check's batched read. 🔒 HUMAN-REVIEW-PENDING (review-ledger row). Tests: `test_def_bil_9254_a_fee_bill_is_not_billed_through.py` (3, PostgreSQL; red before — a quote-only account read `(2026-06-03, 2026-06-03)` as its last window and its bill opened on 06-04); continuity, Check, batch-read and cut suites 101 passed.

_New Connection's five steps, as the Product Owner reviewed them on 2 October (`CR-164-BRC10`)._

**Look in build 2.463.0** — front end and server. Defects `DEF-CUS-9192`–`9200` and `DEF-CUS-9212`.

### Changed
- **Step 1 · Customer.** The *Customer ID* search box is gone. Step 1 looks the owner up by itself
  from what was typed: the same SSN, driving licence or (for a company) Tax ID is a **match**; the
  same name and date of birth is a **possible match**. The clerk sees the customer's number, name and
  the last four of what matched, and picks *Use this customer* or *Not this person*; otherwise it says
  *Customer not found. A new customer will be created.* Owner type is the utility's own owner list
  (Settings), not four built-in words. A date of birth in the future, or an owner under 18, is refused.
  The SSN and licence are masked. Co-applicant and Mailing address are cards that open when needed.
  The language picked on step 1, and the paperless and SMS ticks, now reach the master account.

  customer class; *Budget billing* is no longer on this step. A State that is not a two-letter code, or
  is not the utility's own state, and a ZIP that is not five digits or ZIP+4 each say so under the box
  (nothing is blocked). *Unit, apt.* is hidden for an apartment complex.

  server. *+ Add work order* is one *Applies to* and one work-order list; an added job is edited on its
  own row. *Press Apply to all first* shows only while the rows are empty.
- **Step 4 · Charges.** *What is charged* comes first. Payment terms are a list: 7, 15, 30, 60 or 90 days.
- **Step 5 · Review.** *Work orders* shows the number Create will raise (it was a dash). Meters and
  behind-the-meter devices are counted apart. Messages go *On approval*; a message with no template says
  *No template — add in Settings*; a removed message comes back with *+ Add message*. *What Create
  makes* shows each item's status — premises, master account and customer *Pending → Active on
  approval*, meters *Inventory → Installed*, the request *Requested → Partly activated → Activated* — and
  *Premises* counts 1 when Create makes it. *Master account* replaces *the owner's account* everywhere.

  master account, so step 4 no longer offers one as the payer and says *No master account to bill.
  Remove the charges.* on step 4 (`DEF-CUS-9212`). Who should pay a single-family build's connection
  charges is with the coordinator.

Redeploy 2.462.2. No migration; nothing written by this build needs undoing.

## [2.460.1] — 2026-10-02

_An export that cannot be stored now fails within minutes and says why, and a worker that cannot store exports says so the moment it starts._

**Look in build 2.460.1** — `DEF-TEN-9190`, reported from the first real deployment: a Premises export
built 73 rows and then sat in "running" with nothing in any log.

### Fixed
- **No more silent "running" export.** Uploads to S3 now give up after about 20 s if nothing answers the
  connection and after about 4 minutes if the connection goes silent (it was 5 minutes and more, on
  boto3's defaults), and the export then fails with a plain reason — e.g. *"File storage did not
  answer."*, *"File storage refused the upload."*, *"The storage bucket does not exist."*
- **"Ready" means the file is in the bucket.** The worker reads the file back from S3 before marking
  the export stored; an upload that "returned" with nothing behind it fails as *"File missing from
  storage after upload."*
- **A stuck export is failed, with a reason.** Every 10 minutes celery-beat fails any export job (never a
  bill run) with no progress for 30 minutes: *"The export stopped responding."* — the case of a worker
  killed mid-export, e.g. for running out of memory.
- **The celery log tells the story of each export**: *built premises, 73 row(s)* → *uploading 4849 byte(s)
  to s3://… at t/<utility>/export/…* → *stored*, or one ERROR line naming the stage, the key and the
  bucket. The web log now records a download refused because the job has no stored file, or because the
  file is no longer in the bucket.
- **A worker says where exports go when it starts** — *"celery worker (build 2.460.1): export storage:
  s3://<bucket> via AWS in <region> - reachable"*, or *UNREACHABLE* / *BUCKET NOT FOUND* — and a worker or
  web process with no bucket at all **refuses to start** (`smartbillhub.E003`). A worker that cannot
  reach S3 now starts in seconds rather than minutes.

### HOST STEPS
- **Every celery service needs the same storage settings as web**: `DOCUMENT_STORAGE_BUCKET`,
  `DOCUMENT_STORAGE_REGION`, and credentials (a task role, or the AWS key pair). The workers are what upload
  exports. ⚠ Editing `.env.example` changes nothing on a host that already has a `.env` — add them by hand.
- **Give the celery task at least 1 GB of memory** (and `celery-billing` 1 GB, 2 GB for print sets over
  ~10,000 bills). Measured: a worker with `--concurrency 2` is about 570 MB before any large job, and the
  first upload in each process adds about 21 MB. On ECS, check *Stopped tasks* for
  `OutOfMemoryError` / exit code 137.
- **IAM** for every app task role: `s3:PutObject`, `s3:GetObject`, `s3:AbortMultipartUpload` on `t/*`;
  `s3:DeleteObject` on `t/*/export/*` only — the full policy is in `09-infra/02-aws-runbook.md` §10.6.
- **Network**: worker subnets need a NAT gateway or an S3 gateway endpoint, exactly like web's.
- **Rebuild both images and restart web, celery, celery-billing and celery-beat**, then check each
  worker's first log lines for `export storage: … - reachable`. The full checklist is
  `09-infra/04-exports-to-s3.md` §10.1.

## [2.460.0] — 2026-10-02

_A New Connection is created Pending and switched on by approving it, one unit at a time._

**Look in build 2.460.0** — `CR-162-BRC10`, the New Connection lifecycle.

### Changed
- **Create makes things Pending.** The property a New Connection creates is **Pending**, and so is the
  owner's master account (it still takes the connection charges that day). Both become **Active** on
  the first approval. A Pending property and a Pending master account link to their request:
  *New connection CON-26-0135 · Requested · Open request*.
- **The premises type decides the master account.** Each premises type in Settings now has an
  **Account type** — *Master account* or *Regular account* — shown as a column and required when a
  type is added (*Choose the account type.*). Apartment complex, commercial building, mixed-use,
  mobile-home park and government building start as Master; single-family as Regular. An apartment
  complex with one unit entered now gets its owner a master account; a single-family home never does
  (*Single-family homes have no master account. Open a regular account at Move-in.*). Changing the
  answer affects only what is created afterwards.
- **The Build tab on a property and the Build panel on an account are gone** — the request's own page
  tracks progress and takes every action.
- *Release* now reads **Resume**; *Mark / Close outstanding* left the More menu.

### Added
- **Approve.** On the request's page, *Approve* (header) and the Units tab's *Activate*, *Activate
  selected* and *Activate all ready* open one dialog: what is ready, what a gate holds (*Unit 1: gate
  WO-0057 not passed.*), and every open order on the build (*2 of 4 not complete: WO-0043, WO-0044*),
  with *Activate what is ready*. Activating switches the service on, marks its meters and devices
  **Installed** with today's date, makes the unit Active when all its services are, and on the first
  activation makes the property and the master account Active; the request reads *Partly activated*
  or *Activated*. A gate inspection that has not passed blocks its unit; other open orders only warn;
  open to-dos are listed and never block.
- **Units tab** columns: Unit type, Asset type, Size, Qty, Asset ID (with its stage), Work order, State.
- **To-do tab**: to-dos and **notes** together, newest first, *+ Add a to-do*, *+ Add a note*, *Mark
  done*, *Reopen*, and *Edit note* for your own notes. The Overview says *To-dos open: 2*.
- **Add unit** (with its services) and **Add service** as proper forms in the More menu.
- **Move-in before approval** is allowed: the account opens and says *Billing starts once the unit
  activates.*; its first bill counts only the days from activation (opened 5 Oct, activated 8 Oct → 24
  of 31 October days). Cancelling the request lists the accounts still open on its units and closes none.

### Fixed
- **A property built by New Connection names its master account** (`DEF-MET-9201`). It read
  *Master a/c: Needs an owner* beside a live master account.

### Rollback
- Redeploy 2.459.1's code, then `manage.py migrate metering 0064` (drops `connection_todos.kind` and
  `premises_types.account_kind`; export any notes first — they would read as to-dos). Properties and
  master accounts left Pending by builds made on 2.460.0 stay Pending until activated by hand.
