### Fixed
- **Asking for a bill print set builds it exactly once** (`DEF-BIL-9152`). With a worker running, a request
  that did not ask for the background built the set twice — on the worker and inside the web request — and
  the web request answered with an error. Now a worker, when there is one, is always handed the set (the
  screen already waits for it); with no worker the request builds it itself and sends nothing to the queue.
- **A finance export with a date like `2026-13-01`, or an account ledger with no account, is refused straight
  away with the field named** (`DEF-TEN-9160`). Since 2.357.0 it was accepted and then failed in the
  background.
- **The schedule door checks the same role as the report viewer** (`DEF-REP-9161`): it now reads the role the
  server attached for this utility, as every other permission check does.

## [2.455.0] — 2026-10-02

_Every export file is kept in the environment's S3 bucket, so Download works when a worker made the file._

### Changed
- **Every export — list, report and finance exports, the audit-log export and the bill print set — is
  stored in S3 at `t/<web name>/export/<year>/<month>/<file id>.csv|zip`** (PO, 2026-10-02: *"You can take
  module name as export for all export related actions"*, *"Removed -> Yes we will just be using S3"*).
  Austin Water's September Premises export is `t/austin-water/export/2026/09/<file id>.csv`. Download hands
  over a link to the file that lasts 4 hours. **Fixes `DEF-MET-4954`:** with the job run on a worker, pressing
  Download used to save `file.json` containing a 404.
- **Old exports are deleted once a day, per utility, after that utility's own setting (3 days by default)**,
  and the clean-up can delete nothing outside that utility's `export/` folder (*"make sure that you don't
  delete any other data"*). It used to happen only when somebody ran the next export.
- **The bill print set is built in its own temporary folder and removed afterwards**, success or failure
  (`DEF-BIL-9148`).

### Removed
- The shared Docker `artifacts:` volume, `JOB_ARTIFACTS_DIR`, the Dockerfile's `/app/var/artifacts` and the
  AWS EFS plan. ⚠ **A host needs `DOCUMENT_STORAGE_BUCKET` and `DOCUMENT_STORAGE_REGION` set for exports**
  (the same bucket bills use), and its task role needs `s3:DeleteObject` on `t/*/export/*` and nothing
  wider (`09-infra/02-aws-runbook.md` §10.6). Editing `.env.example` changes nothing on a host that already
  has a `.env` (law 4); delete `JOB_ARTIFACTS_DIR` from it by hand.

### Rollback
Revert the change commits and redeploy, and put the `artifacts:` volume back on `backend`, `celery` and
`celery-billing`. Exports made while this version ran are in S3 only and will 404 after a rollback; they are
regenerable and expire in days anyway. The `job_artifacts` table (tenancy `0055`) can stay — nothing reads it
after a rollback; reverse it with `migrate tenancy 0054` only if it must go.

## [2.454.3] — 2026-10-02

_The AR ageing's totals show again on the Finance Aging download and in the report viewer._

### Fixed
- **The ageing's band totals and grand total are numbers again wherever the screen sends a date
  range** (`DEF-REP-9150`). The AR ageing is a position on ONE date, but the check that stops a
  balance being added up across time read the dates the screen ASKED with, not the date the report
  answered for. Finance → Aging, its download and the report viewer after any filter all send a
  from/to pair, so at Brazos Bend on 31 October every band and the `$340.20` total over 8 accounts
  came back as a dash and *"Balances do not sum across time"*. Now the check asks the report which
  date it describes: one date sums, a real range still refuses. The viewer's Total row reads
  `$0.00 · $37.25 · $228.45 · $74.50 · $0.00 · $340.20` again, and the Aging download no longer ends
  in a row of dashes (it ends on its last account, as every lawful download does). The account
  census's balance total is restored the same way. A report spanning a window over balances (the
  ledger's running balance) still shows the dash. No figure was computed differently. Rollback:
  revert the one commit.

## [2.454.2] — 2026-10-02

_A clerk can open a document filed on an account._

### Fixed
- **Each row on an account's Documents tab has an Open icon (the eye), before Remove**
  (`DEF-CUS-9147`). A clerk could file a lease on an account and then not read it back: the row had
  only a bin. Pressing the eye now opens the file in a new tab, through the same safe route a service
  request's documents already open through, so a PDF, PNG or JPG shows in the browser and a CSV is
  saved. A contract that cannot be removed can still be opened, and every role that can see the tab
  can open its files. Each open is written to the audit log. Files stored under the old August
  address open too. New route: `GET /accounts/{id}/documents/{docId}/content?as=view|download`.
  Rollback: revert the one commit; the tab goes back to the bin alone and nothing stored changes.

## [2.454.1] — 2026-10-02

_One utility's audit export or print set no longer deletes another utility's download files._

### Fixed
- **Each utility's old download files are cleared on that utility's own schedule** (`DEF-TEN-9146`). The
  audit-log export and the bill print set tidied up old download files for EVERY utility at the default 3
  days. So if Lone Star kept its files 7 days and had a 4-day-old export, Brazos Bend running an audit
  export deleted it. Now both jobs clear only the running utility's own files, at its own setting, the way
  the list export already did, and the clean-up can no longer be called without naming a utility. No data
  was exposed. This tidy-up is temporary: the approved move of exports to S3 replaces it. Rollback: revert
  the one commit. Nothing on any screen changes.

## [2.454.0] — 2026-10-02

_A utility's files are filed by its web name and by module, and no file is locked for now._

### Changed
- **Every new file goes in the utility's own folder, then the module's** (`CR-160-BRC10`; PO, 2026-10-02:
  *"Instead of Fucntion can you do it module"*, *"STart from t - dont add Sbh-prod"*, *"Yes, web name"*). A
  September bill PDF for Austin Water is stored at `t/austin-water/billing/2026/09/<file id>.pdf` in that
  environment's one bucket; a receipt goes under `payments/`, an account document under `customers/`, a
  work-order photo under `work/`. Every one of the 48 document kinds maps to exactly one of twelve fixed
  modules. **Files stored before today keep their old address and still open; nothing was moved.**
- **No file is object-locked and none carries an expiry tag, legal files included** (PO: *"we dont want
  this to be enabled right now - dont lock it"*). The product still deletes nothing; someone with direct
  access to the storage account could. The lock stays a setting (`DOCUMENT_STORAGE_OBJECT_LOCK_MODE`,
  now `NONE` by default) and, if switched on, covers files written after that moment only. ⚠ A host whose
  `.env` already says `COMPLIANCE` keeps locking until that `.env` is edited.
- **The app refuses to start against a bucket with a default retention rule** (`smartbillhub.E002`),
  because such a rule would lock every file, exports included, and in COMPLIANCE mode nobody could
  delete one. If it cannot ask the bucket it warns and starts.

### Rollback
Revert the change commit and redeploy: new files go back to `t/<tenant id>/<yyyy>/<mm>/<id>`. Files
written under the new address keep working after a rollback only if the rollback keeps the new key
pattern readable — so revert `document_storage._KEY_RE` LAST, or not at all. Nothing in the database
changes either way.

## [2.453.1] — 2026-10-02

_The base-charge clean-up tool tells the truth and never turns an old plan figure into a price._

### Fixed
- **The base migration creates no charge code from a retired plan figure** (`DEF-RAT-9139`; decision log
  2026-10-02 *"THE BASE MIGRATION CREATES NO CHARGE CODE FROM A RETIRED PLAN FIGURE"*, under the PO's
  2026-09-28 ruling *"we will never take default value from plan $8.0 - that is retired"*). It used to report
  that all six of Silver Creek's bills would be refused, which was false, and `--apply` would have created
  codes that put $8.00 on a home's water bill that charges $0.00 today. Now it asks billing what each bill
  charges. It clears the two sewer $0.00 figures that match, and lists the other four for a person as
  "would raise the bill from $0.00 to $8.00 if a code were created". No bill changes.
- **`--apply` runs as a real System Admin** (`DEF-RAT-9140`). It refused every real user because the role
  was never attached; the role check now sits on the clearing step itself, so it is no weaker.
- **The report no longer tells the operator to fix DEF-477 first** (`DEF-RAT-9141`); that was fixed on
  2026-08-21. The tool's tests now also run on PostgreSQL (`DEF-RAT-9145`: a helper read customer types
  without the tenant's context). Rollback: revert the one commit. Nothing on any screen changes.

## [2.453.0] — 2026-10-02

_Unit prices show the decimals they carry, and the Service filter takes several services at once._

### Changed
- **A unit price shows up to four decimals; every total stays at two** (PO, 2026-10-02: *"Show unit
  prices with up to 4 decimals and keep every total at 2."*). A water price of $0.0425 a gallon now reads
  `$0.0425` everywhere it is shown, `$12.5` reads `$12.50` and `$0.10` stays `$0.10`; zeros after the
  second decimal are dropped, so a price that read `$8.2900` now reads `$8.29`. Amounts — a line total, a
  bill total, a balance, a minimum, a base charge — are unchanged at two, so `$425.00` stays `$425.00`.
  Screens: rate schedule list, details, Rates tab and the Edit review; plan summary; unit pricing; the
  staff bill and the one-time bill; the move-out final bill; the Taxes list (per-unit taxes); the
  customer portal's bill; the printed bill. Display only — nothing stored or billed moved.
- **"+ Filter → Service" now picks several services at once** (PO, 2026-10-02: *"Allow several services
  at once."*). Ticking Water and Sewer shows both and no Trash, and the one chip reads
  `Service: Water, Sewer`. Every list whose filter offers Service does this, and the server applies it
  before cutting the page. Every other filter is still one choice.

### Fixed
- The move-out final bill showed a usage price at two decimals (`@ $0.11` for $0.1126) — `DEF-CUS-9142`.
- The Taxes list showed a per-unit tax at six stored decimals (`0.002500 per kWh`) — `DEF-RAT-9143`.
- The rate schedule list's capacity and demand previews printed six stored decimals
  (`10.000000 per panel`) — `DEF-RAT-9144`.

Rollback: revert `ce717df42`, `3c6ab3306`, `4047fe02b`, `565e6a831` and the release commit; no data or
migration is involved. (Those four subjects say 2.451.0, the number allocated before 2.452.x landed;
the change ships as 2.453.0.)

  owner's bill carries one line per empty home, naming it — *Unit 4 · water base charge, $8.00* — and
  only the base, never usage. A tenant moving in on the 16th of a 30-day month takes the base from
  that day: the owner pays $4.00 and the tenant $4.00. An empty single home bills nobody, because it
  has no master account. An owner whose building has no common area is now billed for its empty homes
  too; before, that owner was not in the bill run at all (PO ruling 2026-10-02, `BR-CUS-1116`,
  `DEF-CUS-9050`, `DEF-CUS-9082`).
- **New Connection offers two unit choices.** *Vacant · service off* and *Vacant · base charges only*;
  *Landlord-billed between tenants* is now the second, and *Open an account now* is removed (units start
  vacant; a tenant's account opens through Move-in). A saved build holding a removed choice opens on
  its replacement.
## [2.443.1] — 2026-10-02

_Rate schedules and charge codes: the lists fit a 1280 laptop, Edit opens on every schedule, and one word for a schedule in force._

### Fixed
- **The rate schedules and charge codes lists no longer scroll sideways on a 1280 screen** (`DEF-RAT-9112`). Below
  1440 wide, rate schedules start without the Sizes and Plans columns and charge codes without Priced by and GL
  account; each is one click away in the Columns picker. At 1440 nothing changes.
- **Editing a rate schedule priced from each customer class's own base code no longer stops at step 1** asking for a
  single code (`DEF-RAT-9111`).
- **A rate schedule in force now reads "In force" everywhere** — the details header said "Active" (`DEF-RAT-9117`).
- **Edit on a charge code's details is a plain button**, as on rate schedule details (`DEF-RAT-9116`).

## [2.443.0] — 2026-10-02

_A portal application the customer never sent is now deleted, with its files, 30 days after their last visit — the Product Owner's ruling of the same day._

### Changed
- **An unsent portal application and the documents attached to it are deleted 30 days after the customer last
  opened it** (`CR-158-BRC10` §5, PO ruling 2026-10-02). Opening the link, saving, or adding or removing a file
  restarts the 30 days, counted in the utility's own calendar days: an application last visited on 1 October goes on
  31 October; one reopened on 20 October goes on 19 November. Each deletion writes one audit-log line with the file
  count and the reason *"unsent 30 days"* — never a name, a contact detail or a file's contents. Sent applications,
  their documents and other utilities' applications are never touched. A nightly job does it at 03:40 UTC
  (`portal.draft_cleanup`); migration `portal/0012` adds the column that remembers the last visit.

## [2.442.1] — 2026-10-02

_Rate schedules and charge codes: page buttons back at the top right, wizard buttons in one row, and real dates where a dash or 01/01/2000 showed._

### Fixed
- **Rate schedules list: "New rate schedule" is back at the top right, beside History**, and opens the new rate
  schedule form (`DEF-RAT-9101`). It had moved under the table, off-screen on a long list.
- **Rate schedule details: Duplicate · Edit · Retire are back at the top right on every tab** (`DEF-RAT-9101`).
- **Rate schedules list: the row of service buttons is gone; Service is a choice inside "+ Filter"** and shows as a

- **Rate schedule Rates tab: From shows the date each base price applies on this schedule** — 08/01/2026 on the
  seeded schedules instead of "—" (`DEF-RAT-9102`).
- **Charge code add and edit: the buttons sit in one row across the page** — Cancel on the left; Save draft & exit,
  Back and Save change on the right — the same as every other form with steps (`DEF-RAT-9104`).
- **Charge code details no longer show 01/01/2000** as a start date (`DEF-RAT-9109`).
- **Rate schedules list: a code such as BASE-W and the "In force" label no longer break over two lines** (`DEF-RAT-9110`).
- **Charge code screens line up with the rest of Plans & Rates** (`DEF-RAT-9114`).

## [2.442.0] — 2026-10-02

_Two rulings by the Product Owner: a billing clerk can size a new connection, and a master account is only for a building with two or more homes._

### Changed
- **A billing clerk now sees the sizes and equipment on New Connection step 3.** The clerk can read
  the asset types, the size lists and the work templates that step needs, read only; adding or
  changing an entry, or a template, is still the System Admin's. Every other Settings list stays
  closed to the clerk (PO ruling 2026-10-02, `DEF-CUS-9048`).
- **A master account is raised only on a building with two or more homes.** On a single-family home
  or a single-unit address every master door now says *"Single unit. Open a regular account."* — the
  property's master form, the request page's *Owner's master account*, New Connection's owner step,
  and an address added with an owner. A common area does not count as a home. The applicant gets a
  regular account on the one unit instead, which holds the services and goes active. A building of
  two or more homes is unchanged. Existing master accounts are not changed: the demo utility has 4,
  none on a single home (PO ruling 2026-10-02, `BR-CUS-1114`, `BR-CUS-1115`, `DEF-CUS-9113`).

## [2.440.6] — 2026-10-02

_Test-only: the capacity-equipment sample bills checked against today's signed figures._

### Fixed
- Test-only. The demo estate's battery, broadband and reference-bill sewer figures were checked against
  rules that changed in September. The bills were right. A 10 kW battery is $30.00 of usage plus the
  $5.00 base added on 7 September, so $35.00. Broadband is $10, $50 or $100 of usage plus a $30.00 base.
  The reference bill's sewer is $36.00, the figure finance re-signed on 8 September (90% of 8 kgal at
  $5.00), plus the $9.00 sewer base the PO confirmed on 1 October. Each line is now checked on its own
  (`DEF-RAT-9092`).

## [2.440.5] — 2026-10-02

_Accounts: a pasted account id works again on the transfer wizard, and the account's Payments tab draws its own eight columns._

### Fixed
- **Pasting an account id into the transfer wizard finds the account again.** Since step 1 moved to

  nothing was looked up (`DEF-CUS-9106`).
- **An account's Payments tab no longer shows Source and Batch by default.** They were added to the

- Test-only. 35 customers screen tests brought up to the screens as ruled between 12 September and

  (`DEF-CUS-9107`). Four billing and rating wizards are recorded on the rail census with their
  defect row (`DEF-GOV-9108`). One unused binding fixed in `NewConnectWizard.test.tsx`.

## [2.440.4] — 2026-10-02

_New Connect: the Asset and Size boxes show the whole name._

### Fixed
- **New Connect step 3 now shows the whole name in the Asset and Size boxes.** A fire row read
  "Fire service li…" because the table squeezed the box narrower than its text. The box now keeps
  room for its longest name, so "Fire service line" reads in full on 1440- and 1280-pixel screens.
  On a narrower screen the table scrolls inside its own frame, so the page does not scroll sideways
  (`DEF-CUS-9093`).

## [2.440.3] — 2026-10-02

_Tests only: the worked-example cohorts price their base again._

### Fixed
- Test-only. The journey cohort plans stated their monthly base only where bills stopped reading it
  on 28 September, so since 30 September they billed it at $0.00 with a warning. WE-1's cohort bill
  read **$210.00** instead of **$221.90**. Each cohort plan now has its base on a charge code bound
  to its own rate schedule. That fixes the two T4-11 cases and three flat-cohort cases
  (`DEF-BIL-9100`). No product behaviour changed.

## [2.440.2] — 2026-10-02

_Sample data: the fire lines on a sample fire customer are checked against its bill._

### Fixed
- **The sample fire customers now prove their fire lines reach a bill.** A check on the sample
  utility had been failing since 7 September: it expected six fire lines on a sample utility that
  does not sell fire, so the sample data rightly planted none. The check now uses a sample utility
  that sells water, sewer and fire. There the six lines are planted with their sizes, and the unit
  with one 6" and two 2" lines bills one fire line of $84.00 ($60.00 + 2 × $12.00). A 4" line bills
  $30.00, and the unit with no line bills $0.00 (`DEF-AST-9083`).

## [2.440.1] — 2026-10-02

_Requests: the history names the customer when the customer acted._

### Fixed
- **A request's history now shows the customer, not "System", for what the customer did.**
  A file sent from the Track page or a note the customer wrote reads, for example,
  *Ama Boateng (portal)*, or *Customer (portal)* when the request holds no name. Rows the
  product writes on its own still say *System*.

## [2.440.0] — 2026-10-02

_New Connect: a fire service gets fire lines with a size; solar and battery no longer get a meter._

### Added
- **A fire service now takes "fire lines" on New Connect, each with a size, the way trash takes
  carts** (PO ruling 2026-10-02). The fire row offers the utility's fire line and fire's own sizes
  (2" to 12" as seeded; each utility can edit the list). Pressing *+ Add row* and choosing Fire again
  adds one more line, so one 6" line and two 2" lines is three rows. The build creates three numbered
  fire lines, not yet installed, and once they are fitted the first bill shows **one fire line of
  $84.00** ($60.00 + 2 × $12.00). The same *+ Add row* works for a second trash cart or a third
  solar panel.

### Fixed
- **A solar or battery new connection no longer fits a net meter** (PO: *"Capacity is the panels or
  battery only"*). Three 4 kW panels bill on 12 kW. Any meter already standing on a solar, battery or
  other capacity connection is no longer counted toward its size, so it can neither change nor stop
  the bill (`DEF-MET-9037`).

## [2.439.11] — 2026-10-02

_Tests only: three checks that had been red on the branch are brought up to their rules._

### Fixed
- Test-only. The bank reconciliation statement tests now give each refund its account, required
  since 3 September (`DEF-PAY-9090`). The deposit-batch screen tests now find a day's batches by
  tender, because a new batch has taken a numbered code from Settings since 22 September; the
  frozen $471.39 and $121.78 are unchanged (`DEF-PAY-9085`). The account-history docstrings now
  state the retention rule without quoting the phrase the retention check refuses, so the check
  can pass for the first time (`DEF-CUS-9084`). No product behaviour changed.

## [2.439.10] — 2026-10-02

_Rate schedules: a service with its own meters can no longer be priced as a share of another._

### Fixed
- **A rate schedule can no longer price a metered service as a percentage of another service.**
  Water set at 38% of electric, on an account with two water meters, charged the 38% once per
  meter: $1,691.64 instead of $860.82. Saving such a schedule is now refused with *This service
  has meters. Price it from its readings.*, and the Structure list greys the option for that
  service. It follows each utility's own "read from a meter" setting, so sewer, which has no
  meter, can still be priced as a share of water; a utility that meters its sewer cannot.
  Schedules already saved are not changed. The real case still bills correctly: a duplex with two
  water meters reading 6 and 4 kgal, sewer at 90% of water usage at $5.00/kgal, bills $45.00 on
  one sewer line (`DEF-BIL-9014`).

## [2.439.9] — 2026-10-02

_Account history: a change made in the app now says which clerk made it._

### Fixed
- **The history of an account's type, sub-type and status now names the clerk who changed it.** A
  change made through the app recorded nobody, because the history only accepted one of the two
  shapes the app hands a service for "who is acting". It now reads the person through the one shared
  helper every other audit write uses. The same gap was closed where it was latent: five writes in
  bank reconciliation (match sets, statement imports, batch events) and the "invited by" on a new
  staff user (`DEF-CUS-9081`).

## [2.439.8] — 2026-10-02

_Customer portal: an applicant asked for more can send it from Track, and paperless is never pre-ticked._

### Fixed
- **When the utility asks for more information, the applicant can now send the document from
  the Track page.** Track shows *Add a document* while a request is waiting on the applicant,
  with the same file rules as the application (PDF, JPG or PNG, up to 10 MB, five files per
  application in all). The file lands on the request; the clerk sees it under Documents and a
  *Customer replied* line in the request's history. Any other request refuses a file.
- **The paperless box on the application now starts unticked**, so paperless billing is only
  chosen by the applicant.

### Checked
- The 21 portal walks were run again: all 12 applications reached an active account, W14 now
  sends its second document, and every application showed the paperless box unticked.

## [2.439.7] — 2026-10-02

_Sample data: two account flags the demo promised are stored again._

### Fixed
- **A new sample utility carries its delivery election and its tax exemption again.** The sample
  data acted through a stand-in for the seed user, and the account history (which records who
  changed an account) refused it, so both were silently skipped. On a fresh sample utility
  A-10650 now has paperless bills and text reminders in es-MX, and A-10714 is tax exempt
  (TX-EX-4471, until 30 Jun 2027) (`DEF-CUS-9080`).

## [2.439.6] — 2026-10-02

_One-time bill: a meter rollover can now be accepted where the bill is held._

### Fixed
- **The one-time bill now lets the clerk accept a meter rollover on the spot.** When a meter rolled
  over partway through the period, the bill was held with no way to clear it on that screen. A panel
  now shows the meter, its readings before and after the rollover and at the period's end
  (99,800 → 240 → 700), and the usage they add up to (900 kWh), with one *Accept rollover* button.
  Once accepted, the bill is priced across the rollover — $90.00 at $0.10 a kWh in the example
  (`DEF-BIL-9077`).

## [2.439.5] — 2026-10-02

_Customer portal: an online application now reaches an active account without retyping, and one applicant keeps one customer number._

### Fixed
- **An address the utility does not hold yet can be applied for to the end**, and the applicant
  ticks the services they want from the utility's own list.
- **The clerk can pick the property and unit on a request that came in online**, sees the unit
  on the request page, and can link a customer already on file from the Approve window.
- **What the applicant typed online is carried forward**: date of birth, a business's Tax ID,
  email and phone, the services asked for, and the class the clerk picked now fill the move-in,
  the master account and New Connect instead of being asked for again.
- **One applicant, one customer number.** A new person's new connection used to create one
  customer for the owner's account and a second for the occupant's; the second door now finds
  the first one's customer.
- **An attached file no longer disappears from the application screen** when a field saves at
  the same moment.

### Checked
- Walked 21 times in a browser on PostgreSQL 16: 12 of 12 applications reached an active
  account the customer could see in the portal; 8 of 9 edge cases behave. Results:
  `08-qa/screens/portal-walk21-2026-10-02/RESULTS.md`.

## [2.439.4] — 2026-10-02

_Bills: every reading a bill charged for is locked, and a meter rollover waits for the clerk._

### Fixed
- **Every meter reading a bill charged for is now locked when the bill is issued.** Since a bill
  started counting every reading in its period (2.439.2), only the last one was being locked, so a
  clerk could still change a reading partway through the period after the customer had been billed
  for it, and the bill and the meter history would disagree. Changing one now goes through the
  billed-reading correction like any other (`DEF-BIL-9075`).
- **A one-time bill no longer under-charges a meter that rolled over partway through the period.**
  A 5-digit dial reading 99,800, rolling over to 240 on 1 Nov and read 700 on 13 Nov used 900 kWh;
  the bill charged 460. It now stops with *the meter rolled over — accept the rollover first*, and
  once the rollover is accepted it bills all 900 kWh (**$90.00** at $0.10). The bill run already
  asked this question after a previous bill; it now also asks it on a meter's first bill
  (`DEF-BIL-9076`). The one-time screen does not yet have the Accept control (`DEF-BIL-9077`).

## [2.439.3] — 2026-10-02

_Sample data and import template: the demo stops showing three things the rules no longer allow._

### Fixed
- **The sample utility no longer shows customers moving house as transfers.** Since 1 September a transfer
  is the sale of an account to a new customer, and a move is a new service request. The sample data still
  tried to seed five moves as transfers; four failed silently and one was left half-started. None is seeded
  now, and each says why. The Transfers tab on a new sample utility is empty (it showed 1 row)
  (`DEF-CUS-9072`).
- **The sample costed work order no longer changes a drawn new-connection build.** It finished a water
  meter set on CON-26-0121, which then read 3 of 5 orders done instead of 2 of 5. It now raises its own
  job at 3450 Oak Ridge Dr, the activated build, and records the outcome as **passed**, not
  "completed", which is not an outcome (`DEF-WRK-9070`, `DEF-WRK-9071`; its accept now goes through the Work seam, `DEF-WRK-9062`).
- **The meters import template's example row names a service that has meters.** On a utility selling
  water, sewer and trash it named sewer, with a blank size, because sewer gained a unit on 8 September.
  It names water again (`DEF-MET-9056`).
- Test-only: the other red cases brought up to the rules they test, among them the storm-water cases that left a
  whole sample utility behind in the PostgreSQL test database for later files to count (`DEF-RAT-9057`)
  (`DEF-BIL-9073`, `DEF-BIL-9054`, `DEF-MET-9055`, `DEF-RAT-9058`, `DEF-CUS-9059`–`9061`).

## [2.439.2] — 2026-10-02

_Bills: a meter reading partway through the period no longer cuts the bill off at it._

### Fixed
- **A bill now charges the whole period's usage when the meter was also read partway through it.**
  Each reading is stored as measured from the one before it, and a bill took the last reading's
  own figure alone, so everything used before a mid-period reading was never billed. Example: dials
  1,000 (15 Oct), 1,200 (1 Nov) and 1,300 (13 Nov) at $0.10 a kWh billed **100 kWh = $10.00** on a
  one-time bill; they now bill **300 kWh = $30.00**, and the bill shows 1,000 → 1,300. Time-of-use
  meters are counted per register, and the bill run no longer refuses a time-of-use meter in this
  case. Across a season change the reading on the change day still splits the usage: 200 × $0.12
  + 100 × $0.10 = **$34.00** (was $10.00). A period with one reading bills exactly as before
  (`DEF-BIL-9016`).

## [2.439.1] — 2026-10-02

### Fixed
- **`DEF-BIL-9004` (last window) — *Check again* takes Price away at once.** At 40,015 accounts the
  Check read takes about 2 seconds; for that long after *Check again* the old results stood with a
  pressable *Price*. The accepted job is now the step's state the moment the server takes it. Found
  re-photographing the walk on 2.438.4. Test: `CloseoutFixes.dom.test.tsx`, red first.

## [2.439.0] — 2026-10-02

_A portal move-in or new-connection request can now be carried by a clerk all the way to an active
customer — regular or master, a new customer number or a linked one (`CR-159-BRC10`, PO 2026-10-01)._

### Fixed
- **`DEF-CUS-9034` — the services an applicant ticks on the portal reach the request.** They were kept
  only as a sentence, so the request's Services table, the move-in job and the build were empty.
- **`DEF-CUS-9035` — a linked customer is no longer given a second customer number.** The move-in now

- **`DEF-MET-6119` — a new connection records every service it sells and how big it is.** Sewer, trash,
  fire and the panels and batteries of solar and battery reached the build on no key; they are now

### Added
- **`DEF-CUS-9036` — an approved request can end in the owner's master account.** The request page links
  to the property's master-account form, which carries the request: the linked customer (or the
  applicant), the class, and the pending move-in job closes. New Connect's owner account does the same.

Not fixed, filed: `DEF-MET-9037` (an unsized net meter on a solar or battery point will refuse that bill
once installed). Fire's device in New Connect waits on `OQ-1361`. Tests:
`06-backend/tests/test_portal_request_to_active.py` (9 cases, PostgreSQL, six services) and
`newConnectUnitServices.test.ts`; each fix red first.

## [2.438.4] — 2026-10-02

### Fixed
- **When water's usage waits for the next bill, sewer's usage waits with it.** Sewer is billed as 40% of
  water's volume, so *Bill base, usage later* on water left sewer with nothing to take a share of. The whole
  bill was refused: 40,004 of 40,009 accounts on the 40,000-account re-walk of `2.438.2`. Sewer now bills its
  base ($5.00 on the test world, beside water's $8.00 base), and both usages come on the next bill
  (`DEF-BIL-9009`).

## [2.438.3] — 2026-10-02

### Fixed
- **`DEF-BIL-9012` — a bill cut at one charge code's price change now splits only the service whose
  price changed** (PO 2026-10-01, option A: *"Split only the service whose price changed. Electric stays
  $12.00, and only water is split."*). A bill for 16 Oct – 15 Nov with water $8.00 → $9.00 from 11/01 and
  electric unchanged at $12.00 charged electric 16/31 × 12 + 15/30 × 12 = **$12.19** on two lines; it now
  charges **$12.00** on one line, and water stays split, $4.13 + $4.50 = **$8.63**. One shared path
  (`backbill.cut_groups`) serves the interim, first, final and cycle bills, the bulk run's *split at the
  change* answer and the catch-up. A rate-schedule version or plan change still cuts every service; the
  seasonal split is untouched. Tests: `test_def_bil_9012_cut_only_the_changed_service_pg.py` (8, red first
  on PostgreSQL); golden + bulk set on PostgreSQL 253 passed, 1 xfailed.

## [2.438.2] — 2026-10-02

### Fixed
- **A bill run opened again while *Check again* is still checking stays on Check and shows the progress.**
  A run that already held draft bills used to open on Sign off with dashes while all 40,015 accounts were
  being checked again (`DEF-BIL-9004`, `DEF-BIL-9010`, found re-walking the fix of `2.437.10`).

## [2.438.1] — 2026-10-02

_The test stack boots again on a fresh database (`DEF-INF-9033`)._

### Fixed
- **The standard end-to-end test stack boots on a database set up from October 1 onward.** Seeding the
  Brazos Bend test bill stopped with *"no partition of relation meter_reads"* for a September 2024 reading.
  Reading storage is split into monthly pieces made for 24 months back from the day the database is set
  up, and the seed writes fixed months from September 2024. The seed now makes sure a protected piece exists
  for every month it writes before it writes. No product behaviour changes.

## [2.438.0] — 2026-10-02

_Customers can attach documents to a new-service application on the portal (`CR-158-BRC10`)._

### Added
- **A customer applying for service on the portal can attach documents.** On *About you* the proof-of-identity
  box is now a real drop zone: PDF, JPG or PNG, up to 10 MB each, at most 5. Each file is listed with its type
  and size and can be removed before sending. Attaching stays optional; Send never waits for a file.
- **The clerk sees and opens them on the request.** The request's Documents tab shows each file's name, type,
  size and date, with Open and Download. Files come through our own route with safe headers, and another
  utility gets *not found*. Every upload, removal, open and download is in the audit log.

### Security
- The file type is read from the file itself, never from the browser. A wrong type or an oversized file is
  refused by its name. A file on an application nobody sent never reaches the utility's staff.

## [2.437.11] — 2026-10-02

_Lists fit their column, and the row icons are never cut off._

### Fixed
- **Rate schedules, Charge codes and Assets ran past the right edge at 1440**, and at 1280 Plans,
  Units and Meter reads did too, so the last icon on each row (Retire, on Rate schedules) was cut
  off and could not be clicked. Column headings may now wrap onto two lines when a list is short of
  room, which brings Rate schedules and Charge codes back inside the column at 1440. A list that
  still needs more room scrolls sideways inside its own box, never the page, and keeps its row
  icons pinned at the right edge (`DEF-SHL-5378`, `DEF-RAT-8842`).
- **The + Filter and ▦ Columns panels still open whole** — only the table scrolls, not the bar
  above it. A row's **…** menu on the last rows opens upward when it would otherwise be cut.
- Five lists still need more room than a 1280 laptop gives and scroll inside their box there;
  choosing which columns they show by default is filed as `DEF-SHL-9032`.

## [2.437.10] — 2026-10-02

_The bill run fixes from the 40,000-account walk._

### Fixed
- **An answer given to every account at once now reaches the bills.** *Bill base, usage later* for all
  40,010 accounts with no reading used to leave 40,005 of them failed with *"no usable read and no
  decision"*. The cause was any account with two unread meters (water and electric): the answer for all
  covered "the one unread meter" and so covered neither. It now covers every unread meter the clerk did
  not answer one by one (`DEF-BIL-9009`).
- **Start checking and Check again show *Checking accounts n of N* at once**, never *Checked 0 accounts*
  beside a *Price 0 accounts* button. The run now names its Check job the moment it is asked for, and Price
  is never offered while a Check or Calculate is under way (`DEF-BIL-9004`).
- **Calculate counts from the start.** Its first pass, about 11 minutes at 40,000 accounts, now shows
  *Reading accounts n of N* where it showed *0 of —*. A run opened again mid-way shows the progress instead
  of Sign off over half-made drafts (`DEF-BIL-9010`).
- **Smaller words and numbers:**
  - No reading counts accounts, not meters (`DEF-BIL-9005`).
  - With *Estimate* for all, the bar says each account needs a figure (`DEF-BIL-9006`).
  - Billing's counts read *40,017*, not *40017* (`DEF-BIL-9007`).
  - A sent run's card says *bills sent*, and Not in this run says *1 unit* (`DEF-BIL-9008`).

## [2.437.9] — 2026-10-01

_Seasonal pricing: a meter reading on the season-change day sets each season's usage._

### Fixed
- **A reading taken on the day the season changes now decides how much usage each season gets.**
  On a bill period that crosses a season change, an actual meter reading dated the first day of the
  new season now cuts the usage there, and each part is priced at its own season's rates; before,
  the usage was always shared out by calendar days. Example (15 Sep – 14 Oct, winter from 1 Oct):
  120 kWh on-peak with a 1 Oct reading showing 80 used before it bills `80 × $0.22 + 40 × $0.18` =
  **$24.80**, where the day split (64 / 56) billed $24.16; the whole sample meter bills usage
  **$83.50**, total **$104.53**, the same through the bill run and a one-time bill. With no reading
  that day, or only an estimate, nothing changes ($82.72 / $103.67). Works for time-of-use windows
  and for seasonal schedules (`DEF-RAT-8849`, PO 2026-10-01).

### Found
- `DEF-BIL-9016` — a reading inside the bill period that the closing reading is measured from makes a
  one-time bill charge only the usage after it (measured: 100 kWh billed of 300). Filed, not fixed.

## [2.434.0] — 2026-10-01

_Adding or editing a rate schedule is now three steps — Details, Pricing, Review — built from the drawings._

### Changed
- **New rate schedule and Edit are one three-step wizard: Details · Pricing · Review** (CR-157-BRC10,
  `05-prototype/rate-schedules-2026-10-01/images` 40–71). A summary of the schedule stays beside every step.
  - *Details*: name, service, unit, customer class, structure and the base charge code.
  - *Pricing*: the base rates table (one row per meter size, the base read from the code, a per-size
    minimum where *blank* reads *No minimum*) and the usage table drawn for the method — flat, tiered,
    time-of-use (the Window is a list and the meter register follows it), demand, seasonal (pick a start and
    end day; it repeats every year), capacity and percent of another service.
  - *Review*: what the schedule says, what changes against the version in force, when it starts, and the
    optional regulator filing.
- **Edit asks one question first: _Change the rate_ or _Fix an error_.** Change the rate makes a new
  version from a date and needs *What changed*; the version in force ends the day before. Fix an error keeps
  the same dates, needs a reason, and keeps the wrong version on record.
- **The per-version *Minimum rate on this version* field is gone** (PO, 2026-10-01): the minimum is set per
  meter size, and that is the one bills charge.

### Fixed
- **Tier boxes no longer show stored zeros** — an edit showed *From 0.000000, To 5.000000*; it now shows
  *0* and *5* (`DEF-RAT-8748`).
- A time-of-use schedule could not be saved from the new wizard: the first window now brings one
  whole-year season with it, which the server requires.

  the cent.

## [2.433.1] — 2026-10-01

_The September one-time bill reports, re-checked on today's build: 20 were already fixed, 2 fixed now, 1 waits for a ruling._

### Fixed
- **Move-outs list: a closing reading with no record of how it was taken now says so.** The Final read cell
  showed *Taken* and a bare dash; it now shows *Source not recorded* beside it, with the full sentence on
  hover (`DEF-CUS-7902`).
- A note inside the billing code said a one-time bill could not be sent; it can, and the note now says how
  (`DEF-BIL-8091`); and a send refused for missing days to pay now says *"No days to pay. Set them on the bill."* instead of a generic line.
- Two test reds found on the way, filed: a one-time page test that only passed on 30 September
  (`DEF-BIL-8806`, fixed), a billing refusal census (`DEF-BIL-8807`) and a Disconnects wording guard
  (`DEF-CUS-8808`) — the last two belong to other lanes and are open.

## [2.433.0] — 2026-10-01

_A bill is now topped up to the minimum set for the customer's meter size (rate schedules)._

### Changed
- **The minimum charge is set per meter size, and bills charge it** (DEF-RAT-8737, CR-157-BRC10). A water
  customer on a 5/8" meter using 1,000 gallons is billed $8.00 + $4.41 = $12.41; with a 5/8" minimum of
  $15.00 the bill is $15.00. On a 2" meter, $32.41 under a $40.00 minimum becomes $40.00. A size marked
  *No minimum* is not topped up.
- **The single minimum for a whole rate schedule version is no longer charged and can no longer be saved.**
  Where a schedule had one, it was copied onto every size that had no minimum of its own, so no bill changes
  (on the demo utility: $15.00 onto 9 water sizes).

## [2.432.2] — 2026-10-01

_A new utility gets its whole sample set whatever day of the month it signs up._

### Fixed
- **DEF-MET-8693:** signed up on the 1st to the 4th, the sample cycle's start day came out below 1 and 16
  sample blocks failed (no premises, meters, accounts, reads, bills or payments). It now starts on the 1st.
- **DEF-BIL-8755:** signed up on the 1st or 2nd, the second sample bill run issued 5 bills instead of 49.
- **DEF-PAY-8756:** signed up on the 1st to the 8th, the second month's sample payments were refused.
- **DEF-RAT-8757:** signed up from November 2026 on, the water rate schedule's sample versions clashed and
  the whole sample set failed. Every sign-up day now lands 75 accounts, 99 bills and 83 payments.

## [2.432.1] — 2026-10-01

_Settings › Configure › Asset types shows each type's category as a name._

### Fixed
- **DEF-TEN-8754:** the Category column read the stored codes `behind_the_meter`, `meters` and `sub_meters`;
  it now reads *Behind the meter*, *Meters* and *Sub-meters* (the same words as the Assets screen's tabs, in all
  eleven languages). A category with no name yet shows its code rather than nothing. Display only; no data
  changed.

## [2.432.0] — 2026-10-01

_The rate schedules list shows each schedule's customer class, base code and how many sizes are priced (rate schedules, part 2 of 3)._

### Changed
- **Rate schedules list, rebuilt from the agreed drawing:** columns Schedule · Service · Structure · Customer
  class · Base code · Sizes (`5 of 5`) · Effective · Plans · Accounts · Status · Actions. The service filter is a
  row of chips (`All · Water · Sewer …`) and is no longer repeated in `+ Filter`. A schedule with a change
  filed reads *In force* with *Scheduled* under it. Each row has Edit, Duplicate and Retire (CR-157-BRC10).
- **Rate schedule View details, rebuilt from the agreed drawing:** four tabs — Overview (Details and Billing
  rules), Rates (Base charges per size with Minimum, Units, Version, From and To, and *From BASE-W* linking to
  that charge code; Usage charges with the method named), Plans (with *Class differs*) and Audit (Filed as,
  Corrected). Tiles: In force · Units · Sizes priced · Next change, and a *Change scheduled* band when a later
  version is filed. The minimum is shown per size, as the PO ruled; a blank reads *No minimum*.
- **New reads for the schedule's own screens:** its base charges per size with version and dates, the units on
  each size, and the plans that use it (paged).

## [2.431.1] — 2026-10-01

_Trash sizes read carts first, and a base code's type reads "Every bill"._

### Fixed
- **Trash prices list the carts first, then the dumpsters, smallest first in each** — CART-35, CART-64,
  CART-96, then DUMP-2 to DUMP-8 — on the charge code's page and in the wizard, as the approved picture
  shows. Fire still reads 2″ to 12″ (`DEF-RAT-8717`).
- **A base charge code's Type reads "Every bill"** on its page (CR-156-BRC10).

## [2.431.0] — 2026-10-01

_The charge-code screens are rebuilt from the approved pictures (charge codes, part 2 of 3)._

### Changed
- **The charge-code list shows each code's kind and what it is priced by**, with chips to show only
  Base, Plan or Other codes and how many there are of each. A code priced by size shows its range — BASE-T
  reads **$9.00 – $40.00** instead of 0.00 — and a code with no GL account says *Not set* in amber.
- **A code's page changes with its kind**: tiles for plans, last month's bills and money; tabs Overview,
  Prices, Plans and Audit (an Other code has no Plans tab); a banner when new prices are scheduled; and an
  Audit list of every price version with who changed it and why.
- **New and Edit are one three-step wizard — Details, Pricing, Review — with a summary on the right that
  holds the GL account.** The code is picked from the Settings codes that are not in use yet, and the bill
  line fills itself in and can be changed. Every new price needs an *Effective from* date (*"Pick a date."*);
  an edit also needs a reason, and step 3 lists what changes, e.g. CART-64 **$12.00 → $13.00**.

### Fixed
- Fire line sizes are listed 2″, 4″, 6″, 8″, 10″, 12″ instead of 10″, 12″, 2″ … (`DEF-RAT-8717`).
- A base code no longer says *"The full amount is charged"*; it says *Cut down by days* (`DEF-RAT-8713`).
- A base code with one amount shows that one amount, not every size as *not priced* (`DEF-RAT-8714`).
- Step 3 reads back every setting chosen on step 1 (`DEF-RAT-8715`); help text is six words or fewer
  (`DEF-RAT-8716`); step 1 and step 3 show the same GL account (`DEF-RAT-8719`).

## [2.430.2] — 2026-10-01

_First and final bills now split at a charge-code price change, like the other bills._

### Fixed
- **A first or final bill that spans a price change charges each part at its own price.** A first bill
  16 October – 15 November with the base going from $9.00 to $10.00 on 1 November now charges
  **$4.65 + $5.00 = $9.65**; it charged **$10.00** before (DEF-BIL-8749, CR-156-BRC10).
- **A charge code with a flat price can be deleted again**, and its price goes with it (DEF-RAT-8751).

## [2.430.1] — 2026-10-01

_A part-month kW line shows the days it was charged for._

### Fixed
- **DEF-BIL-8744:** a solar or battery kW line on a part-month bill read *6 kW · $14.00 · $53.20*; it now
  reads *6 kW · $14.00 · 19/30 days · $53.20*, on the one-time bill's Review, the bill's Charges tab, the
  customer portal and the printed bill. No amount changed.

## [2.430.0] — 2026-10-01

_Two people saving the same rate schedule at once no longer see an error page (rate schedules, part 1 of 3)._

### Fixed
- **Two clerks filing the same rate change at the same moment:** the first is saved and the second now reads
  *"Versions may not overlap"*, instead of a server error. Nothing of the refused save is kept, and saving
  never deadlocks — a correction and a rate change pressed together both land (CR-157-BRC10, DEF-RAT-8750).
- **Two clerks activating the same saved draft at once:** the second reads *"This schedule is already
  active"*; before, the second could delete the version the first had just activated.

### Changed
- **A time-of-use window named On-peak, Mid-peak or Off-peak sets its meter register by itself**
  (On-peak → the on-peak register, and so on). A register that contradicts the name is refused. A window the
  utility names itself still states its register, as before.

## [2.429.2] — 2026-10-01

_A Send stops when the system is broken, instead of marking every bill as not sent._

### Fixed
- **A Send stops when ten bills in a row fail the same way** (`DEF-BIL-8747`). When the program was one update
  ahead of its database, a 40,000-bill Send marked 22,640 bills *not sent* in about five minutes and still
  finished. Now it stops after ten, says *Send stopped — a system fault*, marks no bill *not sent*, and does not
  finish. Once the fault is fixed, pressing Send again sends each remaining bill exactly once. One bad bill still
  goes on the *not sent* list and the rest of the Send carries on, as before.

## [2.429.1] — 2026-10-01

_The current charge-code screen keeps saving price changes while the dated screens are built._

### Fixed
- **A price change saved without a start date starts today** instead of being refused, so the charge-code
  screen in use today keeps working; the old price is kept, ending yesterday (CR-156-BRC10).

## [2.429.0] — 2026-10-01

_A charge code's price now has dates, and an old price is kept rather than deleted (charge codes, part 1 of 3)._

### Changed
- **A price change on a charge code starts on the date you choose and the old price is kept.** BASE-S $9.00
  set to $10.00 from 1 November keeps $9.00 ending 31 October; a September catch-up made in December still
  charges **$9.00**, an interim bill 16 October – 15 November charges **$4.65 + $5.00 = $9.65**, and November
  charges **$10.00** (CR-156-BRC10).
- **Editing a size price never deletes the others.** Changing BASE-T's 64-gallon cart from $12.00 to $13.00 and
  adding the 96-gallon cart at $15.00 keeps the $12.00 price (ending 31 October) and leaves the 35-gallon and
  2-yard prices exactly as they were.
- **A flat charge-code amount is stored as one "All sizes" price**, with the same dates and history as a size
  price; every existing amount was moved once.
- **Every charge code has a kind — base, plan or other** — set from the Product Owner's list.
- *Effective from* is required when a price is added or changed; *Effective to* is optional. Every price
  change is recorded in the rate history, not only changes to codes already in use.

### Note
- The charge-code screens that set the dates arrive with part 2. Until then a price changed on today's
  charge-code screen starts today, as it always did.

## [2.428.3] — 2026-10-01

_The rate schedule wizard is shorter, and its base rates are one table._

### Fixed
- **Step 1 — the base charge code is a dropdown.** It opens on a click with every code, and *Use the declared
  base* is its first choice (`DEF-RAT-8735`).
- **Step 2 — one table with `+ Add row`:** # · Size (only sizes no other row has) · Base charge (read-only) ·
  Minimum · ✕. The separate *Size to price* form and the *Set every size to / Set all* row are gone. Continue
  refuses a row with no size (`DEF-RAT-8736`).
- **Step 4 — 13 sentences down to 1.** No help lines, no *More about this step*, no *Not worked out yet* dashes,
  no *Counted, never zero.* The regulator reference sits with the other regulator fields (`DEF-RAT-8738`).
- **Step 5 — 10 sentences down to 4.** No subtitle, no *Owned by* or *Not read by billing yet* band, no footer
  sentences, no *worst case is unknown*; regulator rows nobody filled in are not shown (`DEF-RAT-8739`).
- **A blank per-size minimum reads back as *No minimum*,** not *No row* or 0 (`DEF-RAT-8740`).
- **Sizes are in size order** — Battery 5 kW before 10 kW, Water 5/8" before 1" — on step 2 and the review
  (`DEF-RAT-8741`).
- **A block reads *0 kW and above*,** not *0.000000 kW and above* (`DEF-RAT-8742`).

## [2.428.2] — 2026-10-01

_A bill that went out is never left listed as not sent after a Send is resumed._

### Fixed
- **Sent no longer lists bills that went out as not sent after a stopped Send carries on** (`DEF-BIL-8746`). When
  the machine sending bills stopped just after issuing some that had failed on an earlier try, those bills stayed
  on the *not sent* list: 985 of them on a 40,000-bill run. The Send now checks every bill when it finishes and
  clears the ones that went.
- **The bulk-run audit no longer fails a Send that was resumed or retried** (`DEF-BIL-8745`). A failed bill
  that later went out counts as sent, and a job the stopped machine left behind counts as done once its work
  finished.

### Measured
- **A 40,000-bill Send takes about an hour, not about 5.8 hours.** It sends 11–12 bills a second (was 1.9) in
  batches of 500. When the machine sending it was killed, the Send carried on by itself within 16–19 seconds.
  All 40,008 bills went out once, no bill number was used twice, and the books balanced at $7,371,531.12.


## [2.428.1] — 2026-10-01

_Two one-time bill fixes found by walking every one-time bill kind for a utility with six services (J75)._

### Fixed
- **A catch-up or penalty bill now prints trash and fire as one line per month**, as every other bill does: one 96-gallon cart is one "$18.00" line a month, not "$15.00" and "$3.00". Amounts unchanged (`DEF-BIL-8733`).
- **A solar or battery charge priced per kW now prorates on a part month, as the signed rule says**: a first bill for 19 of 30 days charges 6 kW × $14.00 × 19/30 = $53.20, not $84.00. Whole months are unchanged (`DEF-BIL-8743`).
- **A fee bill whose charge is not taxed now shows its fee as the subtotal**: a $75.00 reconnection fee reads Subtotal $75.00, Total $75.00 — it read Subtotal $0.00 (`DEF-BIL-8734`).
## [2.428.0] — 2026-10-01

_Sign off opens in half a second on a 40,000-account run, and its Amount due is what the bills will ask._

### Fixed
- **Sign off shows its figures on a 40,000-account run.** Its summary took four to six and a half minutes,
  so a production web worker (given 60 seconds) was stopped before it answered and the figures never
  appeared. It now opens in about 0.5 seconds: every figure is read once for the whole run, saved when
  Calculate finishes, and worked out again the moment anything it was built from changes — a decision, a
  re-Calculate, a payment. Every figure is the same as before, to the cent (`DEF-BIL-8696`).
- **Sign off's other figures (the bill count and total for Send) take 1 second, not 11** (`DEF-BIL-8697`).
- **A problem tag's account list opens in a twentieth of a second, not 3.3 seconds,** and the Ready list
  in a quarter of a second, not 3.8 — the check for changed accounts before every look now costs what
  changed, not the size of the run (`DEF-BIL-8694`).
- **Sign off's Amount due no longer counts the part of a payment plan that is not yet due.** A customer on
  a $45-a-month plan with $62 of new charges is asked $107, as the bill says; Sign off now shows the same,
  with the rest of the plan on its own line, *Plan, due later* (`DEF-BIL-8720`).

## [2.427.0] — 2026-10-01

_A capacity service's base is found by size on every bill, and a missing size price no longer stops the bill._

### Changed
- **Trash, fire, solar, battery and the other capacity services take their base per size: base for that size ×
  how many are installed.** Two 96-gallon carts with a $3.00 base and $15.00 carts bill one line of **$36.00**;
  two 2 kW panels and one 4 kW panel at $2.00 / $3.00 bill a **$7.00** base, the kW usage unchanged. Same on
  the bill run and on every one-time bill (BR-BIL-1067).
- **A size with no base price bills that size's base at $0.00 and the bill goes out**, with the warning
  *"BASE-T has no price for CART-96. Billed $0.00."* on Check, Sign off, Send and the one-time Review.

### Added
- **Every new bill line keeps what it was priced from** — unit, plan and version, rate version, customer type,
  base code, and per size the count, base and price — and the bill shows it under the line.

### Fixed
- **A base charge code priced by size could not bill a capacity service at all on the bill run** — the account
  was refused even when every size was priced (`DEF-BIL-8730`).

## [2.426.1] — 2026-10-01

_A new utility's first look at the product is no longer empty._

### Fixed
- **A utility that signs up for one service now gets sample bills for it.** Signed up for trash,
  storm water, solar, broadband, thermal/heat, battery or fire alone, the sample utility issued
  no bills at all; the equipment those services are counted on was never planted. It is now, and
  each of the ten services that can be sold alone issues sample bills that carry it (sewer alone
  is still refused — it is a share of water, and there is no water) (`DEF-BIL-8725`).
- **Storm water and thermal/heat are back on bills.** Since 30 September they were dropped from
  every bill, because neither can have equipment installed. A house at 1 ERU bills **$4.50** of
  storm water again; a 5-ton thermal connection **$62.50**.

## [2.426.0] — 2026-10-01

_A 40,000-bill Send is sent in pieces of 500, and carries on by itself when the machine sending it stops._

### Fixed
- **Send is cut into batches of 500, like the Check** (`DEF-BIL-8726`). It used to run as one background
  task, and a task is stopped after 8,520 seconds — at 1.9 bills a second that is about 16,000 bills, so a
  40,000-bill Send would have stopped part-way. Now 40,008 bills are 81 batches of at most 500; a utility
  runs half its billing workers' worth at a time (a platform setting, `BILLING_SEND_BATCHES_PER_UTILITY`,
  0 = half the workers, never fewer than 1). The last batch completes the release once.
- **A Send whose worker stops carries on by itself** (`DEF-BIL-8710`). The Send screen now polls its own
  read, which hands the Send back to a worker when none is on it — as the Check's screen already did — and
  pressing Send again does the same instead of re-attaching to the stuck job. Its *n of N* is counted from
  the bills already sent, so it never restarts at 0. No bill is issued twice and no invoice number is used
  twice: proved on PostgreSQL with a worker process killed half-way through a bill.

## [2.425.0] — 2026-10-01

_A landlord's bill with an empty unit goes out, and a meter never read is the clerk's decision._

### Fixed
- **An owner's bill that includes an empty unit's base charge is billed again.** It was refused
  outright. 1408 Elm's owner now gets the hallway $41.20 + irrigation $28.40 + empty Unit D's
  $12.00 base = **$81.60** (`DEF-BIL-8724`).

### Added
- **Bill run Check: "Meter never read".** A meter that has never been read has no multiplier.
  The account used to be blocked as *Pricing refused*; it is now its own decision under Meter
  history — **Hold** (pre-selected) or **Bill with multiplier 1** — saved with who and when, and
  kept through Re-check (changes row 44, PO 2026-09-30).

## [2.424.2] — 2026-10-01

_The move-out screen's final bill follows the Product Owner's ruling of 2026-10-01._

### Fixed
- **The move-out screen no longer prices a final bill for an account with no billing cycle.** It
  charged the whole month's base for a part month — ten days charged the month's $30.50. It now
  shows *"No billing cycle. Assign one on the account."* and no figure, the same as the One-time
  tab (`DEF-BIL-8702`).

## [2.424.1] — 2026-10-01

_A closed account's deposit can be read again._

### Fixed
- **The deposit position no longer fails for a closed account holding a deposit.** It showed an
  error for every such account. Interest is now stated at the day the account closed — the same
  day the final bill settles the deposit. A $150.00 deposit at 2%, received 15 June 2025 and
  closed 15 August 2026, shows **$3.50** interest and **$153.50** to carry forward (`DEF-CUS-8711`).

## [2.424.0] — 2026-10-01

_Send no longer slows down as a utility keeps more months of bills._

### Fixed
- **Each bill line is found by its own index when a bill is sent** (`DEF-BIL-8708`). Sending stamps
  every line with its ledger account, and each of those updates used to read through every line the
  utility had ever billed — 68 ms a line at 300,000 lines, about 7.5 lines a bill, so a 40,000-bill
  Send ran at 1.9 bills a second. A new index on the line's id (billing migration 0037) finds it
  directly. Writes to bill lines wait while the index is built; on 300,000 lines that is about a
  second.

## [2.423.0] — 2026-10-01

_The Product Owner's ruling of 2026-10-01: an interim bill cuts the base down by days._

### Changed
- **An interim bill charges the base for the days it covers.** An interim bill for 10 days of a
  30-day cycle on a $30.50 base now charges **$10.17** (10/30 × $30.50) instead of the whole $30.50,
  the same way first and final bills already do. A 20-day window of a 31-day cycle prorates bases
  of $12.00, $8.00 and $18.00 to $7.74, $5.16 and $11.61 — **$24.51**, not $38.00. A whole-cycle
  interim bill is unchanged.
- **An interim bill for an account with no billing cycle is refused**, with the first bill's
  warning: *"No billing cycle. Assign one on the account."*

### Records
- `OQ-242` closed for interim bills (option (a)); `BR-BIL-1066`. Catch-up, penalty and fee bills
  are not changed. The demo sewer base of $9.00 a month is confirmed by the PO.
- J74's fee case checks its date against the day the bill was raised, not a fixed 30 September.

## [2.422.4] — 2026-10-01

_One sentence on the level-pay screen, spelled the way the rest of the product spells it._

### Fixed
- **Level pay says "Enroll", not "Enrol".** The note under the enrolment step reads *Enroll accounts
  one at a time. No list import.* — the server sent the British spelling while the screen's own
  English was American (DEF-BIL-8721).

## [2.422.3] — 2026-10-01

_The bulk bill run's last four drawing differences, each waiting on a fact the server now sends._

### Fixed
- **Scope says the cycle's frequency.** A 45-day period on a monthly cycle reads *45 days. Cycle is
  monthly. Ends after today.*, beside the field and in the warnings, in every language — it read
  *Cycle expects 30.*
- **Check names the meter.** A row's service reads *Water · W-10442* — the meter's own number.
- **Sign off shows payments apart from credits**, each with how many, and reads the same window the
  bill does (everything received since the last bill). A customer who paid $120.00 against a $34.00
  bill, was given a $10.00 credit and refunded $5.00 now shows *Payments applied $115.00 · Credits
  applied $10.00* and *Amount due −$53.75* on Sign off — exactly what their bill will print. Sign off
  showed *$0.00* paid and *$37.25* due.
- **Sent says the meter reads are locked.** *Meter reads: Locked* once every reading the sent bills
  used is marked billed in Meter Reads.

## [2.422.2] — 2026-10-01

_Records and walks for the six rulings of 2026-10-01; one screen change._

### Changed
- **The bill screen shows a credit as a credit.** A bill whose customer is in credit reads
  *Total due $0.00 · Credit $48.75* instead of *-$48.75*, matching the paper bill.

### Records
- Defects closed: `DEF-BIL-8566` (cart prorates), `DEF-BIL-8246` (no default plan), `DEF-BIL-8670`
  and `DEF-BIL-8412` (whole-account balance forward).
- J74 re-walked on a fresh database: the seven priced bills equal their re-priced totals to the
  cent. J72's September run passes the database audit, with `AC-2026-00007` green.

## [2.422.1] — 2026-10-01

_The Product Owner's beta report of 2026-10-01 on correcting a rate schedule (DEF-RAT-8703, 8704, 8705)._

### Fixed
- **Saving a rate that starts later no longer says it is live.** Correcting a version that starts on
  1 October, on 30 September, now says *"<schedule> starts 10/01/2026."* instead of *"is live"*, which
  matches the list's `Draft` · `Change scheduled — effective 10/01/2026` until that day.
- **Fix an error says how to move the dates.** The dates stay locked, as ruled; the step now reads
  *"New dates? Choose Change the rate."*
- **"We could not count the bills." is gone for a rate that has not started.** The count now asks about
  the version being corrected, so it reads *"No bills went out on this."*

## [2.422.0] — 2026-10-01

_The Product Owner's rulings of 2026-10-01 on what a bill asks for._

### Changed
- **A bill reads the whole account since the last bill.** A customer whose $34.00 bill was paid with
  $120.00 now sees *$34.00 − $120.00 + $37.25 = a $48.75 credit, nothing to pay*, where the bill
  printed *Total due $37.25*. A bill paid in full last month reads *100.00 − 100.00*.
- **A payment-plan customer's bill asks for the new charges plus this month's instalment.** $62 + $45
  = **$107.00** due; the other $225.00 of the plan is printed as not yet due.
- **"Apply next bill" now puts a late payment on the next bill.** It used to bill exactly like
  "Apply to this bill".

## [2.421.0] — 2026-10-01

_The Product Owner's ruling of 2026-10-01 on a meter swapped mid-month._

### Changed
- **A meter swapped mid-month: each meter is priced on its own.** Old meter 120 units and new
  meter 80 units on a tiered rate (first 100 at $0.10, then $0.15) now bill $13.00 + $8.00 =
  **$21.00**, each meter starting at the first tier, instead of 200 units priced once at $25.00.
  Each meter has its own line and its own readings; the base charge is charged once.

## [2.420.0] — 2026-10-01

_The Product Owner's ruling of 2026-10-01 on a unit with no plan._

### Changed
- **A unit with no plan is not billed until its plan is set — there is no default plan.** On the
  bill run's Check, *No plan* now holds the account with *"No plan on the unit. Set the plan
  first."* The clerk sets the plan on the row and re-checks. The *Use default plan* answer is gone.

## [2.419.0] — 2026-10-01

_Two of the Product Owner's six rulings of 2026-10-01._

### Changed
- **A trash cart on a part month is charged for the days, like the base.** One cart on an
  18-of-30-day final bill is 18/30 × $15.00 = **$9.00** (was $15.00). A month split at a price
  change charges each part its share: $7.26 + $7.74. Whole months are unchanged. Fire lines follow
  the same rule.
- **A final bill for an account with no billing cycle is refused, like a first bill.** Step 1 says
  *"No billing cycle. Assign one on the account."* as soon as the account is picked, and nothing is
  drafted until the account has a cycle.

## [2.418.9] — 2026-10-01

## [2.418.0] — 2026-10-01

_The bulk bill run's Check runs in parallel batches of 500 (plan B28, changes row 55)._

### Changed
- **Bill run, Check: the accounts are checked in batches of 500, several at
  once.** One way for every size: 300 accounts is 1 batch, 1,000 is 2, 40,000
  is 80. A utility runs at most half the billing workers' worth of batches at
  a time (never fewer than 1) — 8 workers, 4 batches — so another utility's run
  is never held up behind it. The figure is a platform setting
  (`BILLING_WORKERS`, `BILLING_CHECK_BATCHES_PER_UTILITY`); changing it needs no
  release. *Checking accounts — n of N* adds up every batch; the run's totals
  are counted once, when the last batch finishes.
- **A Check that stopped resumes batch by batch.** A worker lost in batch 3 of
  5 re-checks only what batch 3 had not saved, then batches 4 and 5; batches 1
  and 2 are not touched. A finished batch delivered twice writes nothing.

### Operators
- Set `BILLING_WORKERS` to the number of billing worker slots infrastructure
  runs (default 2). An existing `.env` does not pick this up by itself.


_The bulk bill run's last clerk checks: what happens when something breaks._

### Added
- **Bill run, Check: "Answer for all" now opens on the utility's Billing
  default** (DEF-BIL-8418). With Settings → Billing defaults saying *estimate
  when there is no reading*, the No-reading tag opens with *Estimate* chosen
  and the run keeps it. Other tags open on their usual first answer with an
  *Apply to all* button, so nothing is decided for the clerk.
- **Bill run, Send: bills that could not be sent are listed apart, each with
  its reason, and "Retry failed" sends only those** (DEF-BIL-8421,
  DEF-BIL-8581). *7 bills sent · 1 bill not sent* — See breaks shows
  AC-2026-00008, *A service has no revenue account.* Retry sends that one bill
  again; the 7 already sent are never sent twice. The list survives a refresh.
- **Bill run: a second clerk opening the run is told who else is on it**
  (DEF-BIL-8512) — *"Also on this run: Dana Whitfield."*
- **Bill run, Check: a Check that stopped part-way says how far it got and
  offers Resume** — *"Checking stopped at 400 of 1,406."*
- **Bill run, Scope: "See units" and "See services" now list the units and
  services behind the two counts** (DEF-BIL-8221). *Nobody to bill* shows each
  unit's address, its services and its last account, with **Add account ↗**;
  *Missing meter* shows the unit, the service and the account, with **Fit a
  meter ↗**. Both open the unit in a new tab. The lists are paged.
- **Bill run, Scope: the Bill template list offers every published bill
  template** (DEF-BIL-8222), each with its version — *Standard bill · v4*,
  *Winter insert · v1*. A template with only a draft is not offered and is
  still refused if chosen another way.
- **Bill run, Check: accepting "Meter swapped" bills both meters' parts**
  (DEF-BIL-8244) instead of holding the account.
- **Bill run, Check: the Ready to bill list shows each account's services, its
  plan, and whether every reading was read** (DEF-BIL-8414) — *Electric ·
  Water · Residential 2026 · All read*, or *Some estimated*.

### Fixed
- **Bill run: no account is billed while a question about it is still open**
  (DEF-BIL-8650). *Standing charges only* and *Gap or overlap* now have to be
  answered, like the other questions. Before, AC-2026-00009 was billed $63.25
  and AC-2026-00011 $8.00 with nobody answering; both now wait in *Not in
  this run*.
- **Bill run: "Apply to this bill" is refused for a payment that has not
  cleared** (DEF-BIL-8651) — *"Payment not cleared yet. Apply next bill."*
  Before, the bill said *payments received $0.00* next to a $120.00 payment.
- **Bill run: an account with no reading that nobody answered ends in one
  place** (DEF-BIL-8653), *Not in this run*, instead of also breaking at
  Calculate.
- **A billing worker that dies mid-Check no longer leaves the run stuck for
  hours** (DEF-BIL-8511). The Check screen notices within about 20 seconds that
  no worker has the job and hands it back to the billing worker, which carries
  on from the last account it saved. Resume does the same, and never runs the
  rest of the Check inside the clerk's page request (which is cut off after 60
  seconds). Before, the job came back only after 8,820 seconds.
- **"Meter Reads is not answering" now says who fixes it and gives the same
  reference support sees in the log** (DEF-BIL-8580) — *"Meter Reads is not
  answering. No account was checked. Support can fix this. … Ref
  SBH-73FBC9D7."* It used to show a generic error.
- **Two clerks pressing Send at the same moment still send each bill once** —
  proved on PostgreSQL; the second Send files nothing as "not sent".

### For testers
- A test-only switch takes Meter Reads down on a walk stack (DEF-BIL-8510):
  start the server with `SBH_WALK_SWITCHES_DIR=<dir>` and create
  `<dir>/meter_reads.down`. Production can never use it.
- `seed_j72_bulk_run --send-failure` now really breaks one bill at Send, and
  `--late-october-read` plants the October reading after September is sent so
  the 7 kgal estimate true-up can be walked (DEF-BIL-8420).
