## [2.380.1] — 2026-09-27

### Fixed
- **A bill now charges the base charge code you picked on the rate schedule.**
  Where your catalogue holds more than one charge code ticked as a service's
  base charge, the first step of the rate schedule lets you say which one that
  schedule uses. That choice was saved and shown on screen, and the part of the
  product that produces bills was never told about it — so every bill on that
  schedule stopped with *"3 base charge codes for water. Scope them on Charge
  codes."*, and a move-out final bill could not be produced at all. The bill
  now charges the code you picked.
- **And it says which code when that code stops being usable.** If the code you
  picked is later retired, has its base tick taken off, or is narrowed to a kind
  of customer this account is not, the bill for that one account stops and names
  it — *"BASE-W-COM cannot price water here. Change it on the rate schedule."*
  It does not quietly fall back to some other code, which would put a figure on
  the bill that the rate schedule's own screen does not show. Every other
  account in the run still bills.
- **Nothing changes for a schedule that names no code.** More than one base
  charge code and nobody choosing still stops the bill, in the same words as
  before: with no choice made, the order of a list would decide what a customer
  pays.

## [2.380.0] — 2026-09-27

### Added
- **Reports has a Dashboard tab.** It answers one question — *how are we
  doing* — over one accounting period, and it does not touch the dashboard you
  already have. That one is still the screen after every sign-in and is still a
  clerk's morning glance at what needs them today; this one is an owner's
  monthly read. Pick a month, pick what to compare it against, and every figure
  and every panel moves with it.
- **Four figures across the top: billed, collected, outstanding and days to
  collect.** Each carries its comparison underneath — *3.10% against the
  comparison* — so a number never appears on its own. Days to collect reads
  *Not counted yet*, because no report in the product works that figure out and
  this screen never works one out for itself.
- **Five panels under them, and each one is a report shown small.** Revenue
  over twelve months as bars with the chosen month picked out; where the money
  sits, by how old it is; the mix by service; the biggest movers; and whether
  the month's books foot. Open any panel and the report behind it opens *on the
  same month* — the window never changes under you.
- **The month is in the address bar**, so a link pasted into a board pack opens
  on the same month for whoever receives it. Nothing is remembered and nothing
  is saved: reload and it returns to the current period.
- Two things are deliberately blank with a short reason under them: the biggest
  movers, because nothing in the product publishes how one account's usage
  changed between two months, and comparing against a budget, because nothing
  publishes a budget. Both would have meant this screen inventing a figure.

## [2.379.0] — 2026-09-27

### Added
- **A utility can now say how long its downloads are kept.** Settings →
  Configure → Reference data has a new **Reports** section with two cards.
  *File retention* sets the number of days a generated file stays available;
  it was fixed at three for everybody and no screen said so. The change takes
  effect at once on every run already in the history — a file that was
  downloadable an hour ago shows as expired the moment a shorter window is
  saved, and nothing is deleted by the save itself.
- **And what a download is, unless somebody asks for something else.**
  *Default format* is the second card. CSV is the only answer the product can
  give today, so the control offers one and says so rather than pretending
  there is a choice. A report schedule created without naming a format now
  takes this one.
- **The Reports history screen links to the setting it describes.** The line
  under the table used to read *"Files are kept for 3 days"* whatever the
  utility had chosen. It now states the utility's own number, and for a System
  Admin it carries a link straight to the control. A clerk sees the fact and
  no link, because the form behind it is not theirs to change.


## [2.378.0] — 2026-09-27

### Added
- **Disconnect & Reconnect now opens, and it shows one line per account.** The
  report lists the accounts that have been cut off or are on their way there,
  newest notice first, and each account appears once — on the case it is on
  now. Earlier cut-offs are counted beside it rather than listed as extra
  lines, so the balance at the foot is what those accounts owe today and not
  the same customer added up twice. An account cut for $210 in June, restored,
  and cut again for $185 in September is one line reading $185.
- Two figures the drawing shows are left blank on purpose, each with a short
  reason under it: the product has no rule of its own for who is *eligible*
  for disconnection — that lives in Settings — and a disconnection case records
  what was owed when it opened, never what has been paid since.
- The report's Download button writes the whole list, not the page on screen.

## [2.377.7] — 2026-09-27

### Fixed
- **A rate schedule keeps the base charge code it names when you put a new
  price in from a date.** On the first step of a rate schedule you pick the
  charge code the base comes from. Putting a new price in from a date,
  correcting a price, or running a bulk increase across every schedule threw
  that choice away and the schedule went back to guessing — and the screen
  went on showing your choice until the page was reloaded, so there was
  nothing to see. Emptying that box on purpose still empties it: keeping a
  choice you did not mention and clearing one you did are two different
  things, and the product now tells them apart.

## [2.377.6] — 2026-09-27

### Fixed
- **The Accounts list now says when it could not show you a service.** A row
  showing two service letters used to mean one of two different things — this
  account takes two services, or the list lost some on the way to the screen —
  and there was no way to tell them apart. Now a row that lost something shows
  a small `?2` beside the letters, reading *2 services not shown*. A row that
  lost nothing looks exactly as it did.
- **And somebody hears about it even when nobody is looking at the screen.**
  Every time it happens the system writes a line naming the account, so we can
  answer *how often does this happen* instead of waiting for it to be spotted.

### Note
- **Nothing about what the letters MEAN has changed.** They are still the
  services this account has agreed to take, not the services the building
  offers — an owner's account reads the building, an ordinary one reads its
  own agreements, exactly as before. On the utilities we can measure today
  this happens on none of 479 live agreements; the point of the change is that
  we would not have known if it did.

## [2.377.5] — 2026-09-27

### Fixed
- **We checked whether one utility can read another utility's report schedule.
  It cannot.** On a real PostgreSQL database, a schedule belonging to one
  utility was planted and then asked for from a second utility's session three
  different ways — a plain listing, a lookup by its own id, and the screen's own
  request. All three came back with nothing, and the request answered *not
  found*. Asked with no utility open at all, it also came back with nothing.
- **Five of the Reports tests had been failing since the morning they were
  written, and all five were wrong about the product rather than the other way
  round.** Two read the refusal message from a place it has never been sent,
  one compared a date to a piece of text, and one checked the wrong half of a
  fact the product gets right. The fifth is the isolation check above: it was
  being run against a test database that has no such protection built in, so it
  could never have answered the question either way — it now runs against a
  real one.

### Note
- **One real gap was found while reading them and is not fixed here.** If a
  report run cannot even be STARTED — the queue itself refusing it, rather than
  the report failing once it has begun — the schedule still shows as *On*
  instead of *Failing*. It is written down as `DEF-REP-6929`.

## [2.377.4] — 2026-09-27

### Fixed
- `DEF-REP-6928` — the `2.377.0` entry carried a bare `## 2.377.0` heading and sat
  at the foot of the file, below a stale trailing `[Unreleased]` block. It is now
  `## [2.377.0]`, in version order with every other release. 727 of 728 headings
  were already bracketed; this was the one that was not, and `G35` reads the
  bracket, so the entry was invisible to the only gate that looks.

## [2.377.3] — 2026-09-27

### Fixed
- **A plan now shows the base charge its rate schedule actually names.** Step 4
  of the plan wizard states the monthly base for each service. Where the bound
  water schedule named `BASE-W-FIRE` at $12.00, the step showed `BASE-W` with no
  amount at all — a different code, no price, on a plan that is priced. It now
  reads **12.00 · named BASE-W-FIRE**, and the word *named* is how a clerk can
  tell the code the schedule chose from the one the catalogue happened to list
  first. Reported from the live product on Residential City Plan.
- **Where the schedule names nothing, nothing changes.** The step still falls
  back to the service's own base code and still says *from* rather than *named*,
  which is what every schedule in the product does today.
- **A named code that has since been retired is said out loud.** The step reads
  *Named base code not found.* rather than quietly drawing the other code — the
  bill would not use that one, and a plan showing a price its bills will not
  charge is worse than a plan showing none.

## [2.377.2] — 2026-09-27

*Written after the fact, from the commit, by lane FIX-SMALL (`DEF-GOV-6930`).*

### Fixed
- **A spare meter on the shelf now says what it measures in.** On the Assets
  tab of a unit, four spares carried no size class at all and every one of them
  read `Meter · —`: three water meters and one electric, with nothing on the
  screen to tell them apart. There is a **Unit of measure** column now, and the
  size column reads the tenant's own words.
- **Both tables on that screen name a size the same way.** The assigned table
  printed the stored code — `W-58`, `E-1P-100` — while the shelf panel beside
  it read `Water 5/8"` and `Electric 1φ 100A` for those same codes. Both
  resolve through one lookup now, so they cannot drift apart again.
- **Every dash is words.** A cart, a battery, a backflow preventer, a solar
  array, a charger and a communications unit read **not measured**, because
  they never will be; a meter missing its size or unit reads **no size
  recorded** — a gap worth closing rather than a fact that does not exist.
  Reported from the live product on the Assets tab of a unit.
## [2.377.1] — 2026-09-27

*Written after the fact, from the commit, by lane FIX-SMALL (`DEF-GOV-6930`).*

### Added
- **A person can schedule a report.** The dialog that sets one up had been
  built, tested and mounted by nothing at all — the only thing that opened it
  was its own test, and the report screen offered thirty-nine controls with not
  one of them saying Schedule. There is a **Schedule** button on the report
  screen now, beside Edit. Where a report cannot be produced at all the button
  is there and cannot be pressed, with no explanation attached to it.

### Fixed
- **A refusal says the server's own words instead of a fixed sentence.** Every
  refused report told the reader they cannot run reports — shown to a Billing
  Clerk who is served seventeen report links. A report they may not see now
  says why that report, and the module-wide refusal is unchanged.
- **Scheduling now asks the same permission question that opening does.** A
  clerk refused a report on screen could still have it emailed to themselves
  every month. Nothing had found it because until this release there was no way
  to reach the schedule at all.
## [2.377.0] — 2026-09-27 — the first three joining reads

**`CR-142-BRC07` `P6.11`.** Three reports whose drawing states a grain no
dataset holds now serve rows: **R36 Access Review** (one user of this tenant),
**R32 Read Import Log** (one read-import batch) and **R23 Account Activity**
(one account-lifecycle event). Each is served by a per-report viewer over a read
model in the module that owns the spine; the dataset refusals that named them
stay exactly as they were, because a refusal deleted the day its read model
lands is one nobody can read when the wiring rots.

**On screen:** a report column that is a boolean now renders as a word instead
of `true`, and an ISO timestamp renders as a date in the tenant's own format.
Both were found by photographing the screen. Access Review's *Last sign-in*
column is labelled **Last active**, which is what the stored value is.

**Counted:** `CR-142-BRC07` §9.2 said fifteen multi-source reports; read against
the drawings it is **seventeen**. Three are built; six of the remaining
fourteen now have a PO ruling and none of those six is built yet.

## [2.376.1] — 2026-09-27

### Fixed
- **A property's utility services now show in the header of its page.** Open a
  property and the services it takes — Water, Sewer, Trash, Fire — sit right
  under the address, beside its route and cycle, each with its own colour. They
  were only ever written far down the Overview tab, so a clerk had to scroll
  past ten facts to learn what a building buys. Reported from the live product
  on a property carrying four of them. A property that takes no service shows
  nothing there at all — no empty row and no stray dot — and the fact further
  down still says whether nobody has been asked or the answer was none.

## [2.376.0] — 2026-09-27

### Added
- **A scheduled report now tells the people it was scheduled for.** Until today
  a schedule produced its file on time and nobody was told: the report ran, the
  file appeared on History, and the list of people the schedule named was never
  read again. Set the AR ageing to run on the first of the month and pick
  yourself, and on the first of the month you get an email saying it ran, with a
  link to it.
- **The email carries a LINK and never the file.** A spreadsheet of your
  customers' names, addresses and balances on an email can be forwarded by
  anyone who receives it; the link only opens for somebody who can already sign
  in to your utility. It cannot be edited out — a version of the message without
  it is refused when you try to save it.
- **The message can be switched off, like every other one.** *Scheduled report
  ready — email* is a row on Settings → Notifications. Turn it off and no
  message is written at all.
- **A report that FAILS still tells nobody.** The schedule stays in the list
  marked *Failing* so somebody looks, and no email goes out claiming a file is
  ready.

### Note
- **Nothing is sent yet.** Email delivery ships with all email in a later
  release; what this adds is the message, queued and ready, and the words it
  will say — which are ours until you tell us otherwise (`OQ-REP-12757`).


## [2.375.0] — 2026-09-27

### Added
- **The access-review report is now restricted to System Admins and
  Executives, as it was agreed it would be.** It lists every member of staff,
  their role, who added them, when they last signed in and whether they can
  approve money. That has been written down as a rule since 8 August and, until
  today, anybody with a login could open it — including a billing clerk, who can
  see the other forty-four reports and should not see this one. A clerk is no
  longer shown the card at all, and typing the address in directly is refused.
  Nothing changes for a System Admin or an Executive.

## [2.374.0] — 2026-09-27
### Added
- **A customer statement now reads like a bank statement: both sides, in date order.** It opens on an account and shows an opening balance, every charge and every payment as they were posted, and a closing balance — `$0.00` opening, `$470.59` charged, `$470.59` paid, `$0.00` closing on the account photographed for this release, with the running balance carried down the page. Until now the statement was built from bills alone, so it could show what a customer owed and never what they had paid.
- **Three of its four grains say plainly that they are not built yet.** Asking for a statement about a customer, a building or a unit answers with what is missing rather than quietly showing one account's money under the wrong heading.

### Fixed
- **Choosing what a report is about now reaches the server.** A report address naming an account was rebuilt without it on the way out of the browser, so the screen showed four empty tiles over a link that named one.

### Known
- **My Bills & Payments cannot show a payment.** The customer-facing version of the statement is still built from bills alone and refuses to open rather than showing half a story. It is recorded and waiting on one decision about whether it should show both sides too.
- **A brand-new deployment cannot install the report catalogue.** The forty-six reports we ship are written in a way the live database account is not permitted to write. Deployments that already exist are unaffected; this is recorded and open.

## [2.373.1] — 2026-09-27

### Fixed
- **Twenty-seven reports told a clerk the system had broken when it had not.**
  Opening any of them drew a red panel headed *"The finance figures could not
  be loaded"* — on a meter-reads report — with *"Something went wrong on our
  side. Nothing was saved."* under it. Nothing had gone wrong and nothing was
  being saved. The product already knew why each of those reports could not be
  produced, and said so correctly on its card in the report library two clicks
  earlier; the viewer threw that answer away. Each of them now says the same
  thing the card says: **"This report cannot be produced yet."** The eighteen
  reports that work are untouched, and a real failure still reads as a real
  failure.
- **A report that cannot be produced was headed with its internal name.** With
  no figures to show, the page title fell back to the slug, so the screen read
  `read_completeness` where the card the clerk had just clicked read *Read
  Completeness*. It now carries the name from the library.


## [2.373.0] — 2026-09-27

### Added
- **Seven more reports now actually open and show rows.** Account Census, Meter
  Fleet, Service Order Activity, Audit Trail, My Usage, Usage & Ranking and
  Consumption Exceptions were all built and none of them could be reached from
  the report library — each answered *this report has no engine yet* over an
  engine that was finished, measured and tested. Eighteen reports in the
  catalogue were in that state; none is now.
- **Every report in the library now either opens or says, in its own words, why
  it cannot.** Twenty-eight of the forty-six answer a question the data behind
  them does not hold — a report drawn one row per route over data held one row
  per reading, for instance — and each of those says so and names what it would
  need, instead of showing a table that adds up correctly and answers something
  else.

### Fixed
- **A card in the report library no longer says a report can be produced when
  opening it would refuse.** The library asked only whether the data behind a
  report existed, not whether that data could answer this particular report, so
  for one build every card in the catalogue looked available. A card now
  promises only what a click will deliver.

## [2.372.1] — 2026-09-27

### Fixed
- **The triangle that opens a group row asked for a corner rounding the product
  does not define**, so that one instruction did nothing at all. Nothing looked
  wrong — the control drew and worked — and no test could have seen it, because
  a style rule that is never generated is invisible to every check that reads
  the code rather than the page. The instruction is removed; the control is
  unchanged on screen.

## [2.372.0] — 2026-09-27

### Added
- **A grouped report now opens showing its top level, and a group opens the
  level underneath it where you stand.** A report grouped by year, then month,
  then service used to draw all three at once with no way to fold any of them
  away. It opens on the year now; clicking the triangle beside it shows the
  months, clicking a month shows the services, and clicking again folds them
  back. Nothing is fetched to do it — the whole grouping already arrives with
  the report — so opening and closing is instant and never reloads the page.
- **A group with nothing underneath it has no triangle at all**, rather than one
  that does nothing when you click it. Of the forty-six reports in the product
  only one groups three levels deep and two group one level, so on nearly every
  grouped report the bottom row is the end of the road; the screen says so by
  offering no control rather than by offering a dead one.


## [2.371.1] — 2026-09-27

### Fixed
- **The work-order reports that open sorted by the date a job was raised no
  longer read and re-sort every work order to answer a page.** At a utility with
  40,000 work orders the database had to read all of them and sort them from
  scratch each time, writing several megabytes of scratch data to disk on the
  later pages. Fetching a page of rows is now about nineteen times faster on the
  first page and about four times faster on the last, and nothing is written to
  disk to do it. The screen as a whole is about a fifth faster: the rest of what
  it costs is the summary tiles at the top, which add up every order on purpose
  so the totals describe the report and not the page you are looking at.

## [2.371.0] — 2026-09-27

### Fixed
- **A census as at a past date now shows each account as it WAS on that date,
  not as it reads today.** An account that moved from Residential to Commercial
  in September was appearing as Commercial in June's figures — the exact thing
  the history we already keep was built to prevent. The counts across the top
  and the class and status filters follow the same date, so the tile, the chip
  and the row now agree.
- **Where no history exists for a date, the row says so rather than pretending.**
  Anything that last changed before the history started being kept falls back to
  today's value, is marked on the row, and the report states how many rows did
  that — *12 of 50* rather than a warning that would be true of every report
  forever.

## [2.370.0] — 2026-09-27

### Added
- **The machinery behind three more reports: Account Census, Audit Trail and
  Bill Delivery.** Account Census lists every account as at a date you choose —
  the customer, the address, the services, the status and the balance — with
  counts of how many you have, how many are live, how many are closed and how
  many owe money. Audit Trail lists every recorded act with who did it, what it
  was, and what it read before and after. Bill Delivery lists every bill that
  went out, on every channel, with the address it went to, whether it arrived
  and why it did not. All three come back a page at a time however large the
  utility is, and all three download in full.
- **Bill Delivery needed a kind of report data this product did not have, and it
  has it now.** Nothing is recorded in the audit trail when an email bounces —
  a bounce is the mail provider telling us something, not an act anybody
  performed — so the report reads the message queue itself, which already held
  every column it needs.
- **The retention figure on Audit Trail is the real one.** It reads the period
  actually in force and the oldest day the trail still holds, rather than a
  figure typed into the page.

### Changed
- **Account counts are worked out from what a status DOES, not from its name.**
  A utility can call its account statuses anything it likes, in any language; a
  count written against the English word *Active* would have read zero for
  anyone who did.
- **A bounced message is counted whichever of the three ways it is recorded**,
  and a letter still held in the building is not counted as sent — so the
  delivered percentage is struck against what actually left.

### Fixed
- **Five of the eight reports this work covered would have answered a different
  question from their own title, and now say so instead.** Account Activity,
  Data Quality, Plans & Discounts, Migration Assurance and Access Review each
  need a different kind of row from the one they were pointed at. Access Review
  is the clearest: somebody who has never signed in has never done anything, so
  reading it from the audit trail would report *never signed in: 0* over a real
  dormant login — which is the one row that report exists to find.


### Added
- **Meter readings can now be read as a report, a page at a time however large
  the utility is.** The reading, the usage, the unit it was measured in, whether
  it was actually read or estimated, and any flag it carries — sorted and paged
  by the database rather than in memory, and downloadable in full with no
  row limit. Tested on a utility holding 40,201 readings: the first page comes
  back in 0.054 seconds, the last page in 0.129, and the whole file in under
  four seconds.
- **A usage ranking that cannot mix gallons with kilowatt-hours.** Ranking
  customers by how much they used now requires you to pick one service first —
  it is not a box you can leave blank — because a ranking across water and
  electricity sorts two different measurements against each other and quietly
  produces a wrong order.
- **A total that spans two units of measurement is now refused rather than
  printed.** If a set of readings holds both gallons and kilowatt-hours, the
  total shows a dash and says why instead of adding them into a number that
  means nothing.
- **A customer looking at their own usage sees only their own**, and the figures
  above the table are added up from their readings alone — so a total cannot
  quietly include a neighbour's water even when no neighbour's row is shown.

### Changed
- **Three of the six reports waiting on meter readings are refused by name, each
  with a sentence saying what it actually needs.** Read Completeness counts the
  readings that were *not* taken, which cannot be found in a list of readings
  that were; Read Import Log counts rejected rows, which never became readings
  at all; and Bill Projection is a prediction built from prices, two of whose
  lines have no reading behind them. Serving any of the three would have
  produced a full page of real-looking rows answering a different question.


## [2.369.0] — 2026-09-27

### Added
- **Two more reports can now be run: Meter Fleet and Service Order Activity.**
  Meter Fleet lists every meter a utility owns as at a date you choose — its
  type, its size, where it is fitted, when it went in, how old it is, when it
  was last read and what state it is in — with counts of how many are in
  service, how many are spare and how many are due for a change. Service Order
  Activity lists the field jobs raised in a period with who they went to, when
  they were finished and how long they took, beside counts of raised, completed
  and still open. Both come back a page at a time however large the utility is,
  and both download in full.
- **A spare meter now shows a dash rather than a blank.** A meter sitting in the
  store room has no address and no reading, and that is a fact rather than a gap
  — the two now look different on the screen, because a blank reads as *we do
  not know* and a dash reads as *this does not apply*.
- **A list of rate schedules and their versions**, with the date each took
  effect, the date it stopped, its base charge and who moved it — read at the
  exact precision a rate is stored at, so nothing is rounded on the way out.

### Fixed
- **A report's counts no longer assume nobody ever cancels a job.** *Open* is now
  counted directly instead of being worked out as *raised minus completed*,
  which is wrong by exactly the number of jobs called off.

### Not done, on purpose
- **Disconnect & Reconnect is still not built, and its columns are still not
  agreed.** The design draws it as one line per account showing where that
  account is in the cut-and-restore sequence, and the data it would be built on
  holds one line per field job — an account cut and put back on in the same
  month has two jobs, so it would appear twice and its arrears would be counted
  twice in the total. It needs a different source, and its column set has never
  been signed off.
- **Rate Change History is still not built.** The design draws one line per price
  that moved, and one version of a schedule can move many prices at once — four
  tier prices changing on one date is four lines drawn and one line available,
  with one price column and no way to say which of the four it holds. Building
  it from what exists would show a precise number that answers nobody's question.


## [2.368.0] — 2026-09-27

### Added
- **Group a report and get real group rows with subtotals.** Choose up to three
  levels — a year, a quarter, a month, a day, or a service — and the report comes
  back as those groups, each with its own count and its own totals. The subtotals
  add up to the figure in the footer, because both are worked out by the database
  over the whole report rather than over the page you are looking at.
- **Open a group and get exactly the rows behind it.** Each group carries the
  filters that reproduce it, so the 294 lines behind a July subtotal are the same
  294 lines that subtotal was struck over. Where a group cannot be reopened —
  journal lines with no service on them — it says so instead of offering a door
  that leads nowhere.
- **Thirteen more reports can now run at all.** Two report engines were finished
  this week and neither was switched on. Trend Pack, Cash Reconciliation and
  Payment Exceptions now produce rows. The other ten say, in a sentence, why the
  engine behind them is the wrong one for that report — for example, the Debtor
  List asks who owes money and the payments engine only knows who has paid.

### Fixed
- **Group subtotals that covered one page while the total covered the whole
  report.** The billing register grouped by status showed subtotals adding to
  $14,185.80 under a total of $30,750.07, with nothing on the screen saying the
  groups covered 50 of 92 bills. Grouping is now worked out by the database over
  the whole report; where a report cannot do that yet, the grouping is dropped
  and the reason is given, rather than a subtotal that means half of what it says.
- **A report that said it was grouped and was not.** Choosing a grouping was
  accepted and echoed back on every report while no query ever acted on it —
  measured at twenty groupings across five reports, every one returning exactly
  the ungrouped rows. A report now only says it is grouped when it is.

### Known gaps
- Grouping by premises, consumer class, route or area is not offered yet on the
  two engines switched on here. Only the levels the database can cut are offered;
  the rest are named as unavailable rather than added up in the wrong place.
- The Ledger report still runs on the ledger's own engine and is unchanged. The
  report engine cannot serve it: it has no way to be told which account you mean,
  so it would show every account's lines under one account's heading.
- No screen changed here. The group rows are served; drawing them is the reports
  screen's own work.


## [2.367.0] — 2026-09-27

### Added
- **A subtotal now opens the rows that make it** (`P2.18`). Group a report and
  each subtotal carries a link; clicking *Commercial · 11 rows · $6,382.87*
  opens 11 rows totalling $6,382.87, with the group's filter applied and the
  grouping dropped. Walked in the running product at 1280 and 1440.
- **A machine can read a named list of reports** (`P2.20`, BI tier 1). An
  administrator issues a named, revocable token; granted two reports it reads
  those two and nothing else. It appears in *Started by* under its own name.
  Tenant isolation applies to it unchanged — proved on PostgreSQL with two
  utilities under a database role the isolation rules genuinely apply to.
- **The edit panel's column list, split into Attributes and Measures**, each
  measure carrying its own aggregation (`P2.21`). ⚠ **Not yet on any screen:**
  its screen is `P5.3`, the report builder, which is not built. The test that
  goes red the day it lands is in the same commit.

### Fixed
- **A drill-through built on a group row's `path` would have opened the WHOLE
  report** (`DEF-REP-6869`). The path carries the display label on the display
  column; the filter takes a code on a different name, and the runner drops a
  parameter it does not recognise without saying so. Measured: replaying a path
  returned 30 rows for a group of 11 and for a group of 19 alike. The server now
  emits each group's reproducing filters, derived from the dataset declaration.

### Changed
- **Two of `P0.7`'s six hand-typed maps are deleted** — the 23-card catalogue
  tuple, which nothing had read since `P1.1`, and the front end's four-row URL
  segment table, over a catalogue of 46. ⚠ **Four remain and the count is now
  asserted**, each with its reason: one is another lane's file, two are blocked
  on `DEF-REP-6870`, and one is a per-report list that `P2.17` replaces.

### Known
- **44 of 71 dataset dimensions offer a subtotal that cannot be opened**
  (`DEF-REP-6871`). Those rows draw NO drill-through rather than one that opens
  the wrong rows.
- **Revenue Analysis serves seven columns its declared dataset declares none of**
  (`DEF-REP-6870`), which is what blocks the rest of `P0.7`.
## [2.366.0] — 2026-09-27

### Added
- **A utility can write its own report.** Open one of the forty-five reports we
  ship, change which columns it shows, and save it under a name of your own. It
  appears on a new **Custom** list beside the standard one, it runs at its own
  address, and a colleague can open it once you share it.
- **The builder is a panel beside the live table, not a step-by-step wizard.**
  Every change re-runs the report underneath, so you can see what you are making
  while you make it — switch a column off and it leaves the rows; switch it back
  on and it returns. Nothing is saved until you press **Save as**.
- **Columns can be reordered and renamed** without anyone touching code:
  *Account* can become *Account No* and move to the left.
- **New reports are private until you share them.** A report you save is yours;
  a colleague sees it only once you choose *Everyone here*. A half-finished
  report appearing on somebody else's screen is how people stop saving.
- **`+ Build your own`** now appears on the reports page. It was deliberately
  absent for four releases, because a button that opens nothing is worse than no
  button at all.

### Fixed
- **A report named *History* no longer breaks the History tab.** Four words —
  *custom*, *dashboard*, *scheduled* and *history* — are refused as report
  names, because a report's name sits in the same part of the web address as a
  tab's. A utility that used one would have broken their own tab, invisibly.
- **A report that adds up a balance across months is refused when you save it**,
  naming the figure it cannot add. Three months of receivables of $41,220.00,
  $44,118.50 and $48,221.14 do not total $133,559.64 — that is a number nobody
  owes. The refusal existed and only fired if you happened to name a grouping
  the way the engine does rather than the way the screen does (`DEF-REP-6862`).
- **A report you saved can now be opened, and is titled by its name** rather
  than by the slug in its address (`DEF-REP-6867`).
- **A report you saved is no longer shown to colleagues as unavailable.** It was
  listed, dimmed, with *"This report cannot be produced yet."* over a report
  that ran perfectly (`DEF-REP-6866`).
- **A colleague could see a report you had kept private.** Nothing ever read the
  setting (`DEF-REP-6864`).
- **A refused save now says why.** Naming a report something the product cannot
  accept used to leave the dialog open with no message at all (`DEF-REP-6865`),
  and the Save button refused a group it had filled in itself (`DEF-REP-6863`).


## [2.364.0] — 2026-09-27

### Added
- **A Scheduled tab on Reports.** Set a report to run on its own — daily,
  weekly, monthly, or monthly on cycle close — and it arrives without anybody
  remembering to run it. The tab lists what goes out and to whom, with the next
  date, and you can pause a schedule, restart it, or run one now.
- **Schedule a report from the report you are looking at.** One dialog, three
  fields: how often, the file format, and who gets it. The report and its
  filters come from the screen you are already on.
- **Reports go to your own staff only.** The people picker offers this
  utility's users and refuses anything else. Sending outside the utility is a
  later release, with a step that asks first.

### Changed
- A schedule that runs the same report twice at the same moment now produces
  one file rather than two.
- A schedule whose report stops working stays on the list, marked failing, so
  somebody can see it. It is not silently dropped.

### Known gaps
- The Reports dashboard tab is not built yet, so `/reports/dashboard` still
  says it arrives in a later release.
- A schedule opened on its own page, tenant-configurable retention, and
  delivery of the file by email are not built.


## [2.363.1] — 2026-09-27

### Changed
- **The three bespoke report pages were NOT retired, and there is now a test
  that says when they can be.** The account ledger, the by-premises summary and
  the customer statement all still open at the addresses Finance links to and
  clerks bookmark. Retiring them would have replaced three working screens with
  three refusals: the two definitions meant to replace them cannot produce a
  row — the Ledger reads a data source with no query written, and the Statement
  is declined by its data source because a statement needs the payments as well
  as the bills. The day either can answer, the suite goes red and names the page
  to delete and the links to move with it.

### Fixed
- Nothing. Five defects were found and filed rather than fixed, because each
  belongs to a different piece of work and widening a task quietly is how scope
  stops being reviewable.

### Notes
- The Account ledger's Account box asks for "the account identifier, as the
  accounts list shows it" and refuses exactly that, answering *"Something went
  wrong on our side."* Only the internal database id works, which our own rules
  say must never be a visible value (`DEF-REP-6851`).
- Grouping a report by area is accepted, checked, and echoed back — and changes
  not one row. Measured over four reports and three groupings: 12 of 12 return
  rows byte-identical to the ungrouped run (`DEF-REP-6855`).
- `screenIds.test.tsx` has been failing unread; the router mounts 174 routes and
  the screen-id map covers 153 (`DEF-REP-6852`).

## [2.363.0] — 2026-09-27

### Added
- **A History tab on Reports.** Everything this utility has run, newest first —
  the report, when it ran, who ran it (or *Schedule*), the parameters it used,
  how it went, how many rows it made, and the file. Search it, narrow it by
  report or by status, and turn the page.
- **A run opens.** Click a row and you see its parameters exactly as they were
  set, its status, when its file expires, and a *Download CSV* button.
- **Re-run.** A finished run can be run again with its original parameters,
  untouched. It makes a NEW run and leaves the old one and its file alone — the
  two figures may differ, because the data moved, and that is the point of
  keeping both.

### Fixed
- **The export message pointed at a screen that did not exist.** Exporting any
  report said *"Your CSV is being written. It appears in Jobs when it is
  ready."* — and there was no Jobs screen anywhere in the product: no page, no
  menu word, nothing. It now says *"Find it on History."*, and History is a tab
  that opens, in all eleven languages.
- **A file that has been cleaned up no longer offers a download.** Files are
  kept for three days; the run stays in the list for ever. A run whose file has
  gone now reads *Expired* and shows a dash where the download used to be,
  instead of a button that would have returned nothing.

## [2.362.1] — 2026-09-27

### Added
- **The payments data can now be read a page at a time, and downloaded whole.**
  A report over payments asks the database for the fifty rows it is showing
  instead of fetching everything and throwing most of it away. A download still
  contains every row, and there is no limit on it.
- **Payments can be grouped four ways — by method, by teller, by purpose and by
  day.** The design asked for all four and only grouping by method existed.
  Money taken over a wire, and money banked before tills existed, say so rather
  than naming a teller who does not exist.

### Fixed
- **Deposits were about to go missing from payment reports.** The payments data
  was described as one row per *payment against a bill*, and a deposit is not
  against a bill. On a 40,000-payment utility that is one payment in five, so a
  day's takings would have read low with nothing looking wrong.

### Known
- **Today's Payments report still reads every payment one at a time.** On a
  40,000-payment utility it takes over a minute, which is longer than a web page
  is given. The faster read is built and measured; switching the report over to
  it is a separate change.
- **Eight of the ten reports listed against the payments data are still not
  available**, and each now says what it actually needs. Most of them are not
  reports about payments — Deposit Batches is about a batch, Cash Reconciliation
  is about a bank statement line, Deposits is about the security deposit held on
  an account.

## [2.362.0] — 2026-09-27

### Added
- **A total the product may not lawfully add up now shows a dash and the
  reason, and never a number** — on screen and in the downloaded file. Three
  sums were wrong and nothing caught them: a balance added up across months,
  a collection speed averaged across routes, and two different units of
  measure added together. Grouped by month, the receivables report now reads
  *— Balances do not sum across time* where it used to print a confident
  figure; each month's own subtotal is still a number, because that one is
  correct. (`P2.22`, `OQ-REP-12740` for the download-format question.)
- **A report's filters now come from the data it reads rather than being
  hand-picked one report at a time.** The receivables report goes from 2
  filters to 9, and every other report on the same data gets them too, with
  nothing edited. Four are on the bar and the rest are one click away —
  thirteen filters on screen at once is a worse screen. (`P2.17`, `P2.26`.)
- **Reports can be grouped to three levels with a subtotal at each**, and a
  subtotal knows which sums it is allowed to show. (`P2.17`.)
- **A report now rolls up ONE calendar and refuses to mix two.** A billing
  cycle straddles two months, so filtering by accounting period while
  grouping by billing cycle is refused when the report is saved, naming both
  sides. (`P2.25`.)
- **The Statement and Ledger reports can be asked about an account, a
  customer, a building or a unit** — one setting, four answers. A master
  account is an ordinary account and is not a fifth choice. (`P2.14`.)
- **A report says which question it answered** — *Based on today's customer
  details*, or *Based on details at the time* where we have the history, or
  both with a count of the rows we could not date. A report that silently
  answers a different question from the one asked is worse than one that
  refuses. (`P2.19`, `P2.27`.)

### Fixed
- Three counts in the reporting model that no check compared against each
  other: the time levels a report offers now come from the calendar that
  report declares (`DEF-REP-6846`), and a filter is only offered where
  something actually honours it — 37 of 71 do, and the other 34 would have
  been controls that did nothing (`DEF-REP-6847`).

## [2.361.0] — 2026-09-26

### Added
- **Every report now says what one row is**, in four words under its title —
  *One row per account*, *One row per bill*. A report you cannot read the grain
  of is a report you cannot check.
- **A search box, a pager and a column chooser on every report.** The report
  screen was one long table with none of the three; it is now built on the same
  table the rest of the product uses, so a report of any size opens showing
  fifty rows and you can turn the page, sort it, search it and choose which
  columns you want. Your column choice is remembered per report.
- **Sorting, where the report can actually be sorted.** An arrow appears only
  on a column the database can order by. Nothing offers an arrow that quietly
  does nothing.
- **A consumer-class filter on the AR ageing.** The server has been able to
  narrow the ageing by class since the day it was written and no control was
  ever drawn for it, so nobody could reach it.
- **A one-click *Today* on every report date box**, and the utility's own time
  zone named beside the as-of date.

### Changed
- **A report no longer fetches every row to draw a screen.** It asks for the
  page it is showing. A download still contains every row — that is checked
  now, because when the billing register started paging its download silently
  inherited the screen's fifty rows.
- **A figure the product cannot work out reads *Not counted yet*** with the
  reason one click away, in the tile where the number would be.

### Fixed
- `DEF-REP-6838` — a report's table drew its rows and **not one cell**: thirty
  rows of nothing. Any list whose columns come from the server was invisible.
- `DEF-REP-6839` — the AR ageing printed `D1_30` as a column heading and as a
  tile label, on a live money report.
- `DEF-REP-6840` — three of the four reports said *"More than one currency was
  billed"* over books billed in no currency at all, and one printed
  `currency_not_derivable` on screen.
- `DEF-REP-6841` — the billing register's *Bills* tile read `15734.170000`:
  six decimal places and no currency symbol.
- `DEF-REP-6842` — the date boxes were **empty** while the head named the
  window the report had just run over.
- `DEF-REP-6843` — typing a date range the wrong way round sent two requests,
  collected two errors and replaced the report with an error panel while you
  were still typing. It now says *To must not be before From.* under the box
  and sends nothing.
- `DEF-REP-6844` — the AR ageing failed outright the first time any filter was
  applied to it.
- A page number past the end of a report drew a range that counted backwards —
  *51–45 of 45*.

## [2.359.0] — 2026-09-26

### Added
- **The billing data behind the reports can now be asked for a page, a sort, a
  search or a whole file** — and it can be asked by any report built on it,
  rather than by one report at a time. Measured on PostgreSQL 16 over **40,092
  bills and 120,732 bill lines**: a page of fifty costs **0.674 s**, and the
  **last** page (802) costs **0.673 s** — the work does not grow as a utility
  does. A whole-file download of all 40,092 rows streams in **43.98 s** without
  ever holding the file in memory.
- **A report a utility asks to be filtered by billing cycle now can be.** The
  register has only ever run on a date range, which the design calls out as the
  one report where a cycle must be a parameter.

### Known
- **Seven of the eight billing reports still cannot be produced, and now each
  says exactly why.** They were listed as though the same data would answer
  them, and it will not: Bill Run Readiness is about accounts waiting to be
  billed, Bill Adjustments and Adjustment Register are about corrections, Bill
  Print File is about print batches, Write-Offs & Late Fees is half a
  receivables report, and Statement and My Bills & Payments both need payments
  as well as bills. Each now names what it needs instead of saying only that it
  cannot be produced (`DEF-REP-6835`).
- A report filtered by consumer class is **not** narrowed by it today — the
  figure covers every class, and the report says so rather than leaving a
  filter that only looks applied (`DEF-REP-6837`).

## [2.358.0] — 2026-09-26

### Added
- **Four finance reports that could not be produced at all now open and
  run** — Trial Balance, Journal Export, Tax Remittance and Close Pack. They
  read the posted books, they can be paged through on screen and downloaded
  whole, and each one says which date it is counting money by.
- **Journal Export is new.** It lists every posted journal line in the period
  with its account, its reference and its debit or credit, alongside the
  batches already sent to the accounting system.
- **The Trial Balance now states whether the books balance**, with the
  difference beside it. If that figure is anything but zero the posting service
  has a fault; the report says so and never quietly adjusts it.
- **An account range and a Detail / Summary switch on the Trial Balance.**
  Summary groups the same figures by account type. With a range set the report
  stops claiming the books balance, because a range only shows part of each
  entry — the difference is still shown, it just is not evidence about the
  books any more.

### Changed
- Long journal lists are fetched a page at a time from the server instead of
  all at once. A download still contains every row and always will.

### Known
- **Six of the ten reports on this dataset still cannot be produced**:
  Revenue Analysis reads the bills rather than the books (`DEF-REP-6831`),
  Regulatory Filing and External Reconciliation need facts this product does
  not hold yet, Trend Pack needs a revenue target no utility has set, the
  Ledger already opens from the sidebar, and the Operational Dashboard is a tab
  rather than a card by design.

### Documented
- **[REP-REGISTER] The 46 report drawings on brief p49-p73 are in the repo instead of only in a PDF.**
  `04-docs/05-modules/12-reports/02-business-rules.md` gains the R1-R46 section: one row per report
  with its group, sub-group, dataset, date basis, **the drawn column list in the drawn order**, and
  its warning **verbatim**. **53 warnings classified - 34 LAW, 13 TEST, 6 DEFECT, 0 OPEN.**
  No open question was minted and that is the finding: every warning either restates signed law,
  is checkable, contradicts the product, or was ours to decide (law 13). One candidate was caught
  by law 13 - `OQ-620(a)` already ruled *"a tariff rate shows four decimals"* on 2026-08-27.

### Measured
- **[REP-REGISTER] `10-scripts/rep_r1r46_drawn.py --report`** - the drawn column sets as data,
  measured against the datasets their definitions name: **48 of 51 drawings differ**, and
  **16 share no column at all** with their dataset because their rows are aggregates. Widest:
  R1 Payments 5 to 19. **Nothing is seeded** - the column sets stay unratified per `BR-REP-021`.
  All 46 definitions resolve to the declared nine datasets.

### Added
- **[REP-REGISTER] Two guards, both proved RED first through pytest**
  (`06-backend/tests/test_rep_r1r46_drawn_register.py`): the drawn register stays in step with
  the seed **in both directions**, and **R17's footer publishes no cross-service quantity total**
  (hard rule 3 - *"gallons plus kilowatt-hours is not a number"*).

### Filed
- `DEF-REP-6824` R5 draws Cycle as a parameter; the query runs on a date range only.
- `DEF-REP-6825` R1 draws a Group-by with four values; the query groups by method only.
- `DEF-REP-6826` the brief's R10 warning quotes the `/outstandings` justification **withdrawn** 2026-09-23.
- `DEF-REP-6827` **a fifth** unpaginated read - `/reports/by-premises` - outside `DEF-PAY-4221`'s four.
- `DEF-REP-6828` R17 is drawn with a USAGE column and the built query serves no usage at all.
- `DEF-REP-6829` R37's warning displays percentages at six; `BR-RAT-087` ruled two on 2026-08-20.

## [2.357.2] — 2026-09-26

### Fixed
- **A customer is now billed for the services they bought, not for everything
  their building is connected for.** A clerk has been able to say *this account
  takes three of these six services* since yesterday; the bill had not learned,
  and charged for all six. On a test utility one account's September bill was
  **$475.68 with water, sewer and trash on it that the customer never took**;
  it is now **$282.29** and those three services are nowhere on the document.

- **Sewer cannot be bought without water.** Sewer costs 90% of the water a

## [2.357.1] — 2026-09-26

- **The Reports page now lists every report this product knows about — 45 cards
  in 6 groups instead of 23 in 3** — and the list comes out of the database, so

- **A search box and two filters on that page.** Typing a name finds it, and a
  utility can narrow the list to one group or one of its own services. All
  three are worked out on the server, so the page stays quick as the list

- The **By-premises summary** report is no longer listed on the Reports page.

## [2.357.0] — 2026-09-26

### Changed
- A billing register of 38,412 bills opens on a page of fifty instead of loading
  the whole year. Measured on PostgreSQL 16 over a 39,981-row register: a page
  is **0.211 s** where reading the whole book was **3.416 s**, and the last page
  costs the same as the first. The register now sorts and searches on the
  server, so a clerk finds one bill instead of scrolling. The account ledger
  pages the same way and keeps its running balance correct on every page.

### Removed
- **No export is refused for being large any more.** The 100,000-row ceiling is
  gone — a utility with 57,000 accounts bills about 685,000 times a year and
  could not download its own year. Nothing counts the rows before writing the
  file either, so an export is built once instead of twice.
- The message a clerk saw when an export was too big, in all eleven languages.
  There is nothing left for it to describe.

## [2.352.3] — 2026-09-25

### Fixed

- **The check that guards our frozen billing figures is running again.** It had
  been reporting over a thousand errors, and none of them were about money: it
  was starting the wrong Python — one without the web framework installed — so
  every test file failed to load before a single figure was checked. It now

## [2.352.2] — 2026-09-25

### Fixed

- **Our own checks can now see a style that renders as nothing.** A class name
  that compiles to no rule at all leaves a panel with no border and no
  background — exactly what happened to the move-out refusal panel fixed in
  2.352.1. Every check we had passed over it: the type checker, the tests and
  all of the merge gates. The one check that can spot it needs the front-end
  toolchain and had not been part of a merge since early September. It is part
  of one again, and where the toolchain is missing it now says out loud how
  many files it did not look at instead of staying quiet.
- **Five merge checks that were red because the product got better.** Each had
  recorded a backlog — over-long descriptions, unexplained absences, a parked
  gap, a count of screens a person cannot reach — and each had been asking, in
  its own failure text, to be told the backlog had shrunk. The counts now match
  what the product actually holds. **No product behaviour changed and no
  screen, rule or figure was touched.**


## [2.352.1] — 2026-09-25

### Fixed

- **Move-out — the panel that refuses to close a master account is red again.**
  When an account still has open tenants, or empty units that still bill, the
  screen says so in a panel meant to carry a red left border and a pale red
  background. Since 24 September it had been drawing with **no border colour
  and no background at all**: the two colours it asked for are not colours this
  product declares, so the browser drew nothing. It now uses the same red every
  other warning panel uses. Only the colour changed — the words, the figures
  and the behaviour are exactly as they were.

## [2.352.0] — 2026-09-25

### Fixed

- **A service on the plan that the property is not connected for no longer
  stops the whole bill.** Where an account's plan priced a service the property
  has no connection for — a fire line most often — the bill would not price at
  all, and the clerk was told a size was missing. That service is now charged
  **$0.00** on its own line reading *"(not connected)"*, and the account goes to
  the Check screen for someone to look at. No other charge moved: all 75
  accounts on a test utility priced identically, to the cent. Some of those
  bills still do not appear, for two separate reasons already being worked.


## [2.351.103] — 2026-09-25

### Fixed

- **Move-outs list — the row action is an icon, not a button.** Every row
  carried a full-size bordered **↗ Open**. It is now the same row-action icon
  the Disconnects list uses, from the shared component, with *Open the
  move-out* as its tooltip and its name for a screen reader. A draft row shows
  the pair it always had, **Resume** and **Discard**, now both as icons.
- **Move-outs list — the Settlement column stops explaining itself.** It
  printed *"No settlement yet — the final bill is not readable"* on every row.
  Where there is no settlement the cell is an em dash, which is what the
  blueprint draws. The reason is still there on hover.
- **Move-outs list — the Step column no longer shows empty grey dashes.** A
  move-out with no recorded step said so in words AND drew an empty progress
  bar above them. The bar is drawn only where there is a step to show. The
  Move-ins list is fixed by the same change.
- **Move-outs list — the first tile no longer says "Open" over rows that say
  "Completed".** The figure has not changed and nothing was recounted: it is
  move-outs that have closed and have not been finally billed yet. The tile is
  called **Awaiting final bill** and the small print under it is gone, because
  the title now says what the number is.
- **Move-out wizard, step 2 — the meters section no longer touches the Reason
  field.** The heading *Meters on this unit* sat flush against the select above
  it and read as a caption on that field. Every section on the step is now
  separated by the same 24px the rest of the product uses.


## [2.351.102] — 2026-09-25

### Changed

- **Cutting service at an address is four steps instead of five.**
  **Choose · Check · Schedule · Confirm.** The old steps 4 and 5 were the same
  screen twice — the fees, the deposit and the consequences appeared on both —
  so they are one screen now. Nothing was dropped: the ladder check moved onto
  step 2, where it belongs, and every fact appears once instead of on every
  step.
- **A protection now warns you and lets you carry on.** A medical certificate,
  a weather moratorium or a payment plan used to stop the whole job. The screen
  shows what is in force and you decide. It asks you for nothing first — no
  typed reason, no tick box, no supervisor.
- **A missing proof of service warns instead of refusing.** The screen still
  asks for it.
- **The protections list is yours to keep.** Six checks arrive on the step and
  four more can be added. Each one can be marked **Recorded**, **Checked** or
  **Not required**, and nothing on the list is compulsory. What you type in
  *What happened* is kept on the case instead of being thrown away.
- **Continue tells you what is missing.** Pressing it with no cut date used to
  do nothing at all. It now says *Set the scheduled cut date* and stays where
  it is.
- **The steps along the top are no longer buttons.** They never did anything
  when pressed. Back and Continue are how you move.
- **A master account says so.** Cutting a building shows one line naming how
  many occupying accounts are affected, splits what the owner owes from what
  was passed up from the units, and asks who has to be told.
- **The disconnection and reconnection fees say where the price came from**, and
  the panel names the account's plan and category.

### Fixed

- **The step you are on is visible again, on every wizard in the product.** The
  number in the circle was white on near-white and the step you were standing
  on looked the same as the ones ahead of it.
- **The account you picked is shown by its number, not by an internal id.**
  Arriving at the disconnect wizard from an account showed a long internal
  reference in the search box.
- **The restrictor option is gone from the treatment list.** It was offered and
  could never be used, with a paragraph underneath explaining why.
- **The reconnection figure no longer subtracts a deposit that does not move.**
  Applying a deposit against what is owed is recorded as a decision; no money
  moves, so the figure you are shown is what the customer actually has to
  clear.

### Known limits

- Scheduling a cut over a protection, with no proof of service, or reconnecting
  before the balance is clear are all **allowed by the screens and still
  refused by the server.** The rules changed on 2026-09-25 and the server has
  not caught up.
- A master account's occupant count, its occupants' protections and the debt
  passed up from its units are **not yet shown** — the screen says so rather
  than showing a zero.
- Nothing raises the work order for the crew visit yet; the button says so.



## [2.351.99] — 2026-09-25

### Fixed

- **Accounts → Disconnects: the Case # column held a paragraph.** A row for an
  account with no case printed a 22-word explanation of why there was no
  reference, making the row **277px tall** against a normal row's 80. It shows
  an em dash.

- **The Actions column was off the edge of the screen.** Ten columns came to
  1453px inside a window that does not scroll sideways, so the eye — the only
  row action on the list — was cut off: slightly at 1440 and by **173px at
  1280**, where it could not be reached at all. `Last notice` comes off the
  default columns and stays one click away in the column picker.

- **A row could say it was in two states at once.** A held account read *At
  notice* and *On hold · Medical certificate* in the same column. One word
  now, with the reason underneath it.

- **The `On hold` filter could never find anything.** It asked the case record
  for a state that is never written there; a hold is held on the account. It
  returns the rows it names. Every state filter now carries its count, so a
  view that is genuinely empty says so before it is opened.

- **Two rows in six offered no way in.** The eye was greyed on accounts that
  are on the list for a protection and have no case. It opens the account.

- **A crew that went out and could not cut left no trace on the list.** A
  locked gate or a refused entry sends the case back to *Notified* and clears
  the cut date, which read exactly like a case nobody had visited. The row now
  says so — *Visited · Locked gate · 24 Sep* — beside the state.

### Changed

- **The Disconnects list is redrawn.** The four quick-view chips above the
  filter panel are gone: they offered the same things the panel offers, so one
  filter list remains. The state words are the ones a clerk uses — **Notified ·
  Scheduled · Off · Paid · Restored · Held** — on the five tiles and in the
  table alike, in all eleven languages. The same words now appear on the
  disconnect case record, which read the same vocabulary.


## [2.351.83] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **The Export screen said "Close September" at the top.** Close & export is
  two screens now, and the heading had not caught up — it named the other one,
  over the export filter, the preview and the hand-over history. It reads
  **Export** over *Closed through September.*


## [2.351.81] — 2026-09-24

### Added

- **Finance → Close & export is now two screens, and the second one is new.**
  A strip at the top of the tab switches between **Close** and **Export**.
  Close is the screen that was there; Export is the new one, and it is where
  the month is handed to the accountant.
- **Pick any two dates.** The export screen takes a start date and an end date
  instead of only offering the month that is open. The server always accepted
  any two dates; the screen never asked for them.
- **One filter where there used to be three buttons.** A **Group by** chooser
  offers Account, Service, Premises and Tax authority, and the table below it
  changes to match. The three separate extracts that no screen ever offered are
  those last three.
- **Choose the columns, and the file has exactly those columns, in that
  order.** The ▦ control on the preview shows, hides and reorders columns, and
  the ↓ download carries whatever is on screen.
- **The download hands back a real file.** Pressing ↓ produces a spreadsheet of
  the table as shown, for whatever dates are set, and records nothing — it is a
  copy, not a hand-over.
- **The four things that must be true before a month can be sent are on
  screen**: the months are closed, it has not been sent before, it balances,
  and every account has a code in your accounting package. Each one that is not
  true says what to do about it.

### Changed

- **Sending and downloading are now clearly two different acts.** Download is
  the table as shown and is not recorded. Send hands the range over once, in
  the accounting format, and is written down — so a QuickBooks file cannot be
  taken twice and imported twice.
- **Send now hands over the dates that are on screen**, not the open month.

### Known

- **There is no PDF of the export table.** The download offers a spreadsheet
  only. Nothing in this deployment can produce a PDF yet.
- **Send is only for the Account grouping.** The other three groupings download
  and do not hand over; the screen says so beside the button.


## [2.351.78] — 2026-09-24

### Added

- **You can now act on a line of a deposit batch.** The list of payments in a
  batch is where a wrong cheque number is usually spotted, and until now there
  was nothing you could do about it there. Each line now carries three
  controls: open the payment, correct its reference, and — behind the `…` —
  reverse it. Correcting a reference works even after the money is banked; only
  the method is fixed at that point, because deposits are grouped by till and
  method.
- **A batch that no longer adds up says so.** If a cheque inside a reconciled
  batch is returned, the batch keeps the total it was signed off with — that is
  correct, because the bank statement it was agreed against did not change — but
  until now nothing told you the money behind it had gone. A new *Live payments*
  figure sits beside *We recorded* and states the gap, for example *Since the
  cut −$501.33*, and the line that came back is marked on the table.
- **A difference can now be explained in more than one way at a time.** A card
  day short by $172.50 is often a $147.50 processor fee **and** a $25.00
  chargeback — two different reasons going to two different accounts. The
  explain form now takes as many lines as the difference has causes, with
  *+ Add explanation*, and shows a running *Residual* as you type. *Resolve and
  reconcile* stays switched off, saying why, until that residual reaches $0.00.

### Fixed

- **Every money column on the deposit-batch screen was left-aligned** and should
  have been right-aligned, so figures could not be scanned down the column. It
  had been that way since the table's styling was rewritten in August.


## [2.351.77] — 2026-09-24

### Added

- **Every download in Finance now works.** Six controls that had shown a small
  greyed-out arrow — the trial balance, the tax remittance report, the export
  preview, the deposit slip, the by-premises summary and the account ledger —
  produce a real spreadsheet of exactly what is on the screen. The customer
  statement does too. Each file names the period and the basis it was prepared
  on in its own filename, so two files of the same month cannot be confused.
- **The deposit slip a bookkeeper has been promised.** The Deposits & Bank
  screen's download now produces the list of deposits under whatever filters

### Fixed

- **The account ledger report has never worked, and now does.** Typing an
  account and a date range always answered *"The finance figures could not be

  the screen and the server used two different words for the same thing. Every
  run since that screen shipped was affected.
- **Four sentences explaining why a download could not be used are gone**,
  because the downloads work. They said things like *"Downloads are not built
  yet"* and *"No deposit slip to download."*

### Known

- **The account box on the account ledger asks for the wrong thing.** It says
  *"the account identifier, as the accounts list shows it"* — and the accounts
  list shows a number like `AC-2026-00001`, while the report wants the
  account's internal reference. Typing the number produces an error page rather

## [2.351.76] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **The refund screen said *cheque* where the rest of the product says
  *check*.** The head of a refund read *"No cheque written yet"* directly above
  a chip reading *"Check"*, and the queue it opens from says *"Check not written
  yet"* — one feature, two spellings, on the screen an approver reads before
  giving money back. The two English words are corrected; the ten other
  languages were always right in their own (`DEF-LED-6624`).

## [2.351.75] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **The Finance screens showed `$0.00` on a database that was full, and now
  there is a way to fill the month they actually show.** Every Finance figure is
  for *the month you are in*, and there is no way on the screen to look at
  another one. The demo utility's bills were written for June and July, so from
  1 September everything that counts this month was correctly zero — on 92
  bills, 115 payments and 229 journal entries. Nothing was broken and nothing
  went red, because the data really is there. A new command puts money into
  whichever month is open when it runs: payments taken across the month, a few
  customers who paid too much and asked for the difference back, and three
  write-offs. It goes through the same buttons a clerk would press, the books
  still balance to the penny afterwards, and running it twice changes nothing.
- **It cannot be pointed at the shared demo by accident.** It refuses to start
  without being told which database to write to, and refuses the shared one by
  name. That matters because money rows can never be deleted once written — a
  screenshot seeded twelve refunds into the shared demo earlier the same day and
  they are there for good.

### Added

- **A walk that photographs all thirteen Finance screens and says what is on
  each one** — how many rows, how many figures, and how many of them are not
  zero — so a screen that is still empty says so with a number beside it instead
  of being quietly filed as finished.

## [2.351.74] — 2026-09-24

### Changed

- **The month-end close screen says which month you are closing and what is
  left of it.** It was headed *Finance*, with a panel of seven facts you could
  not act on, no amounts, and no way from a row to the screen that finishes it.
  It now reads **Close September** over *September is open. 3 things left.*, and
  the work is two numbered steps: finish the month, then close it. Every
  unfinished row carries a link to the screen that clears it — *Post accruals*,
  *Open taxes*, *Open bank rec* — and the button at the end reads **Close
  September ✓**.
- **Each row on that list now says what it is worth.** *Accruals posted ○* did
  not tell you whether it stood for five minutes of work or a day. The figures
  were already being calculated to decide done against not done and then thrown
  away; they now reach the row. A row that is done shows nothing rather than
  `$0.00`, because a zero beside a tick reads as a measurement somebody took.

### Fixed

- **A row on the month-end list read `unpaid_cost_accrual`** — a name from
  inside the code — on every close screen since 2 September. It now reads
  *Supplier costs accrued*, in all eleven languages, and a new check goes red
  the day a further item is added without its words.
- **The partner ledger feed stops handing out internal identifiers.** Every row
  it sends now carries its journal-entry number, the printed number of the bill
  or payment behind it, and — on a tax row — which authority levied it. A
  partner asking *which entry is this?* can now be answered; this morning they
  could not be.

### Added

- **A hand-over to the accounting package can now be answered.** We recorded
  what we sent and when, and nothing came back — so *did QuickBooks take July?*
  had no answer anywhere in the product. A clerk can now record what the
  accountant told them against the batch: **accepted**, **rejected**, or
  **partial**, which is the one that actually happens when a package refuses
  two lines and takes the other thirty. A batch nobody has answered for shows
  no status at all rather than a guess, and an answer can be corrected — the
  trail keeps both.
- **A supplier's invoice can be stored against the purchase it settles.** The
  file store this needs has existed since CR-049 and the work was two names and
  one migration rather than the spike it was sized as. **Nothing is uploaded
  yet:** whether a supplier's PDF must be kept for seven years like the rest of
  the financial records is a question with the Product Owner, and the product
  will not store the first one until it is answered.

### Known gaps

- The sending machinery still sits under the close on one page; moving it to its
  own **Export** view is separate work in the same phase.
- The hand-over's answer has no control on a screen yet, for the same reason:
  it belongs on that Export view.
- *Bank reconciliation up to date* still reads *nobody can tell*, because the
  part of the product that would know publishes no count.
- A correction made in October against a September bill lands in October, so a
  partner who already collected September never sees it. Three ways to fix that
  are written down and none has been chosen.

## [2.351.72] — 2026-09-24

### Added

- **The four month-end entries the product already works out can now be posted
  from a screen.** Unbilled revenue, unpaid supplier costs, depreciation and the
  bad-debt allowance have all been calculated correctly for weeks, and there was
  no way to post any of them without a command line. Finance → General ledger →
  **Accruals** now lists them with what each one is worth, shows the lines behind
  any of them before you commit, and posts them one at a time or all four
  together. Pressing it twice is safe: a month that has already been posted
  reports that it was, and posts nothing again.
- **Which entries cancel themselves, and which do not, is on the screen.**
  Unbilled revenue and unpaid costs reverse on the first day of your next
  period; depreciation and the bad-debt allowance stand and say **Never**. Those
  two words are the difference between a plant value that is right and one that
  goes back to its purchase price every month.
- **A month closed by mistake can be reopened from Close & export.** Every closed
  month now carries a reopen control. It asks for a reason, keeps it with the
  reopen and records who did it, and it tells you first when the month has
  already been handed over to your accounting package — reopening does not
  recall a hand-over, and the difference has to be posted by hand. Only a System
  Admin may reopen; a Billing Clerk sees why not, on the control.
- **An approver can see whose money they are giving back.** Opening a refund from
  the Revenue & AR queue now shows the account and the premises it belongs to,
  how much credit that account holds, which payments built that credit, and what
  has happened to the refund so far. Until today the approval screen apologised
  for not being able to name the account.
- **The whole GL map is saved on one screen.** Which account each service's usage
  and base charges land in is now set on Finance → General ledger → **Chart**,
  beside the roles it already showed, instead of sending you to Settings →
  Services for half of it. The screen reports how many services actually changed
  rather than how many were sent.

### Known

- **The refund screen does not say whether the customer owes money on another of
  their accounts.** A refund cannot be raised at all while they do, so the
  situation is rare — but nothing in the product answers that question about a
  refund that already exists, and the screen says nothing rather than saying
  *None* about something it has not checked.
- **The refund history does not name who did each step.** The product records it,
  and there is no way yet to turn the stored identifier into a person's name for
  this screen, so the column is left out rather than filled with a code.
- **Four roles on the GL map still show their internal code** rather than a name
  — `accrued_expenses`, `accumulated_depreciation`, `allowance_doubtful_accounts`
  and `cash_over_short`. They resolve to the right accounts; only the label is
  wrong. Filed as `DEF-LED-6612`.


## [2.351.71] — 2026-09-24

### Added

- **Closing a month now produces a file you can hand to your accountant.**
  Until today the hand-over was only *recorded*: the product knew July had gone
  to QuickBooks, and nothing was ever written down that a person could open or
  email. Every recorded hand-over now downloads as a real file in the format it
  was sent to — a plain spreadsheet, a QuickBooks Desktop file, a QuickBooks
  Online sheet or a Xero sheet. Downloading the same hand-over twice gives
  exactly the same file, and changing an account's QuickBooks reference
  afterwards does not alter a file that has already gone.
- **Seven Finance reports can now be downloaded.** The trial balance, tax
  remittance by authority, the account ledger, the by-premises summary, the
  customer statement, the export preview and revenue by service each produce a
  spreadsheet of exactly what is on the screen. Each file names the period and
  the basis it was prepared on in its own filename, so two files of the same
  month cannot be confused.

### Known

- **The QuickBooks Online and Xero files have not yet been tried against those
  products.** They follow each company's published import template, and nobody
  has watched either one accept a file we produced. The plain spreadsheet and
  the QuickBooks Desktop file are not affected. Any of the four can be opened
  in a spreadsheet and checked before importing.
- **The QuickBooks, Xero and QuickBooks Desktop files carry the journal side of
  a hand-over and not the cost-of-service lines**, because an accounting import
  has to balance and those lines deliberately sit outside the balance. The
  number of lines left out is stated with every download. The plain spreadsheet
  carries everything, each line labelled with the section it came from.

  Services, Aging, Tie-out, Write-offs and Refunds sit in a strip under the
