## [2.351.68] — 2026-09-24

### Added

- **A download now carries the columns you chose to see, in the order you put
  them in.** Before today every downloaded file held that list's standard set
  of columns, whatever you had shown or hidden on screen, and in the order the
  product happened to define them. Hide four columns and the file still had
  them; move a column to the front and the file still had it fourth. The
  product now sends your choice with the request and the file holds exactly the

## [2.351.70] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **Finance → Deposits & Bank now searches, filters and pages like every other
  list in the product.** It used to ask for every deposit batch the utility has
  ever banked in order to draw the first few, with no search box, no column
  chooser and no page footer. Measured on a real database before the change: a
  book of 60 batches cost **316 database statements** and one of 300 cost
  **1,516** — the work grew with the register. After: **18 statements at 60 and
  18 at 20,000.** The four figures above the table still describe everything you
  have narrowed to, not just the page you are looking at, so *In transit* does
  not shrink as you turn the pages.
- **You can find a deposit by its batch code, the bank's own reference, or a
  cheque number off the slip in your hand.** The search reaches the server, so
  it looks through the whole register rather than the rows already on screen. It
  asks for two characters before it starts.
- **The deposit status buttons and the new tender filter come from the server.**
  They used to be a list typed into the screen, which meant a new deposit state
  would have been filterable and completely invisible. The same is now true of
  the refund states and the two refund methods.
- **The refund approval queue no longer asks for every refund ever raised.** It
  reads one page and states the true number waiting beside the heading — so a
  page can no longer hide what is pending, which is the objection the old
  unbounded read existed to answer.
- **Importing a bank statement is a proper two-step flow.** It was two headings
  on one long page: the second half appeared underneath once the file was sent,
  and there was no way back. It now has a numbered rail, you can step back to
  correct the account or the dates without losing the file you uploaded, and the
  upload itself shows *Working…* and cannot be double-sent.

  which identifier to ask for and shows none — so the heading and its
  instruction now arrive together with the boxes they describe, and leave with
  them. The same block is used by the move-in request and by new connect.

## [2.351.66] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **When a closing bill cannot be priced, the move-out said so in a paragraph of
  sixty-three words. It now says it in ten.** On step 3 of closing an account,
  where the draft bill is shown, a clerk was reading things like *"service
  electric: base charge code BASE-E prices per connection size and states no
  amount for size None. An unpriced size is REFUSED and never substituted (PO
  ruling 2026-08-28) — charging this connection another size's rate is not
  charging it for the connection it has. Price that size on the charge code, or
  record the connection's size. The run continues for every other account."* On
  the utility we are walking, thirty of the seventy-four open accounts showed
  one of these. They now read **"This connection's size is not recorded. Record
  the connection's size."** — what is wrong, and what to do about it.

  Eight of these messages were rewritten, covering every way a base charge can
  stop a bill. None of them any longer quotes a rule number, a defect number, a
  screen number or the date something was decided; none of them explains why the
  rule is the rule. All of that is still written down — it moved into the code
  beside each message and into the defect register, where an engineer can follow
  it. **One thing was genuinely dropped rather than moved:** where an account's
  customer type is covered by no charge, the message used to list the types that
  *are* covered. It now names the type and the service and sends the clerk to
  Charge codes, where that list is on screen.

  **Two smaller things in the same messages.** One printed a figure the way it
  is stored — `48.000000` — where money is shown to two decimals everywhere else
  in the product; it now reads `48.00`. Another printed the word `None` where a
  connection's size should have been, because one message was trying to cover
  two different problems at once; those are now two messages, each saying the
  one true thing.

  **And every step of the move-out no longer ends with** *"Closing an account is
  recorded in the audit log by the server, with who, when, and everything that
  changed."* Nineteen words telling a clerk how the product works rather than
  anything about the account in front of them. It is deleted, not shortened.
  Closing an account is still recorded exactly as it always was.

  The same messages are what the bill run's exception list shows, so that screen
  gets shorter too — it is one sentence from one place, which is why it was
  fixed there rather than on each screen.

## [2.351.65] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **The transfer's second step takes the buyer's details again.** A clerk
  selling a property saw a search box, a *Search customer* button and the red
  line *"Search for the buyer first."* — and no way past it to type somebody
  who is not already a customer. Every field was still there in the code; the
  step simply would not show them until a search had been run and come back
  empty. The name, the person-or-company choice, the identifiers, the date of
  birth, the email, the telephone number, the co-applicant, the mailing
  address and the Documents panel are all on the step from the moment it
  opens.
- **Searching is now a convenience beside the form rather than a toll gate.**
  A clerk with a brand-new buyer fills the form in and carries on. A clerk who
  finds an existing customer presses *Link*, and **the form fills in and stays
  editable** — so a telephone number that has gone out of date is corrected at
  the counter instead of being discovered by a returned bill, and the
  corrected value is the one that is saved. *Search again* lets go of the
  customer without throwing away what has been typed.
- **The *Create customer* button is gone**, because the form it used to reveal
  is now always on screen.
- The account's **category and sub-category** have not moved: they belong to
  the account being sold, they are shown on step 1 and on Review, and a sale
  does not re-classify an account.

## [2.351.64] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **Our published API description told partners the partner endpoints need no
  credentials. They have always needed one.** A partner — an ERP, or the payment
  provider that posts us payments — reaches us with a key we issued them, never
  with a password or a browser session. The document we hand them works out what
  each address wants by looking at which of the ordinary sign-in methods it
  accepts; these addresses accept none of them, on purpose, so the document
  printed *no credentials required* against twenty-three of them. One of those
  twenty-three is the address a payment provider posts money to.
  **Nothing was ever open.** Every partner address was called with no key at all,
  against a real database, and every one refused the call — including the payment
  one. Only the description was wrong, and a partner's engineer reading it, or a
  client program built from it, would have built the wrong thing and been refused
  on their first call with no idea why. The description now says what these
  addresses actually want: a key, sent as a bearer token. Two further addresses —
  the payment-kiosk door and the payment gateway's callback — have the same wrong
  description for the same reason; they are recorded and will be corrected
  separately, because each proves itself a different way and needs its own
  description rather than this one.

## [2.351.63] — 2026-09-24

### Changed

- **Closing an account is four steps instead of six, and three panels the
  Product Owner asked us to remove are off the screen.** They opened the
  move-out, saw a six-step bar and all three of the things they had personally
  asked to have deleted, and said so. The stepper now reads **Find account ·
  Date & reads · Bill & deposit · Review & close**, and step 3 no longer
  carries *The five landings, one arithmetic*, *What the other three would ask
  for* or the sentence *"The subtraction has not run yet."*
- **Two steps were merged into their neighbours rather than dropped.** The
  shortfall and the final bill were always one subtraction — *Short by* is its
  bottom line, not a separate fact — so settling the money is now one screen,
  and the four ways to handle a shortfall appear on it only when the account is
  actually short. The old fifth step had nothing on it a clerk could type, so
  it sits on the review with everything else. **Nothing was removed but the two
  steps**; every fact either screen carried is still there.
- **A move-out you parked before today opens where you left it.** A draft
  parked on the old *shortfall* step now reopens on **Bill & deposit** — the
  money — rather than skipping past it to the confirm.
- **Closing a landlord's account is now refused while anyone is still there.**
  A master account says so plainly, names how many tenants are still open and
  how many empty flats still bill to it, and lists them with a way to close
  each one. Its second step shows every unit in the building and the state it
  is in.
- **The review says what the empty unit will be charged**, as one line with the
  services behind it, and lists the meters with their closing readings instead
  of describing them in three sentences.

## [2.351.62] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **A completed property sale could not be opened. Now every sale can be, in
  every state.** On the Transfers tab, the reference was plain text and there
  was no way in on any row — the Product Owner found a finished sale on Ottumwa
  Water Works and could not look at it. There is now an open control at the end
  of every row, and it works the same on a sale that has completed, one still
  part-way through and one only scheduled. It opens the sale's own page, which
  shows who sold, who bought, the date, the money at the moment of sale and what
  did not change — and which has been live and reachable by typing its address
  since 20 September. Nothing about that page changes; what was missing was the
  door to it. **The rule behind the fix, which the Product Owner stated and which
  now applies everywhere: a record can be looked at whatever state it is in.**
  Anything a clerk cannot do with it is greyed out on the record itself, with the
  reason; we never take away the way in. The only row that still cannot be opened
  is one with no reference number at all, and it says so when you hover it.

## [2.351.61] — 2026-09-24

### Added

- **The Finance screens now go red by themselves when one of their "not
  available" messages stops being true.** Six checks watch the conditions the
  remaining Finance refusals name — the four downloads that have no export yet,
  the period pack, the cost-of-service download and the account-line detail —
  and each one fails on the day the thing it is waiting for arrives, naming the
  control that is still greyed out over it. This is how the property-filter
  message went on being shown for three weeks after the filter was built.

## [2.351.60] — 2026-09-24

### Changed

- **The sidebar, the top bar and the main column now use the product's own
  spacing steps.** Fourteen hand-picked gaps and paddings in the application
  frame — the tenant block, the navigation items, the sub-menu, the collapsed
  rail, the footer menu and the padding around every screen's content — were
  values like 9px, 10px and 14px that belonged to no scale. They are on it now,
  so the frame has the same rhythm as everything inside it. Three values were
  deliberately left as they were, each for a reason recorded beside it: the
  brand lockup's size, the sub-menu's indent, and the search box's internal
  padding, which makes room for its icons.
- **The shared list control and the Finance screens moved onto the same steps**,
  which is where most of the small unevenness between Finance lists came from.
- **The "not available" figure is now part of the shared component kit** rather
  than living inside Finance, where Payments and Reports had been reaching in to
  borrow it. Nothing a user sees has changed; it is the same figure, with the
  same reason, in the same place.

## [2.351.59] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **The accounting-export format list comes from the server.** The four formats
  on the Close & export screen were written into the front end by hand, so a
  fifth one added to the product would never have appeared in the picker and
  nothing would have reported it. The screen now shows whatever formats the
  product actually supports.

## [2.351.58] — 2026-09-24

### Changed

- **Five places in Finance stopped blaming a service that is running.** The
  trial-balance download, the remittance report, the period pack, the three
  report downloads and the cost-of-service reconciliation each told a clerk
  that something was *"not running on this deployment"* or that *"nothing on
  this deployment writes a report file"*. The export service **is** running —
  it already produces nine other downloads — so those sentences sent people to
  their administrator for a switch no administrator has. Each now says the
  plain thing instead: that report has no download yet. **None of the buttons
  changed**; they were correctly unavailable before and they are correctly
  unavailable now. Only the reason was wrong. And one of them, on Cost of
  service, said a decision *"has not been ruled"* that was in fact ruled on
  3 September; it now names the smaller thing that genuinely is still open.

## [2.351.57] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **A planning document said we had no way to attach a file to anything. We have
  had one for weeks, and it is on screen in three places.** The Finance
  blueprint sizes "attach a document to a purchase" as a piece of exploratory
  research, on the grounds that the product has no general attachment store at
  all, and that storage, tenant-scoped access, size and type limits, virus
  handling and retention would all have to be invented for it. The Product Owner
  said we had already built this, and they are right. Four of those five already
  exist and are tested: files are kept in locked cloud storage for seven years,
  one utility can never see another's file, anything over 10 MB is refused, and
  only PDF, PNG, JPG and CSV are accepted. The fifth, virus scanning, is not
  missing — the Product Owner asked twice for it to be removed and it was.
  **Nothing in the product changes today.** What changes is the size of the job:
  attaching a supplier's invoice is an ordinary task — point the file picker
  that is already on three screens at a purchase — and not a piece of research.
  The one real question left is how long that particular file should be kept,
  and that is still open for the Product Owner to answer.

## [2.351.56] — 2026-09-24

### Added

- **A finance officer can type a month-end of journal entries into one screen
  and post them together.** Each row is one entry — a date, a type, a memo, the
  account debited, the account credited and one amount — and the screen adds it
  to a list you can edit or remove before anything is committed. Pressing
  **Post all** posts every entry in one go, and if any of them is not ready the
  whole batch is refused and **nothing is posted at all**; the refusal names
  which entry and why, before anything is attempted. Entries can also be saved
  as drafts and come back to later. This replaces the pop-up that could only
  take one entry at a time and left nothing to return to.

## [2.351.55] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **Filtering the trial balance to one property no longer says the books are
  broken.** Picking a property made the screen announce *"The books do not add
  up"* and mark the period **Unbalanced** — the strongest warning this screen
  has, on books that were perfectly fine. A balance narrowed to one property is
  not meant to add up, because balancing is a property of a whole journal entry
  and one property only ever holds part of one. The screen now says nothing
  either way in that case, which is the honest answer: the totals are still
  shown, but no verdict is drawn about them. (`DEF-LED-6524`)

## [2.351.54] — 2026-09-24

### Changed

- **Closing a month is now a signed rule rather than our best guess at one, and
  the month-close screen has one fewer line of small print.** The product has
  always let a System Admin or a Billing Clerk close a month, and let only a
  System Admin reopen one. Until today nobody had actually asked the Product
  Owner whether that was right — it had been read across from a different
  decision about correcting a posted entry — so the close screen carried a note
  saying as much, which came out as "The books will not state this. The reason
  has no wording yet." The Product Owner has now ruled: **a clerk closes the
  month, and only an admin can unwind one, with a reason.** Nobody's permissions
  change. The note is gone from the screen.
- **Three neighbouring jobs still carry that note, on purpose.** Posting a
  month-end accrual — depreciation, unbilled revenue, unpaid supplier bills —
  recording a tax remittance, and handing the books to an accounting package
  were never put to the Product Owner, so those stay marked as unconfirmed and
  go back on the list to ask about. Clearing them because their neighbour was
  settled is exactly what the mark exists to prevent.


## [2.351.53] — 2026-09-24

### Added

- **Finance → General ledger can now be filtered to one property.** On the
  Balance view there is a Property box: start typing an address or a premise
  number and pick one, and the trial balance is redrawn for that property
  alone. It searches as you type rather than listing every property, so it
  works the same on a utility with forty thousand of them as on one with
  thirty. (`DEF-LED-6499`)

### Fixed

- **The screen has stopped saying that filter does not exist.** A panel on the
  same screen read *"Every journal line carries its property. No report filters
  on it yet."* That stopped being true on 3 September, when the filter was
  built. The panel is removed rather than reworded — there is a working control
  there now, and nothing left to explain. (`DEF-LED-6499`)
- **Two leftover messages about unbuilt features are gone**, and one missing
  message was written. The payments bulk bar no longer carries the wording for
  *"Reapplying is not built yet"* or *"Receipts are not built yet"* — those
  buttons came off the bar, and reapplying a payment has worked since
  3 September. And on Cost of service, the note telling a clerk to record a
  purchase on the asset instead was only ever written in English, so ten of the
  eleven languages showed English there; it is now translated.

## [2.351.52] — 2026-09-24

### Added

- **The Finance tab opens on the journal, and the journal is a real list at
  last.** It used to sit as a panel below the trial balance with no search box,
  no filters, no column chooser, no page controls and no sortable headings — a
  clerk saw fifty entries and had no way to reach the fifty-first. It is now its
  own view and the one Finance opens on, with a search that matches the memo and
  the entry number, filters for type, state and source, columns a clerk can
  choose and reorder, sortable Entry no. and Date headings, and a pager over the
  whole book. **A filtered journal can be sent to a colleague as a link and
  opens the same way for them** — the search, the filters, the sort and the page
  now all travel in the address.

### Changed

- **The four sections of the General ledger tab are named in one word each** —
  Journal, Balance, Chart, Accruals. Two of them used to read "Trial balance &
  journal" and "Chart of accounts & mapping", which described two things where
  there is now one. Existing links to those sections still work.

### Fixed

- **Switching section no longer throws away what a clerk had typed.** Moving
  between the four sections replaced the whole address, so the search text, the
  filters, the sort and the page were all lost and the browser's Back button
  could not bring them back. Only the section changes now.

## [2.351.51] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **The move-out now says why it cannot work out a final bill.** The Product
  Owner asked, looking at the running product, *"why are we unable to generate
  the bill here?"* — and the answer had been sitting on the server the whole
  time. The billing engine explains exactly what is wrong and what to do about
  it, in its own words: *"service electric: base charge code BASE-E prices per
  connection size and states no amount for size None … price that size on the
  charge code, or record the connection's size"*. That sentence reached the
  screen only through a piece of code that could never run, so the panel showed
  two rows and no explanation at all. It now appears above the bill whenever the
  bill cannot be priced, and never when it can. On the demo utility, 30 of 75
  open accounts are in that state. (`DEF-CUS-6464`)

## [2.351.50] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **The journal list no longer builds every entry a utility holds in order to
  show fifty of them.** Opening Finance on a utility with a large book read
  every journal entry in the database, then threw away all but the fifty on the
  page. Measured before the fix: sixty entries cost 67 database statements and
  three hundred cost 307 — one per entry — so a utility at the top of the
  supported range was forty thousand entries' work for one screen. The database
  is now asked for one page at a time, and the cost no longer grows with the
  book: **twelve statements at sixty entries and twelve at twenty thousand.**
  Three facts the screen states — how many entries there are, whether the book
  holds more than one currency, and how many posted entries carry no number —
  are still worked out over the whole book rather than over the page, so the
  same screen cannot say two different things depending on which page a clerk
  stopped on. (`DEF-LED-6493`)

### Added

- **A finance officer can post a whole batch of journal entries in one act, and
  it posts in full or not at all.** Five month-end entries totalling $2,142.75
  now go in together. If any one of them is not ready — no memo, out of balance
  — **nothing posts at all**, and the officer is told which entry and why
  **before anything is attempted**, with every problem in one answer rather than
  one problem per attempt. A posted entry can never be removed, only reversed,
  so a batch that posted the first two and stopped would have left $1,227.50 in
  the books for good. Re-submitting a batch after fixing it does not post
  anything twice. (PO ruling, `BR-LED-798`)

- **The journal's Entry no. column sorts by the entry's date rather than by the
  number as text.** The number reads `JE-011526-0001`, which puts January 2026
  before February 2025 when sorted as text although it is eleven months later.
  Sorting by that column now orders by the date the entry was made, and a test
  pins it so it cannot quietly become a text sort later.

## [2.351.49] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **Finance now shows the whole amount a utility is owed, cents and all.** The
  headline figure on the Finance screens was being cut short — it read
  `$23,766…` where the real figure is `$23,766.56` — because the tile it sits
  in was narrower than the number. The cents were not rounded away, they were
  simply not drawn, so the amount on screen looked smaller than the amount in
  the books. The tiles are wider now and nothing is cut: `$23,766.56` reads in
  full, and so does a figure as large as `$1,234,567.89`. The same tiles are
  used on about twenty screens across the product, so every one of them gains
  this. ⚠ One visible consequence, stated rather than left to be noticed: the
  Finance strip carries six tiles today, and wider tiles mean they now sit on
  two rows instead of one. (`DEF-LED-6498`)

## [2.351.48] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **A deploy could not start, and now it can.** Yesterday's change that makes
  the database check every accounting and category reference stopped a system
  from starting up at all. One deposit rule — the figure a new customer of a
  given category is asked to pay — was pointing at a customer category that no
  longer exists, left behind when each utility got its own list of categories
  on 17 September. The new check examined it, found it broken, and refused to
  finish. The checks are now added in the form that guards everything written
  from here on **without** examining what is already there, so a system with an
  old, broken row starts normally. **Not one row of anybody's data was changed
  or deleted to achieve this.** (`DEF-RAT-6494`)

- **And the broken rule is still broken, on purpose.** We will not delete a
  deposit rule or guess which category it meant — both change what a customer
  is charged. We are asking which category it was written for, and until that
  is answered nobody should describe these eight checks as having examined the
  existing rows. (`OQ-RAT-12633`)

## [2.351.47] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **The move-out's first step no longer shows the same heading twice.** The
  account panel and the step above it both printed *"Which account is moving
  out?"*, one line apart. The panel now carries its own heading, *This account*,
  which is what the approved drawing gives it. (`DEF-CUS-6497`)

### Changed

- **The account panel is built from the shared building blocks rather than laid
  out by hand.** It now uses the same fact-row component every other detail
  screen in the product uses, so the label column, the row spacing and the type
  sizes are the product's own and not this screen's. The two-column arrangement
  the drawing shows is the only layout decision the screen still makes for
  itself. Nothing a clerk reads has changed. (`DEF-CUS-6496`)

## [2.351.46] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **A completed move-out stops telling the clerk three things that are no longer
  true.** Every move-out ended with a list of what it had not done, and three
  entries on that list had gone stale: it said billing "has no tables" and so no
  final bill could be issued, that refunding a deposit "runs through payments,
  which has no tables", and that the deposit-interest engine "is not built".
  All three of those modules shipped weeks or months ago. What is still true is
  said instead, and said shortly: a move-out works out the closing figure and
  hands it over, and billing raises the invoice on its own run; the deposit
  cannot be settled until that invoice exists. **Deposit interest is now only
  reported as missing when it really could not be worked out** — before, every
  clerk was told it had not been done, including on the accounts where it had.
  A fourth sentence, about the move-out date not being checked against issued
  bills, blamed a missing invoices table; it now says what is actually the case,
  which is that the account has no issued bill to check against. The two
  remaining entries — dunning and the close-out letters — are untouched, because

## [2.351.45] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **The move-out's meter step no longer goes blank on an owner's account.** A
  master account — the one a landlord holds for a whole building — has no unit
  of its own, and on those the meter area of step 2 showed nothing at all: no
  heading, no table, and no sentence saying why. It now says the account holds

  (`DEF-CUS-6492`)

## [2.351.44] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **The move-out's account panel shows the four things it was missing.** Step 1
  now lists the mailing address, the account type, the sub-type and whether the
  account is a regular one or a master — beside the number, the name, the
  service address, the services, the plan, the status, the opening date and the
  balance it already showed. **Every one of the four was already being sent by
  the server**; the screen simply never drew them. Where no separate mailing
  address is on file the row says *Same as service address*, which is a
  different statement from an address nobody typed, and the panel keeps the two

  unit and then to the property, so a bill and a map can never disagree about
  where a place is. (`DEF-CUS-6476`)

### Changed

- **The panel is laid out in two columns, as drawn.** It was a single list.

## [2.351.43] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **Four partner connectors could not be used for about two hours today, and
  they work again.** Utilities connected to Workday, SAP, Infor or MSGP would
  have found every one of their partner's calls turned away with *We cannot
  serve this request* — which reads, to the partner receiving it, as *your key
  is wrong*, so the first thing they would have checked is the one thing that
  was fine. It was caused by this morning's Invoice Cloud work: a list of which
  connectors may use the partner doors is worked out rather than written down,
  and the rule for working it out was corrected in a way that fitted Invoice
  Cloud and quietly excluded those four. (`DEF-INT-6490`)


## [2.351.42] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **A new Invoice Cloud key no longer arrives able to take money.** When a
  connection has no key yet, the *Generate a key* screen pre-selects every
  API the connector has — which was right when all of them were *Read*, and
  stopped being right the moment *Take a payment* existed. The first key a
  clerk issued reached it **without anybody ticking it and with nothing on the
  screen saying so.** The pre-selection is now the reading APIs only;
  taking payments is granted by ticking its own line, which is what that line
  is for. (`DEF-INT-6488`)

- **The published API document described the new payment address as a read.**
  Partners build their software from that document. It said *GET* with four
  paging parameters for an address that is a *POST* taking a payment — so a
  partner following it would have built a call we refuse, and gone looking at
  their key for a fault in our paperwork. It now says POST, lists the fields a
  payment needs, and says which of them are required. Nothing about the five
  reading addresses changes. (`DEF-INT-6489`)


## [2.351.41] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **A move-out can send somebody to read the meter again.** The move-out screen
  asked whether a field visit was needed using a panel that offered only the
  work templates a utility had published — and most utilities have published
  none, so the panel a clerk saw was usually empty. It now uses the same
  seven-column table the move-in and the transfer screens use, where a clerk
  picks a job type, a priority, a due date and a crew, adds as many rows as they
  need, or ticks *No visit needed*. **More importantly, those rows now actually
  reach the crew.** The move-out's own door was reading only the old template
  ticks, so had the new table simply been put on the screen, a clerk could have
  filled in seven columns, pressed Continue, watched the account close — and no
  work order would ever have been raised, with nothing anywhere to say so. That
  half is fixed in the same release, and *No visit needed* is now recorded as
  the answer it is rather than discarded. (`DEF-CUS-6487`)

### Changed

- **The move-out's meter step is one table, not a list beside a panel.** The
  step used to show the account's meter numbers as a plain list, and then a
  separate box underneath for typing the closing readings — the same registers
  written out twice, one copy with nowhere to type. It is now the single
  nine-column table the Product Owner approved: asset number, type, service,
  register, the last reading and when it was taken, then the closing reading,
  its date and an estimate tick. The move-out's reading box still opens with the
  register's last reading already in it, because the figure a tenant leaves is
  the one that closes the account; the move-in's still opens empty, because a
  prefilled box nobody touched would record a reading nobody took.
- **The column a clerk types into no longer says "Move-in reading" on a
  move-out.** Sharing the table handed the move-out the other flow's word, in
  the column heading and in the label a screen reader announces.

## [2.351.39] — 2026-09-24

### Added

- **Invoice Cloud can now send us a payment as it is taken, instead of us
  waiting for a file.** A customer pays their bill on Invoice Cloud's portal
  and Invoice Cloud tells us straight away, naming the account and the bill,
  their own reference for the payment, the date, the amount and how it was
  paid. The payment lands on that account against that bill, with our own
  payment number, and Invoice Cloud gets that number back so the two systems
  can talk about the same thing afterwards. **Nothing any member of staff does
  changes, and no screen moves** — this is a door for their computer, not for
  a person.

- **If the same payment arrives twice, it is taken once.** A partner whose
  connection drops mid-request will send the payment again, which is the right
  thing for them to do. The second one is recognised as the same payment, is
  answered with the number of the first, and no second payment is created.
  That matters more here than almost anywhere else in the product: a payment
  can never be edited or deleted, so a duplicate would be permanent and the
  customer would be recorded as having paid twice for good.

- **A key that can read cannot pay.** Every key we have ever issued a partner
  could only read. Taking a payment is a separate permission, shown as its own
  line on the connector's set-up screen — *Take a payment*, beside five lines
  that say *Read*. **No key that already exists has it**, and someone has to
  tick it deliberately. A key without it is turned away in exactly the same
  words, with exactly the same delay, as a key we have never seen — so nobody
  can go looking for the door by trying it.

### Changed

- **What the payment says about itself, while one question is still with
  Invoice Cloud.** The payment is recorded, and it is recorded as *not yet
  cleared* — which means it does not reduce the bill's balance, does not reach
  the books and is not included in the day's banking. That is deliberate rather
  than a gap: we have asked Invoice Cloud whether a payment they send us has
  definitely been taken from the customer or might still fail, and until they
  answer, saying the money has arrived would be a guess on a money path. Every
  reply we send them says so in as many words. When they answer, it is one line
  of code.

- **Card and bank payments only, on this route.** Cash, cheques and money
  orders are turned away with a sentence saying why. Money that passes through
  a person's hands belongs to a till that somebody counts at the end of a
  shift, and a partner has no till — so a cash payment sent this way would end
  up in the day's banking with no drawer and no count behind it. Invoice Cloud
  is a card and bank-transfer portal, so nothing real is lost.

### Fixed

- **A partner's set-up screen can show the address of a door they send things
  TO, not only the ones they read from.** The check deciding whether an address
  may be printed on that screen was asking the wrong question, and the effect
  was invisible until now: the payment kiosk's three inbound addresses have
  never been drawn, so a clerk looking at that connector sees fewer addresses
  than exist. That is the same complaint raised about Invoice Cloud's own
  screen a week ago, sitting unreported one row over. (`DEF-INT-6485`)

## [2.351.38] — 2026-09-24

### Added

- **The system now knows what a currency is.** There was no table anywhere
  saying so: **39 columns across the product hold a three-letter currency code
  as free text**, the list of allowed codes lived in one line of code in one
  place, and the symbols lived somewhere else entirely. There is a proper list
  now, with the same five currencies that were allowed before — US and Canadian
  dollars, Mexican pesos, euros and pounds — and the two places where the money
  actually matters, a utility's own setting and every journal entry, are now
  checked against it. Nothing a user can do changes. (`P0.6`)

- **Settings → Company offers the currencies instead of asking you to type
  one.** The field was a free-text box over a value the server already refused
  when it did not recognise it — so you could type `US$`, press save, and only
  then be told no, with nothing on the screen having said what the answers
  were. The list is served with the value now. (`P0.8`)

### Fixed

- **A journal entry can no longer be written in the wrong money.** Two holes,
  both silent: an entry saved without a currency quietly became US dollars, and
  an entry saved with the wrong currency was accepted outright — it balanced,
  the trial balance footed, and nothing anywhere went red. For a Canadian
  utility that is its books becoming American, one entry at a time, and a
  posted entry can never be corrected — only reversed. Both are refused now,
  and the refusal says which currency the utility keeps its books in.
  (`P0.7`)

- **A check that had never once been able to pass on the real database now
  passes.** A numbering test read a utility's settings without saying which
  utility, which the real database answers with *nothing* — so it read zero
  rows and failed, every time, since 21 September. It had looked green because
  the everyday test database has no such rule. (`DEF-LED-6484`)

## [2.351.37] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **A mistyped or stale accounting-code reference is now refused when it is
  saved, instead of turning up as a wrong figure on a report.** Thirteen
  references across four areas — the accounting code on a bill line, on an
  adjustment, on a charge, on a discount, on a plan's service and on both
  halves of a tax; the two accounting settings a System Admin maps on Settings;
  a tax-exemption certificate's account and who verified it; a plan's deposit
  rule; and the property an owner's account is anchored to. Checked first on
  the live data: **not one of the thirteen held a reference to something that
  does not exist**, so nothing had to be cleaned up before the rules went on.
  *Unmapped* is still a perfectly good answer everywhere it was before — only a
  reference to something that is not there is refused. (`P0.4` · `P0.5` ·
  `P0.12`)

  ⚠ **One behaviour change worth knowing about:** a property that an owner's
  account is anchored to, and an accounting code that something points at, can
  no longer be deleted. The attempt fails and says so, rather than quietly
  leaving an account or a bill line pointing at nothing.

## [2.351.36] — 2026-09-24

### Added

- **Every journal entry the system posts now carries the `JE-` number you asked
  for.** Before today only entries a person typed by hand got one: bills,
  payments, accruals and tax remittances all went into the books with no
  reference anybody could read aloud. On the demo utility that was **167
  entries and not one number**. The format is the one ruled on 23 September —
  an entry dated 2 August 2026 is **`JE-080226-0001`**, and the forty-third
  that day is **`JE-080226-0043`**. New utilities are set up with it; an
  existing one is moved to it only if it has never issued a number, so nobody's
  books end up holding two spellings of the same series.
  ⚠ **One consequence, stated rather than discovered:** because the month comes
  first, these numbers do not line up in date order when sorted as text —
  `JE-011526-0001` comes before `JE-020325-0001` although it is eleven months
  later. Every list therefore sorts by the entry's date, and a test now holds
  that in place. (`P0.13` · `P0.3` · `P0.10`)

- **A journal line records the customer who held the account at the time.**
  Asking *"what did this person owe us in August?"* used to be answered by
  looking up who holds the account **now** — so the day a property changed
  hands, every past line quietly moved to the new owner, with all the totals
  still adding up. The customer is now written down at the moment the money is
  posted and never worked out again. ⚠ **The 661 lines already in the books
  stay blank**, permanently: a posted line may never be edited, and the only
  thing left to look them up from is the same answer that moves. (`P0.1`)

- **An account can say which of two joint holders is billed.** Two people can
  hold one account, and nothing recorded which name goes on the bill. All
  **54** of the demo utility's accounts have a single holder, so all 54 were
  filled in automatically and nothing on screen changes. Where an account
  genuinely has two holders, neither is marked — the system will not guess a
  name onto a bill. (`P0.2`)

- **A tax line can finally name the authority the money is owed to.** Billing
  has asked Rating for this one fact by name since 11 August and nothing
  answered, so the figure was NULL on **all 661** lines in the books and the
  by-authority tax report could not be built from them. (`P0.3`)

### Fixed

- **The Finance tab had one property filter under two different names.** Narrow
  the journal to one property, open the trial balance, and you got the whole
  ledger back — correct, balanced, and about every property. Both spellings are
  accepted now and saved links keep working. (`P0.14`)

## [2.351.34] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **The Cancel button is gone from the failure panels that had nothing to
  cancel.** Every "something went wrong" panel in the product drew Retry,
  Download error report and Cancel — and on 44 of them Cancel did nothing at
  all, because there was no job to abandon: the page had simply failed to load
  and Retry was the only act. Cancel is now drawn only where a handler is
  given, and it still appears on the import and sync panels it was written for.
  (`DEF-INT-5562`)
- **The check behind "Download error report" runs again.** Its fixture used a
  refusal the product retired on 23 September, so the panel printed the message
  code where the sentence should be and the check had been failing since that
  morning. It now uses a refusal the server still raises: an account that holds
  no unit cannot be sold. (`DEF-SHL-6482`)

## [2.351.33] — 2026-09-24

### Changed

- **The move-out screen stops explaining itself.** Sixteen paragraphs came off
  the six steps of the move-out — 495 words in total, replaced by 11 — after the
  Product Owner walked the whole flow and said the same thing six times in an
  hour: *"too much text on this screen please reduce it"*. What went was the
  writing that told a clerk why the product works the way it does: a 48-word
  paragraph standing over every step, two panels on the last step running to 66
  and 59 words about what confirming does and does not do, and the notes under
  the date box and the meter list. Nothing a clerk acts on was removed, and no
  refusal was softened — every one still fires and still says so. The words are
  gone from all eleven languages, not hidden.
- **Finding an account on the move-out is one box now, not two.** A clerk used
  to type into an *Account* box and then pick from a second *Matching account*
  list — two gestures for one choice. It is now a single search-as-you-type box,
  the same control Payments and the transfer screen already use. It still tells
  a clerk apart the two things that used to look identical: *no account matches
  what you typed*, and *the search itself could not run*. An account id pasted
  in from a link still opens that account directly instead of being searched
  for.
- **The move-out no longer shows one utility's account-number format to every
  utility.** The help under the Account box quoted `AC-2026-00025` as "the
  account number as your lists show it". Account numbers are set per utility,
  and the one the Product Owner was looking at numbers its accounts `A-10650`.
  The line is gone and no example replaces it.
  (`DEF-CUS-6474`–`DEF-CUS-6481`)

## [2.351.32] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **Two more customer-portal fixtures open their accounts with the deposit the
  plan asks for.** The same rule change that stopped the connection-fee tests
  stopped forty-five more: the landlord with four accounts and the neighbour
  who is not one of them were both opened on a plan that asks a $150.00
  deposit and sent no answer. Both now record it as assessed and due on the
  first bill, so no balance moves — the four accounts still total $872.82.
  Measured across the twelve files they live in: **58 red before, 13 after**.
  (`DEF-CWP-6472`)

## [2.351.31] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **Moving a payment out of a reconciled deposit is checked on the real
  database again.** The check builds a bank deposit for a cheque, and it built
  one with no counter till behind it — which PostgreSQL has refused since 22
  September, when a deposit became one till and one tender. The default test
  database has no such rule, so the check passed there and failed on the only
  database where the guarantee exists. The deposit is now banked the way every
  deposit is: Dana opens a till at the counter and the deposit names it. The
  rule it protects is unchanged — a payment inside a deposit the bank has
  already agreed cannot be moved to another account. (`DEF-PAY-6463`)

## [2.351.30] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **The Age column on Service requests counts in the utility's own day.** From
  7 p.m. every evening until midnight UTC, every request on the list read one
  day older than it is, and the seven-day highlight came on a day early with
  it: a request filed six days ago was flagged as a week old from 7 p.m. The
  age was being worked out on the server's clock while the request was dated on
  the counter's. Both halves now use the utility's own clock — the one set on
  Settings → Company → Regional. Nothing else on the screen changes.
  (`DEF-CUS-6433`)

## [2.351.29] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **A new request's town, state and ZIP are allowed again where the check said
  they were not.** On 22 September the Product Owner ruled that a request takes
  the address in parts so a clerk can find the property; a test written under
  the week-old refusal it reversed was still forbidding those three boxes, so it
  had been failing for two days. The check now says what the ruling says — the
  three "as given" parts are a record of what the applicant said and are kept,
  and any other address column on a request is still refused by name, because
  the address itself belongs to the property. (`DEF-CUS-6458`)
- **A Billing Clerk sees the account sub-categories on New account and Move-in.**
  Recorded as fixed: the pickers already read the customers-side list rather
  than the Settings door that answers a clerk "not allowed", shipped in
  `2.350.7`; the register row was never closed. Re-proved here — the clerk's
  read answers with rows, and the fourteen screen checks pass. (`DEF-CUS-6426`)

## [2.351.28] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **A fee taken at the counter is now part of the drawer count.** When a clerk
  takes an application fee in cash, that money is in their drawer — but the
  Close screen did not expect it, so counting the drawer honestly came out
  over by the fee, and since yesterday an over is posted to the books. The one
  fee was being booked twice. The Close screen now expects it: a counter
  holding $400.00 that takes a $70.00 cash fee expects $470.00, and a clerk
  who counts $470.00 is square. Nothing in the books changed — the fee is
  still recorded once, when it is taken. A fee paid by card is not part of the
  count, because a card total cannot be counted in a drawer.
  (`DEF-PAY-6375`, `OQ-PAY-12621`, PO ruling 2026-09-24)

## [2.351.27] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **The Move-outs checklist shows the deposit money it is actually about.** The
  "Deposit money" tile read **$0.00** on every run, whatever the refunds came
  to, and always said US dollars. It was adding up the closing accounts again
  from scratch without the settlement that priced them, so every figure came
  out empty and every currency came out as the default. It now reads the
  figures the run already recorded: two refunds of $10.0050 total **$20.01**,
  and a run whose accounts are in two different currencies shows no total at
  all instead of a made-up one. (`DEF-RBS-6467`)
- **The Move-outs checklist tests run again.** Six of them had been failing
  since the checklist was written on 7 September — the test harness handed the
  run the letter "t" where a real utility was expected — so nothing had ever
  checked that an approved refund reaches the payment door, that a
  carry-forward does not wait for a second approval, or that the money on each
  row is the money the settlement decided. All thirty-four now pass, and it is
  the second of those, unmasked by the first, that found the $0.00 tile above.
  (`DEF-RBS-6457`)

## [2.351.26] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **The delivery-queue tests count the customer's portal copy as well as the
  paper one.** Since 7 September every bill has left two rows when it issues —
  one for print and one for the customer's own copy on the portal — and the
  eight cases that check the queue were still counting one per bill, so they
  had been red for seventeen days and the whole delivery path had no running
  test. They now name both rows rather than counting them: a run of two bills
  leaves four rows, two print and two portal, and a staff re-send makes a
  second copy of each. Nothing about how a bill is delivered changed.
  (`DEF-BIL-6456`)

## [2.351.25] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **The portal demo's occupied address now answers the deposit its own plan
  asks for.** The sample utility opens an account at 1408 Elm St · A on a plan
  that asks a $150.00 residential deposit, and sent no answer to the deposit
  question at all. Since the deposit rule changed on 2026-09-23 — *"No" only
  when the plan asks none* — that account is refused, so every customer-portal
  test that seeds that street stopped before it began, the eleven cases behind
  the connection-fee screen among them. The account now records the $150.00 as
  assessed and falling on the first bill: no money moves, so no balance,
  payment or ledger figure anywhere in the demo changes. (`DEF-CWP-6424`)

## [2.351.24] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **Move-in step 6 (Review): the customer's messages are shown, as the
  blueprint draws them.** (`DEF-CUS-6365`)
  - The last section of the review is now a table headed "What goes out", with
    a column for each of the six the drawing has: Send, What it says, To,
    Channel, Template, When. On the sample utility a move-in with no deposit
    shows two rows — "The new account and its number", going out on Printed
    letter and Email using the "Welcome / account opened" letter at version 1,
    and "The service agreement", which the move-in writes and which nothing
    carries, so its channel and its letter both read "—". A deposit taken at
    step 5 adds "A receipt for the deposit", and a deposit that also clears on
    the day adds "The deposit has cleared".
  - Every line in that table is read from the utility's own notification rules
    and its own published letters, using the same calls the save itself makes,
    so what a clerk is shown and what is actually queued cannot disagree. A
    utility that has switched an event off sees that row's tick empty.
  - The tick in the Send column says whether the message really will be queued.
    It cannot be clicked: a move-in does not yet take a choice about which
    messages go out.
  - Removed from this step: "What this move-in will not write" (60 words) and
    "Nothing is delivered to the customer" (57 words). Both explained why the
    product works as it does, which belongs in the code and not on a clerk's
    screen, and parts of both had become untrue — the first said a move-in
    commits no opening reading, which it has done since the reading table
    landed the day before.

## [2.351.23] — 2026-09-24

### Removed

- **An unused column on payments is gone.** Each payment row carried an empty
  field naming which processor payout had paid it out. Nothing could ever
  write it — a payment is locked the moment it is recorded, and a payout
  arrives days later — so it sat empty on every row in every utility. It has
  been removed. Nothing on screen changes: *Awaiting settlement* has always
  been answered from the payout's own list of payments, which is unchanged,
  and the rule about what may be changed on a recorded payment is exactly what
  it was. (`OQ-PAY-12608`, PO ruling 2026-09-24)

## [2.351.22] — 2026-09-24

### Changed

- **The medical-protection line on Payments is shorter.** The "What is
  missing" panel on the Payments summary and on Debtors read "Medical
  protections cannot be shown here. Notices still apply them." It now reads
  "Medical protections apply. Not shown here." The protection itself has not
  changed — notices still apply it — and nothing else on either screen moves.
  (`OQ-PAY-12612`, PO ruling 2026-09-24)

## [2.351.21] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **A billing clerk can now waive a deposit.** When the plan asks a deposit,
  the move-in and new-account steps offer *Take it* or *Waive*. Pressing
  *Waive* used to be refused for a billing clerk — *"Only a supervisor may
  waive this."* — so a clerk at the counter had to stop and find a system
  administrator. A billing clerk or a system administrator can now do it: the
  reason is still required and it is still kept on the account, so Rosa
  Alvarez's waived $150.00 reads *Waived · $150.00* with who waived it and
  why. Anyone else who tries is told *"Your role cannot waive a deposit. Ask a
  Billing Clerk."* (`OQ-CUS-12623`, PO ruling 2026-09-24; closes
  `DEF-CUS-6372`)

## [2.351.20] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **A property can be sold more than once.** Selling an account a second time
  — A-11512, sold to Aiden, Tim and then by him to Reyes, Carla — failed at the
  last step with "Something went wrong on our side." It now completes, and both
  sales stay on the Transfers list. Starting a second sale while one is still
  open is still refused, by name. Database change `customers/0069`.
  (`DEF-CUS-6431`)
- **A finished sale no longer reads like a draft.** The sale record said
  "Committed by: Not committed yet" on sales that were completed weeks ago.
  Nothing records who pressed the button, so a completed sale now says
  "Not recorded" and only an unfinished one says "Not committed yet".
  (`DEF-CUS-6429`)
- **The Transfers list names the buyer under "Sold to", not the seller.**
  TRF-26-0001 showed Hollis, Marcus — the seller — in the column headed
  "Sold to". It now shows Aiden, Tim, who bought it. A sale that has not
  committed yet still says so instead of naming anybody. (`DEF-CUS-6462`)

## [2.351.19] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **The counter takes the whole application fee, or the fee is waived.** A
  clerk could record part of a service request's application fee — $25.00 of
  a $130.00 fee — and leave the rest open. Now an amount that is not the whole
  fee still owing is refused: *"Take the full $130.00. Or waive it."* Nothing
  is recorded when it is refused. A request that was part-paid before today
  keeps what was taken, and the rest can only be waived; trying to take the
  rest now says *"Already taken on receipt RCP-26-4471."* The sample request
  for David Okonkwo now waits on the whole $130.00 instead of showing $25.00
  taken. (`DEF-CUS-6455`, PO ruling 2026-09-24)

## [2.351.12] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **"The register" is gone from the Accounts screens.** It was our internal
  name for a list, and clerks know each list by its own name. The Accounts
  page is titled *Accounts*; the back link on a move record reads *Move-ins*
  or *Move-outs* (whichever list it returns to); a disconnect record's reads

## [2.351.11] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **A service request can be corrected: Edit is on the requests list and on
  the request's own page.** A pencil beside each row's eye reads *Resume* on a
  Draft and *Edit* while the request is Submitted, Under review or More info
  needed; the request's page has an *Edit* (or *Resume*) button in its head.
  An Approved or Refused request has neither — it is decided — and opening one
  by its address says *"Approved already. It can't be edited."* instead of
  showing a form. (`DEF-CUS-6427`, `DEF-CUS-5881`)
- **Opening a saved request shows what was saved, on every step.** The New
  request wizard used to open a saved request with every box empty, and saving
  over those empty boxes erased the stored email, phone and SSN. It now loads
  the applicant, category, services and their start dates, the service and
  billing addresses, the fees and *What they said*. The SSN and driver's
  license boxes open empty and show only their last four (`••• ••• • 5236`,
  `•••••9566`); leaving them alone keeps the number on file, typing replaces it.
  (`DEF-CUS-5880`)
- **Saving sends only what changed.** Correcting one phone number changes the
  phone and nothing else, and the audit trail records that one change, before
  and after. On a request that has been submitted, the button is *Save
  changes*, it takes the clerk back to the request, and the service address
  line stays as the applicant gave it. (`DEF-CUS-6427`)

### Notes

- The server now refuses an edit, a category change or a services change on a
  request that is past approval (`approved`, `in_fulfilment`, `on_hold`) with
  `customers.serviceRequest.approvedNoEdit`; it already refused a closed one.
- `serviceRequestResumeHold.test.ts` is retired, as it instructed, in the
  commit that wired the door; `serviceRequestEdit.dom.test.tsx` guards the same
  data-loss path directly.

## [2.351.10] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **Fifteen more defects get a number of their own.** Each of fifteen numbers
  had been given to two different defects. The one filed second now has a new
  number (`DEF-6440` to `DEF-PAY-6454`), and the notes in the code that pointed

## [2.351.9] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **Download error report on a payment's page stays on that page.** When a
  payment's page failed to load, *Download error report* downloaded the report
  and then jumped to the Payments list. It now just downloads the report.
  *Cancel* still goes back to the list. (`DEF-PAY-6435`)

## [2.351.8] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **A returned letter stops the post, not the email.** The collections
  runbook treated an account whose letter came back as unreachable on every
  channel, so a customer with a working email would have been told nothing.
  Now it drops only the post: if an email is on file, the notice is planned by
  email. With nothing else on file it is still skipped. The runbook is not
  live yet, so no customer missed a notice. (`DEF-PAY-6380`)

## [2.351.7] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **Print bills sends a bill to the same address the delivery queue does.**
  A bill whose account has no mailing address was held out of the print-shop
  file as "address incomplete", while the delivery queue addressed the same
  bill to the property. The print file now uses the mailing address, or else
  the service address (the property's street, city, state and ZIP, with the
  unit on line 2), exactly as the queue does. A mailing address with a part
  missing is still held; a property with a part missing is held too, and the
  held-back list now says which one to fix. (`DEF-BIL-6373`)

## [2.351.6] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **A waived application fee says how much was waived, and why, in words.**
  After a waive the request's fee panel read "Application fee $0.00 waived.
  BILLERR". It now reads, for example, "Application fee $45.00 waived. Billing
  error correction": the amount that was waived and the reason's name from
  Settings. The fee table's "Waived — …" line shows the name too.
  (`DEF-CUS-6423`)
- **The request's fee data no longer says the money is kept out of the books.**
  Since 15 September a fee taken at the counter is posted to the ledger, but
  the request still reported that nothing was posted. It now reports it once
  the posting exists. (`DEF-CUS-6381`)

## [2.351.5] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **Payment-plan letters are kept again.** Since 19 September the document
  store refused to keep a copy of three payment-plan letters: the instalment
  reminder, the missed-instalment letter and the plan-voided notice. Their names
  were misspelled in the store's list. They are spelled correctly again, and
  nothing else in the list changes. (`DEF-TEN-6425`)
- The backend test suite now fails when a data model changes without its
  database migration.

## [2.351.4] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **The Customer step on Move-in and New account is one shared set of fields,
  and it is shorter.** Both wizards now mount the same fields, so a fix to one
  reaches the other. (`DEF-CUS-6356`..`6360`)
  - Category is a dropdown instead of seven buttons across.
  - "Sub-type" is now "Sub-category" everywhere it is shown, including the

  - Date of birth, and the move-in date on step 3, are typed and shown in the

  - Mailing address: a "Same as service address" box, checked by default.
    Unchecked, the shared US address fields appear (street, apt/unit, city,

  - The explanatory hints under the fields are removed, and the "say whether

## [2.351.3] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **The rule that a banked payment's tender cannot be corrected is proved on
  the real database again.** Four checks of it had been failing on PostgreSQL
  since 22 September, because their setup made a deposit batch with no till,
  which the database now refuses. The setup opens a till first, the way every

## [2.351.2] — 2026-09-24

  test still expected a refund raised without naming a payment to be refused.

  (`DEF-PAY-6346`)

## [2.351.1] — 2026-09-24

### Fixed

- **In the demo, card and bank-transfer payments say Digital, not Counter.**
  The Payments list's Source column read *Counter* on every sample card and ACH
  payment, although that money never passed through a counter. A freshly
  loaded demo now shows *Digital* for card and ACH and *Counter* for cash and

## [2.351.0] — 2026-09-23

### Fixed

- **Selling an account with nobody linked to it now works.** A-11512 (Hollis,
  Marcus) has no customer on file, and the sale was refused after all five
  steps. It now goes through, and the seller is kept by the name on the account.
  (`DEF-CUS-6387`)
- **Step 2 finds the buyer first.** A *Search customer* box takes a customer
  number or a name: one match shows the customer's details with *Link*, several
  show a table (Customer # · Name · Person or company · Email · Phone · Accounts
  held), and nobody offers *Create customer*. Email and phone are masked. A
  linked buyer is not asked for an ID again, and their phone and email on file
  come with them. New Connect uses the same finder. (`DEF-CUS-6386`)
- **At the sale, the seller's email, phone, mailing address and autopay are
  removed.** The buyer's are used where given; otherwise bills go to the service
  address. (`DEF-CUS-6393`)
- **Selling a premises' master account makes the buyer the property's owner.**
  A regular account leaves the owner as it was. (`DEF-CUS-6394`)
- **A co-applicant is kept.** The buyer's second person (name, email, phone) is
  stored on the account and shown — and editable — on the account page under
  *Co-applicant*. (`DEF-CUS-6391`)
- Step 1 is one searchable box for the account; *No customer linked* replaces a
  dash; the sub-category shows beside the category; base charge, billing cycle,
  current period, next bill and *Unbroken since* are real figures on steps 1 and
  3. (`DEF-CUS-6382`, `DEF-CUS-6383`, `DEF-CUS-6384`, `DEF-CUS-5182`)
- Step 2 says *Mailing address*, with *Same as service address* and the US
  address fields; it is laid out in two columns; *Give one ID or a phone.* sits
  beside the IDs; and it takes the buyer's documents, filed on the account when
  the sale completes. (`DEF-CUS-6388`, `DEF-CUS-6389`, `DEF-CUS-6390`)
- The review lists the messages the sale queues — to the buyer, to the seller,
  and a text about the visit when one is asked — each *Queued on confirm*, and
  the done page says where each was queued. Nothing claims a message was sent.
  (`DEF-CUS-5949`)
- A sale that cannot happen is refused on the step where its cause is picked —
  an account already being sold on step 1, a buyer who already holds the account
  on step 2 — not after step 5. (`DEF-CUS-6395`)
- Explanations a clerk had to read past on every step are removed.
  (`DEF-CUS-6385`)
- **The field visit on step 2 is the work-order table** the move-in uses:
  *+ Add work order* (job type, priority, due, assigned to, note) or *No visit
  needed*. The orders are raised when the sale completes, the review shows
  them, and the done page links each real order number. (`DEF-CUS-6392`)
- The review's line *"The balance and deposit are recorded as they stand"* was
  not true (the figures are kept on no record); it now reads *Balance and
  deposit move with it.* (`DEF-CUS-6430`)
- The transfer record no longer says the owner record and the contact details
  are still the seller's. (`DEF-CUS-6393`, `DEF-CUS-6394`)

### Notes

- Database change: `customers 0068` — a sale may have no seller customer, and
  keeps the seller's name. Undoing it needs any such sale dealt with first.
- Known and filed, not fixed here: selling the same account a second time
  fails (`DEF-CUS-6431`); a completed sale's record says *Not committed yet*
  under *Committed by* (`DEF-CUS-6429`).

## [2.350.7] — 2026-09-23

### Fixed

- **A billing clerk now sees the sub-categories when opening an account or a
  move-in.** The list was read from a Settings screen's data, which a billing
  clerk may not open, so the clerk saw no sub-categories at all. It is now read

## [2.350.6] — 2026-09-23

### Fixed

- **Every defect in the register has its own number again.** Six defects had
  been filed under two numbers, three each, so four of them could not be looked
  up or closed. Four rows go back to the numbers they were first given
  (`DEF-CUS-5975` to `5978`), and every note that cited them now points at the

## [2.350.5] — 2026-09-23

### Fixed

- **A move-in can raise work orders again, and shows them.** Step 3's *Field
  visit* opened with a sentence about a move-out and offered only the
  utility's published templates, so a utility with none could raise nothing.
  It is now a table: *+ Add work order* adds a row with Job type, Priority
  (the utility's *Normal* to start, or the job type's own), Due, Assigned to
  and a Note, and *No visit needed* clears it. The same rows are shown on the
  review step with *On save* as their number, and after saving each order's
  real number links to it with its live status and who it is assigned to. The
  orders are still created only when the move-in is saved. (`DEF-CUS-6363`)
- A due date picked for a work order is kept as that day in the utility's own

## [2.350.4] — 2026-09-23

### Fixed

- **A billing address is now a proper US address, and none of it is required.**
  On *New request* step 3, unticking *Same as the service address* used to give
  one free-text box. It now gives Street address · Apt, suite or unit · City ·
  State (a searchable list) · ZIP code, in the order an envelope reads. Nothing
  is required. A ZIP that was typed must be 5 digits or ZIP+4
  (`78664` or `78664-1234`). Requests captured before today keep the one line
  they were given, exactly as typed; nothing tries to split it. The same five
  fields are now one shared component that the move-in and New account screens
  can reuse, and the account door now keeps the "Apt, suite or unit" line as
  its own line. (`DEF-CUS-6408`)
- **The requested start date is kept, and shown on the review and on the
  request.** Step 2 showed the connection date in every service's box but saved
  every service with no date, so *Check & submit* and the request's Applicant
  tab both read `—` (SR-26-0016: Water, Sewer, Trash and Fire). A service the
  clerk does not change now carries the connection date — the PO's ruling of
  22 September — and a box the clerk empties still means "not given". Requests
  already submitted this way hold no per-service date and cannot be given one
  after the fact; their connection date is still shown beside them.
  (`DEF-CUS-6409`)
- **Capture another opens a blank step 1.** It used to leave the clerk on the
  confirmation of the request they had just finished. A fresh visit to
  *New request* now always starts empty, with no draft carried over, so the next
  request takes its own number. (`DEF-CUS-6410`)
- **Fees are a table on step 5, on the review, on the confirmation and on the
  request.** Fee · Charged per · Qty · Unit price · Amount, with the Total
  underneath. On step 5 you pick a fee and it becomes a row; a Waive checkbox asks
  for the reason; the ✕ removes a fee while the request is still a draft. After
  submitting, a fee is waived, never removed. The request page also shows
  *Paid*. (`DEF-CUS-6411`; the PO's approval of this layout closes `OQ-357` as
  "both")
- **"Waive the fee" is no longer a way to pay.** Picking it wrote the word
  *waive* and waived nothing, so the request still owed the whole amount.
  Waiving is now done on the fee itself, with a reason. (`DEF-CUS-6415`)
- **The fee price is set by the charge code, not by the screen.** The server
  used to store whatever price it was sent. It now prices each fee from the
  utility's own charge code at the moment it is added, and refuses a different
  figure by name. A fee already on a request keeps its price if the charge code
  changes later. (`DEF-CUS-6416`)
- **Money always shows its currency.** "0.00 collected of 70.00 quoted" now
  reads "$0.00 collected of $70.00 quoted", on the review, the confirmation and
  the request. (`DEF-CUS-6412`)
- **Words, not codes.** The confirmation's *How it was paid* reads *Cash*, not
  `cash`; the review's category reads *Residential*, not `residential`; a date
  of birth uses the utility's date format. (`DEF-CUS-6413`)
- **Less explaining on screen.** Removed: "stored encrypted" beside the last
  four digits; the 25-word sentence under *When is it being paid?* (now "Record
  the cash on the request."); "Documents gate this, not money."; and the two
  long sentences about charging on the confirmation. *What happens next* is four
  short lines. "Less was handed over. Not a waiver." now shows only when some
  money was actually handed over. (`DEF-CUS-6414`)
- **The confirmation says what happened to the acknowledgment email.** It said
  "none is waiting to be sent" on every request, although the email has been
  queued since 15 September. It now reads the request's own answer — queued, or
  why not. (`DEF-CUS-6418`)
- **Found in Premises.** Step 3's match panel was headed "What the register
  matched"; a clerk knows that list as *Premises*. Its search hint now reads
  "Search Premises. Pick the address." — one of the eight strings
  `DEF-CUS-6422` lists; the other seven are on other screens.

### Not fixed here

- Phone numbers are still shown exactly as typed, on every screen. There is no
  phone format in the product yet; it wants one rule applied everywhere at
  once, not on one screen. (`DEF-CUS-6419`)

### Notes

- New columns: `service_requests.billing_line1_as_given`, `billing_line2_as_given`,
  `billing_city_as_given`, `billing_state_as_given`, `billing_postal_code_as_given`
  (migration `customers 0067`). Nothing is backfilled.
- New route: `DELETE /service-requests/{id}/fees/{fee_id}` — a draft's fee line only.
- `POST /service-requests/{id}/fees` refuses a `unit_amount` the charge code does
  not carry (`feePriceMoved`) and a code the catalogue cannot price
  (`feeCodeNotPriced`).
- Sample data: the *Load sample data* button now also creates the charge codes
  `CC-EXPEDITE` ($45.00) and `CC-METERTEST` ($60.00) beside `CC-REQFEE`,
  because the sample request quotes them and a fee is now priced from the
  catalogue; without them the sample's $130.00 quote would have shrunk to
  $25.00. Neither is given a ledger account.
- The server no longer lists `fee_line_cannot_be_removed` or
  `acknowledgement_cannot_be_queued` among a request's unavailable things.

## [2.350.3] — 2026-09-23

### Fixed

- **An expired session now says so, instead of saying you lack permission.**
  When a session ran out, the next screen opened — Payments, and 77 others —
  said *"You don't have access to this. Your role can't open Payments. Ask a
  System Admin if you need it."*, even to a System Admin. It now shows one
  card in place of the whole screen: **Session expired** · *Sign in again to
  continue.* · **Sign in →**. The button opens this utility's own sign-in page
  and, after signing in, returns to the page you were on (a filtered Payments
  list comes back filtered). Anything the tab was holding is cleared before
  the card appears. A person whose role really cannot open a screen still sees
  *You don't have access to this.*, exactly as before. (`DEF-SHL-6378`)
- The same card replaces the shell's *"We couldn't load your regional
  settings"* with a Retry that could never work, when a page is reopened after
  the session has ended. (`DEF-SHL-6378`)

### Notes

- The sign-in page now accepts the page to return to. It only follows a page
  inside the same utility; anything else — another website, another utility's
  address — is ignored and the Dashboard is used, as before.
- A form half-filled when the session ends is lost, except Move-in, which keeps
  a draft as you type: signing in again reopens it from the last saved draft.
  Other wizards keep a draft only if *Park* was pressed.
- Rollback: revert the commit. Nothing stored changes.

## [2.350.2] — 2026-09-23

### Fixed

- **Download error report now downloads a report, on every screen.** When
  something fails, the red panel offers *Retry*, *Download error report* and
  *Cancel*. The middle button did nothing on 99 of the 101 screens that show
  the panel. It now saves a small text file named after the screen and the
  time, for example `TRF-02-error-20260923-1555.txt`. The file says which
  screen, the page, the time in your utility's time zone, the version, the two
  sentences the panel showed, and which request was refused with its code and
  a support reference. (`DEF-SHL-6377`)

### Notes

- The file leaves out anything typed into the form, the details of the
  request, search terms in the address, record numbers and links in
  addresses, cookies and passwords. It says so at the top.
- On a payment's page that could not load, the button still also takes you
  back to the payments list afterwards, as it did before.

## [2.350.1] — 2026-09-23

### Fixed

- **A move-in now works on a unit nobody has lived in.** Picking a vacant unit
  with no earlier tenancy on *Accounts → Move-ins → New* showed a red strip
  telling the clerk to open a new account instead. The unit is now named as the
