  explanation in 224 notes, in a panel just over 14,000 pixels tall**, and the table
  is a table again.
  - **Whether an account can be deleted has not changed at all.** An account in use
    still cannot be deleted; the Delete button is still greyed out, and it still
    tells you why when you point at it — including what is holding the account, such
    as journal lines. That sentence used to be printed twice: once on the button and
    once again underneath every row. Only the second copy is gone.
  - **"Proposed" is now a status, in the Status column**, next to Active or Retired,
    instead of a sentence stuck to the account's name. One short line at the foot of
    the list says what it means.
  - **Account 5700 showed `depreciation_expense`** in the *Role in the books* column
    where every other account shows a phrase. It now reads *Plant value used up*, in
    all eleven languages.

## [2.327.2] — 2026-09-22

### Fixed

- **The upgrade to 2.327.0 would not install, and on some databases it would
  have installed silently wrong.** The release added a column recording where
  each payment came from — a clerk's entry, a bank feed, or an import — and
  filled it in for payments already on file. Two things were wrong with that
  step. On the live database it was **refused outright**, because a payment
  that has cleared is financial history and nothing may change on it; the
  upgrade stopped with an error naming payment `PY-260808-0001` and the release
  could not be installed at all. On databases where it was not refused it did
  something worse: it **quietly filled in nothing** and reported success, so
  every payment already on file would have been left with no origin while
  everything reported the upgrade as done.
- **Both are fixed, and the upgrade now refuses to claim success over work it
  did not do.** The fill-in step runs once for each utility on the database, so
  it can see the payments; the freeze that protects cleared money is lifted only
  for that one step and is put straight back before the upgrade finishes; and
  the upgrade now counts the payments it left without an origin and stops with
  that number if any remain. Checked on a copy of a real database holding 74
  cleared payments: 0 of 74 were filled in before, 74 of 74 after, and cleared
  money is still refused every other kind of change.

## [2.327.1] — 2026-09-22

### Fixed

- **A rate schedule's tier ladder lines up again, and the sentence under it is
  said once.** Typing blocks of usage on *Plans & Rates → a rate schedule →
  step 3* — whether the structure is *Tiered* or *Percent of another service*
  on the usage basis — the **To** box sat 43 pixels higher than **From**,
  **Rate** and **Remove tier**, so the four controls in a row no longer read as
  a row. The reason was the help line underneath it: it made that one box
  taller, and it was printed under **every** block — three blocks printed it
  three times, six printed it six — while saying *"on the last row"*, which was
  only true of the bottom one. It is now written once, under the last block,
  and the four controls sit on one line. Measured in a browser: a 45-pixel
  spread before, 1 pixel after.
- **The sentence is shorter, and it says the same thing.** *"Leave blank on the
  last row for no upper limit."* is now *"Leave the last To blank. That block
  has no upper limit."* — two short sentences instead of one long one, in all
  eleven languages.
- **`+ Add tier` looks like a button again.** It was being stretched to the full
  width of its panel — 1,088 pixels against 102 for *Continue* — so the bottom
  of the ladder read as an empty input box. It now takes its own width, which is
  what the blueprint draws.

## [2.327.0] — 2026-09-22

### Added
- **New World / Logos reads our receipts** (`CR-132-BRC07`). `GET /api/partner/v1/receipts` serves
  the online payments a utility took as Tyler New World's four-level Receipt file — header,
  transaction, GL distributions, payment node. A sixth named ERP connector, `erp_newworld`, one
  manifest file and no screen code. **`GET /api/partner/v1/ledger` is reused unchanged**; the GL
  accounts come from the same seam Aclarian's ledger rows resolve through, so a GL rule still
  changes in one place.
- **A payment records where it came from** (`payments/0029`). `payments.origin` — `entry` ·
  `webhook` · `import` — written once at creation and never updated, indexed, and readable instead
  of being a prefix inside an idempotency key that is NULL on every payment recorded without a
  reference. Existing rows are backfilled from the key prefix and marked `origin_is_derived`,
  because a derived value is not an observed fact. The New World feed carries `webhook` only.
- **`G130`** — the four New World credit-card fields are not built and cannot be added by accident.

### Note
- An unbalanced receipt is **sent, flagged and counted**, never refused and never plugged (PO
  ruling). Measured on the real path: **7 receipts, 7 balanced, largest difference $0.00.**

## [2.326.0] — 2026-09-22

### Changed

- **A route now reports the readings that were collected on it.** Ask a route what
  was read on it and the answer used to be *"the readings on the meters that are on
  it today"* — so the moment a property moved to another route, a hundred readings
  left the old route's list, its progress count and its last-read date, and the new
  route picked them up as if its reader had taken them. The reading itself never
  moved; only the screens did. They now answer with the route the reader was
  actually standing on. The route column on the readings list moved with the filter,
  so the two cannot disagree.
  ⚠ **One thing to expect on an older utility:** a reading taken before we started
  recording which route collected it has no route at all, so it will not appear when
  you filter by route, and its Route column is blank. On the demo data that is none
  of the 516 readings; on a utility that has been running since before this was
  recorded it will be some of the oldest ones.

- **A route now remembers which PROPERTIES are on it and works out the units, meters
  and accounts every time you ask.** It used to store a list of units, taken at the
  moment somebody last pressed Save — a photograph. Add a unit, fit a meter or move a
  tenant in, and none of it reached the route until somebody re-opened the wizard.
  Now it does, immediately, with nobody re-opening anything.

### Fixed

- **Building a route across large properties works.** Six properties holding 726 units
  left step 3 of the route wizard showing *"No meters yet"* and step 4 sitting on
  *"Working…"* for ever with no error. The screen was sending the address of every
  single unit to the server — about 38,000 characters, far past what a server will
  accept — and the save was writing 726 rows one at a time. It now sends the six
  properties and saves six rows.

- **When the meter list cannot be loaded, the wizard says so.** It used to draw
  *"No meters yet"* over a request that had failed, so a property with no meters and
  a broken connection looked identical. There is now a message and a Try again button.

## [2.325.1] — 2026-09-22

### Fixed

- **The Owner box on a property now searches the accounts you actually have.** On the
  add form, on the edit form and on a property's own page, it searched a list of
  *owner records* — and nothing anywhere in the product could put anything into that
  list. All three boxes worked perfectly and found nothing, every time, for everybody.
  They search master accounts now: type a name or an account number and the account
  appears. Adding a landlord's twelfth address finds the account the first eleven used.
- **Adding a property is one press again, and it tells you what it did.** The property
  saved and the owner's account quietly did not open, and the screen said *"Premise
  created"* over the top of it. **Nothing was broken and nothing said so** — which is
  why it was so hard to describe. Now the same one press creates the address, links the
  account, and says which: *"Owner's account linked"*, or the reason it could not, in
  plain words.
- **One word for one thing.** The same fact was called *Owner*, *Owner (record)*,
  *Owner / manager* and *master account* on four different screens. It is **Owner**
  everywhere now, with the account number beside it. The box underneath is for the
  managing agent and says **Managed by**, because that is a different thing.
- **The dead instruction is gone.** The edit form said *"Not listed? Type the name
  below"* under a list that could never list anybody, and typing the name below created
  nothing. There is a search that finds accounts and no instruction that leads nowhere.

## [2.325.0] — 2026-09-22

### Added

- **The screen for saying which share you mean.** `2.323.0` taught the engine that a
  service billed as a share of another can be a share of its **charge** or of what it
  **used**; this is the card a clerk picks that on, with the rate beside it. Sewer at
  90% of the water used, priced at $5.00 a thousand gallons, is four fields and one
  press.
- **A block ladder for the share that follows a meter.** One price to start with; press
  *Add tier* and the blocks appear. A share of a **charge** is offered no rate at all —
  a percentage of money needs no price per gallon, and there is nothing there to type a
  wrong number into.
- **The unit a rate is priced in is now the one the utility said it uses.** Open a sewer
  schedule at a water utility and the unit picker opens on **kgal**, because that is
  what Settings says sewer is measured in. It offered eight units before, all of them
  choosable and none chosen. The other seven are still on the list, greyed, each saying
  why — so nobody has to wonder whether a unit is missing or just wrong here.

### Fixed

- **A share-of-another-service rate could not be saved at all.** Since 8 September the
  screen sent no rate and the server had required one, so the last button always failed
  and there was no box to put the rate in. It saves.
- **Five sentences that described the old arithmetic are gone**, in all eleven
  languages, along with three refusals that were reaching a clerk as a line of computer
  code instead of a sentence.
- **A schedule could be set to a percentage of itself.** The list of services to take a
  share of no longer offers the one being priced, and it is built from what the utility
  has switched on — so a utility that starts selling something new can price a share of
  it with nothing changed here.

## [2.324.1] — 2026-09-22

### Fixed

- **A clerk who cannot save a chart-of-accounts change is now told why, where they are
  looking.** Adding and editing an account were forms at the very bottom of the page — on
  a utility with 129 accounts that is about seventeen screenfuls down — while the one line
  that reported a refusal sat at the very top. So pressing *Save* on a change the product
  could not accept appeared to do nothing at all. Both forms are dialogs now, the reason
  appears inside the dialog next to the button that failed, and where the reason belongs
  to one box — the number is already used, the role is already held — it is printed on
  that box.
- **Adding an account is one press.** *+ Add account* sits at the top of the list beside
  its heading instead of being reached by scrolling past every account the utility has.
- **The refusals themselves are shorter and say what to do next.** *"You already have an
  account numbered 1200."* is now *"That number is already used. Use a different one."*
  One of them had also been printing an internal code where a clerk expected a name.
- **The note explaining that an account's number and type are fixed** moved into the edit
  dialog, beside the two fields it is about.

## [2.324.0] — 2026-09-22

### Fixed

- **Adding a property now opens the owner's account, which is what the form has been asking
  for all along.** A clerk who filled the form in completely — the owner's name, *person* or
  *company*, one identifier, and an account type — got the property saved and **no account
  opened**, with no explanation anywhere on screen. The reason was that the code wanted an
  *owner record* first and gave up before it ever looked at what had just been typed — and
  **no screen in this product can create an owner record**, so that could never be satisfied.
  Measured on a copy of the live data before the fix: **0 of 79 properties** had an owner
  account. That matters because the charge for an empty unit and a move-out shortfall are both
  billed to the owner, and there was nobody at any address to bill them to.
- **A property can be pointed at an account that already exists**, on the add form and on the
  edit form both — *"we are unable to find and map master account to premises later"*. An
  account that is not an owner's account is refused and says so.
- **Every outcome now reaches the screen.** The server has worked out five different answers
  for a while — the owner has no identifier yet, the identifier is the wrong kind for the kind
  chosen, no account type was picked, and so on — and **none of them was ever drawn anywhere**.
  Each now carries its own sentence, in all eleven languages.
- **Where a property is already recorded against an owner, nothing moves.** Older properties
  keep answering through the record they have; nothing is back-filled and no existing link is
  taken away.

## [2.323.0] — 2026-09-22

### Added

- **A utility that bills one service as a share of another can now say which share it
  means.** Sewer billed as a percentage of water can be a percentage of the water
  **charge** — water charge $100.00 at 80% bills **$80.00** — or a percentage of the water
  **used** — 100 gallons at 80% bills **80 gallons**, priced at the utility's own sewer
  rate. Until now only the second existed, and the screen described the first, which is
  what made it look missing.
- **That second kind can be priced in blocks, not just at one rate.** The same 80 gallons
  through a first 30 at $1.00, a next 30 at $2.00 and the rest at $3.00 bills **$150.00**
  across three lines, and each line says it came from 80% of the water.
- **The list of services a share can be taken of comes from what the utility has switched
  on**, not from a list built into the product. A utility that starts selling an eleventh
  service can price a share of it without anything being changed here.

### Fixed

- **A schedule priced in blocks would have charged every unit at the first block's price.**
  The projection that hands a schedule to the bill run read only the first block and threw
  the rest away. Nothing could create a second block until today, so no bill was ever
  wrong; it is fixed in the same release that makes the second block possible.
- **Every rate schedule already in the system has been written down as *a share of the
  water used*, one by one and by name.** Nothing already billed changes: the reference
  sewer bill still charges **$36.00**. Read the other way it would have been **$35.55**.

## [2.322.1] — 2026-09-21

### Fixed

- **A clerk who put a new-connect build down and came back finished that build**, instead
  of starting a second one beside it. Approving an application raises the build straight
  away; parking its wizard used to forget which build it was, so the last button either
  made a duplicate on the same property — leaving the first one sitting there unfinished
  and still the one the application named — or was refused outright and the whole wizard's
  typing was lost. The row a parked wizard leaves on the New connects tab had no
  connection number on it either, so nobody could see what it belonged to. It now carries
  the build's own number, and finishing the work clears the parked row away, so one piece
  of work is one row.
- **A clerk can get back into an unfinished build at all.** Its number on the New connects
  tab went to the property page, where *Edit details* was greyed out reading *"No edit path
  exists yet."*; where the address had not matched a property the row had no link
  whatsoever, and the only way on was to type the address in by hand. The number, the eye
  on the row and *Edit details* on the property all open the build's own wizard now. A
  finished build still goes where it always did.

## [2.322.0] — 2026-09-20

**The first disconnections this product has ever completed happened today**, and every
item below was found only because a cut finally committed. Until 2026-09-20 every cut
refused on every utility, over a reconnection charge code no utility has ever had.

### Added

- **A utility can put a customer back on.** Reconnection and restore-service were built
  in August, routed, tested — and called by nothing for 26 days. They have doors now, on
  the case record, and the commit control is whichever act the case's state admits.
- **A crew that attends and does not cut can be recorded** — locked gate, access refused,
  paid at the door, disputed. The first three clear the cut date and return the case for
  re-scheduling; a dispute stops the ladder. Recording a payment at the door records no
  amount: a crew holding a cheque is not a posted payment.
- **Something reads cut dates daily.** A per-utility nightly watch reports what is due and
  what is overdue, and a **Due now** view finds them. ⛔ **It cuts nothing and writes
  nothing** — the only thing that performs a cut is still a person pressing a button.
- **A cut whose final bill was refused can be finished.** Before this, such a cut was
  stuck for ever: nothing in the product could revisit it. **Finish disconnection** raises
  the bill and writes the status, and still refuses to write it if the days cannot be
  billed.
- **The New Connect build record**, as sections on the property's Build tab — the drawn
  header, five tiles, the blocking banner and four sections, fed by one read.

### Fixed

- **A household was quoted one whole reconnection fee too much.** The figure a customer
  must clear read **$8,390.00** where the signed figure is **$8,315.00**, because the fee
  was added to a balance that already held it the moment the cut issued it. Both readers —
  the record panel and the reconnection gate — now read the position once.
- **The customer's own arrears screen added the same fee twice** — `$75.00` owed plus a
  `$75.00` fee shown as `$150.00`, over one bill.
- **A cut case could be un-cut, and cut again, raising a second fee.** The commit path
  refused a second cut by name; the schedule path wrote the state back with no such check.
  Both now read one fact, and so does the screen.
- **A cut was about to bill five and a half years another system had already billed.** With
  no bill of ours to work from, the window fell back to the date the account opened. It
  double-billed nobody only because the engine refused for an unrelated reason. The window
  now prefers the cutover date.
- **A `$75.00` fee counted as having billed a day of service**, which would have marked an
  account disconnected across five years on the strength of that fee.
- **The register said two households were due to cut when their supply was already off**,
  and its own list showed none of them. A tile is a door: it is counted by the predicate of
  the list it opens.
- **Two of the five cut reasons could never commit.** Tampering and abandoned premises sent
  spellings the server refuses — proved against the running server, 422 then 200.
- **The cut dialog promised a status the server had deliberately held.** It reads the
  server's own answer now.
- **Raw server codes reached a clerk** on the wizard's review and three of the register's
  filters. A code with no label now refuses visibly instead of printing itself.
- **The wizard's "Case reference" showed the word `service`** — the ladder's sequence where
  the case number belongs.
- **New Connect step 4 offered eleven services to a utility that sells two.** Nine of the
  tick boxes offered services the commit refuses by name, after all eight steps.
- **A picked address lost the services it offers**, so a clerk's ticks were a local fiction.
- **A build made through the wizard could never raise a charge**, because pricing required
  an application. A build prices itself now.
- **Meters were recorded as installed on the day a build was committed.** A build generates
  an asset number; it does not fit anything.
- **Step 8 said *energise*** where the ruling is *activate*.
- **A committed build recorded nothing about the services it provides.** Its own record
  read *0 units, 0 of 0 activated, 0 of 0 service points* over a build that had just made
  eight units, sixteen meters and a **$315.00** bill. The units, the plans and the meters
  were all real; what was never written was *which service this build provides at which
  unit*, and every one of those figures counts exactly that. A build committed today reads
  its true figures.
- **The only *Add service* control could add one service, and it was always water.** It
  now offers the services this utility sells and the unit to attach one to, so a utility
  selling three can add three.
- **Picking a charge the product itself offered destroyed the whole build.** Step 6 listed
  every one of a utility's charge codes, and six of them carry no price at all. Choose one
  — *New service tap fee*, say — and the last button answered *"Something went wrong on our
  side."* **Thirty-three clicks gone and nothing saved.** The list now offers only charges
  that can be billed, and a charge that stops being billable after it was picked is refused
  **on the Charges step**, in words, with every answer still on the screen.
- **Adding units to an address that already has those unit numbers did the same.** A second
  `Apt 101` at a building that already has one cannot exist, and the clerk met that as the
  same raw error, after eight steps. The Units step now says **"Apt 101 already exists
  here."** before anything is typed, and marks every row it applies to. If it is only found
  at the last button, the message lands **on the Units step** and the build is still there.


## [2.317.1] — 2026-09-20

### Fixed

- **The Approve dialog now says which outcomes this request can actually
  become.** All five were offered the same way on every request, so a clerk
  could pick *A move-out* for somebody who holds no account to close. Each
  choice now carries the answer the system already had: a choice this request
  cannot be is **greyed, with the reason beside it** — *"No live account at
  this address."* — and the one the evidence fits is marked **Suggested**.
- **Nothing was taken off the list, and that was asked about directly.** A
  move-out is refused for THIS applicant because they hold no account here; for
  somebody actually moving out it is the option they need. An option that is
  not on screen cannot be chosen, so hiding them would leave those requests
  with nothing to file them as. They are shown, and shown as unavailable.
- **The reason is words on the screen, not a tooltip.** Someone on a phone or
  using a keyboard never sees a tooltip, and the whole point of greying a
  choice is that the reason gets read.
- **A disconnect is unchanged.** It stays available on every request, exactly
  as before. Whether a disconnect should ever be greyed is still an open
  question with no answer from the Product Owner, and this change does not
  invent one.

## [2.317.0] — 2026-09-20

### Changed

- **A landlord with tenants still on supply can be moved out again — the clerk
  is warned instead of refused.** Yesterday's build stopped the move-out
  outright: step 1 showed *"2 sub-accounts are still open. Close or reassign
  them first."* over a `Continue` that would not move, and the server refused
  the commit. It now shows **`2 sub-accounts are still open.`** as an amber
  warning, `Continue` works, and the close goes through and carries the same
  fact back on its answer. The tenants beneath are untouched, as they always
  were.
- **Why it changed, because the reason is the useful part.** Where a landlord
  has SOLD the property, moving out is not the right act at all — a transfer
  is, and a transfer hands the account, everything owed on it and the ownership
  to the new owner with the tenants left exactly where they are. So the thing
  the refusal was guarding against already has its own screen, and all the
  refusal actually blocked was a landlord leaving for some other reason.
- **The instruction is gone from all eleven languages, deliberately.** *"Close
  or reassign them first"* told a clerk to do something the product no longer
  asks of them. What is left is the fact and the number, and nothing else — no
  reason on screen and no code.
- **The clerk is not asked to tick anything.** A confirmation box would be the
  refusal again with one more click, and there are still five steps and a named
  commit button between reading the warning and closing an account.


## [2.316.3] — 2026-09-20

### Fixed

- **A note filed by another part of the team was overwritten ten minutes
  earlier and has been put back.** Two people wrote up a problem at the same
  moment and the product's own numbering gave them both the same number, so one
  write-up replaced the other. Nothing a customer can see was affected — both
  are internal notes — and both now exist, with different numbers.

## [2.316.2] — 2026-09-20

### Fixed

- **A customer who moves out part-way through the month is no longer charged
  the whole month's standing charge.** Until today a closing account was billed
  its base charge in full however few days it had used — on the case the
  Product Owner was shown, **$18.50 for twelve days of a thirty-day cycle,
  where twelve days is worth $7.40**. That is **$11.10 too much on the last
  bill anybody will ever read**, on a customer who is leaving. The final bill
  now divides the base charge over the customer's own billing cycle, and the
  line on the screen says *(prorated)* so a clerk can see it happened.
- The figure a clerk is shown on step 3 of the move-out wizard, the figure the
  One-time tab shows for a final bill, and the bill Billing actually raises are
  all the same number, because all three ask the same one function for it.
- **Nothing else changed.** An interim, catch-up, penalty or fee bill over a
  short window still carries its base charge whole — that was ruled on
  2026-08-23 and is untouched — and an account whose cycle has no calendar on
  it still bills exactly as it did yesterday rather than having a month
  invented for it. No account on the demo utility changes price: every one of
  them has a longer unbilled stretch than a month, and the charge was already
  capped at one month.

## [2.316.1] — 2026-09-20

### Fixed

- **The sale's own reference now shows in the trail at the top of the screen,
  and in the browser tab.** The transfer record shipped an hour earlier without
  it, because nothing in the product let a detail screen put its own number up
  there. That mechanism had in fact been built the same day by another piece of
  work, and this simply uses it. The two words before the number — *Accounts*
  and *Transfers* — still do not appear, because the shell works those out from
  the menu and a sale's address does not sit under it; that remainder is
  recorded rather than left unsaid.


## [2.316.0] — 2026-09-20

### Added

- **A sale can now be read back.** Until today a clerk could sell a property —
  hand an account to a new owner — and then had no way to look at what had
  happened. The sale had a record in the database and no screen anywhere in the
  product. There is one now, and it opens on the sale's own reference, the
  `TRF-` number a clerk quotes down a phone.

  It answers four questions, in the order somebody asks them. **What happened**
  — the account, the unit, the address, the day, who sold, who bought, what
  identification they gave, whether they were already a customer, and who
  pressed the button and when. **What did not change** — the account number,
  the unit and its meters, the plan, the service agreements and the ledger,
  because a sale in this product moves the owner and nothing else. **The money
  as it stood on the day** — the balance and the deposit the buyer took on.
  **What this record does not say** — the things a clerk still has to do by
  hand, chiefly that the property's owner record and the account's contact
  details both still name the seller.

  **The two rows that matter most read `$0.00` on purpose.** Nothing is
  refunded to the seller and nothing is re-collected from the buyer: the
  deposit simply stays where it is. That is the rule the whole sale flow exists
  to make true, and the record now shows it rather than leaving a clerk to hope.

  **Where the product does not know something, the screen says so in its own
  words instead of showing a figure.** Deposit interest is not shown as zero —
  it is worked out when an account finally settles, so on the day of a sale
  there is nothing to show and the screen says *counted at settlement*. How many
  unbroken months the ledger runs is not counted anywhere yet, so the screen
  says the length was never counted rather than printing a number nobody
  measured. And where the seller's name was not kept — the product overwrites it
  today, which the Product Owner ruled on 20 September must stop — the record
  says the seller was not kept instead of inventing one.

  **The record has no buttons, and that is the answer rather than a gap.** A
  sale has already happened; there is nothing left to decide about it. The only
  two controls are doors: one opens the customer, one opens the account.

### Known

- **Nothing links to the new screen yet.** The Transfers tab does not offer a
  way to open a sale, because the file that draws that list is being changed by
  another piece of work at the same time. The screen is reachable by typing its
  address, and the missing link is recorded so it is not forgotten.
- **The screen is waiting on its server half.** The read that fills it is being
  built alongside this, so until it lands the address says the reference names
  no transfer rather than showing an empty version of the record.


## [2.315.1] — 2026-09-20

### Fixed

- **The Transfers tab now describes the sale a transfer actually is.** Since
  2026-09-01 a transfer has reassigned one account to a new owner — a property
  being sold — and the list beside it went on describing the job that was
  replaced: a customer moving to a new address. Six of the things it told a
  clerk were untrue. `Open` read *"same customer, new address"* when a sale is a
  DIFFERENT customer at the SAME address; `Moving this week` counted sale dates;
  two tiles counted a deposit and an arrear election that nobody makes any more;
  the empty state described the one case the wizard's own red warning says is
  **not** a transfer; and a note explained that a transfer's *"two halves"* are
  kept out of two other lists, when a sale has no halves.
- **The list is now the three tiles and eight columns the blueprint draws.**
  `Open · Selling this week · Owed on accounts being sold`, over `Reference ·
  Address · Account · Sold to · Sale date · Step · Taken on · State`. The
  property's address is shown for the first time; the two account numbers with
  an arrow between them are one account; the two date columns, which were always
  the same day, are one `Sale date`; and `Money` — two stacked sentences about
  positions that do not move — is one `Taken on` figure, the balance the buyer
  takes on. About seventy words of explanation came off the screen.
- **Two things the blueprint draws are deliberately still absent**, and each
  would have had to be invented. `Sold by` cannot be shown because the seller's
  name is overwritten when the sale completes and the only other copy is in a
  log that gets deleted on a schedule. The `↗ Open` row action is not drawn
  because there is no page for it to open. Both are recorded, and the test suite
  now goes red on the day either becomes possible.


## [2.315.0] — 2026-09-20

### Changed

- **The Accounts screen now reads the way it was drawn, on all ten of its
  tabs.** It is one screen with ten tabs across the top, and its head had never
  been built to the design: the page was simply called *Accounts*, the same
  word as the menu item that opens it, with nothing saying which tab you were
  looking at. It now reads **ACCOUNTS** in small letters over the title **The
  register**, and under that a line saying *10 tabs · Move-outs* — the tab you
  are actually on. The trail at the top of the window follows it too, so it
  reads *Accounts › Move-outs* instead of stopping at *Accounts*, and the word
  *Accounts* there is now a link back to the list.

- **The create button at the top right is quiet now.** It was a solid red
  button — the loudest thing on the page — sitting over tabs that are often
  nearly empty, so *+ New transfer* shouted at a clerk who had opened the tab
  to read two rows. It is the same words in the same place and it does the same
  thing; it is simply no longer a filled button. Every tab still offers its own
  way in.

- **The number beside the Accounts tab is gone.** One tab out of ten carried a
  count, and it was not the number of accounts you have: it was the number of
  rows matching whatever you had typed in the search box, so it moved as you
  typed. The list's own footer already says *1–50 of 782* for what is on
  screen, which is the honest place for it.

  **The line under the title does not yet say how many are still open.** The
  design asks for it — *10 tabs · Move-outs · 1 still open* — and no tab can
  answer it today without a second, separate count of the same thing, which
  would sooner or later disagree with the tile beside it. It is left out rather
  than printed as a zero, because a zero would say *nothing is open*, and that
  is a claim nothing here can make.

## [2.314.3] — 2026-09-20

### Fixed

- **A move-out's final bill can be priced again, and the screen says what it
  was priced from.** The wizard asks for the closing meter reading on step 2
  and prices the final bill on step 3, while the readings themselves are
  written at step 6 with the close — so when step 3 ran, the closing register
  did not exist yet and the bill was refused on every move-out in the product,
  with a sentence about a missing meter factor. Step 3 now prices the readings
  the clerk has keyed and nobody has committed, and carries one line saying so:
  *Priced from reads not yet committed.* Nothing is written any earlier than it
  was: the readings still commit with the close, in the one transaction, so a
  clerk who walks away halfway leaves the meter exactly as they found it.
  Measured on a real account: a clerk keys a closing electric read of 52,410
  against a last committed 51,776, and the bill is 634 kWh at $0.12 = $76.08
  plus a $20.00 base charge, **$96.08** — and no invoice, no journal line and
  no bill number are created by looking at it.
- **The figure is worked out again when, and only when, a reading changes.** A
  clerk who corrects a register on step 2 and steps forward sees a re-priced
  bill; one who walks back and forth between the steps sees the figure they
  already saw.
- **A clerk who closed the account first is now told why the bill cannot be
  raised.** Asking for a final bill after the move-out had already committed
  answered with a sentence about tariff versions. It now answers with the one
  that matters — the final bill has to be produced before the move-out writes
  the close — which the product had always known and had never been able to say.
- **Step 3 is called *Final bill & deposit*.** It read *Settle the money*,
  which names the act and hides the noun a clerk is hunting for.

## [2.314.2] — 2026-09-20

### Fixed

- **A landlord's account can no longer be closed while their tenants are still
  on supply.** Until now the product allowed it without a word: the account
  closed, its services ended, and it wrote a numbered move-out record saying
  the move had happened. Two things quietly broke when it did. If one of those
  tenants later left owing money, the clerk's fourth option on the shortfall
  step — *tie it back to the landlord* — had no account left to tie it to; and

  again when the clerk presses the button, and reads
  `2 sub-accounts are still open. Close or reassign them first.`
  **Nothing already recorded is changed** — the two move records on the beta
  were checked and neither is against a landlord's account.


## [2.314.1] — 2026-09-20

### Changed

- **The transfer wizard says a great deal less, because the Product Owner read
  it aloud and most of it was not for a clerk.** 272 words come off steps 1, 2
  and 3, and 21 more with step 4's panel — 293 in all, counted from the
  sentences themselves and net of the four that replaced them. Step 1 no longer apologises for what the
  screen cannot look up, no longer tells a clerk to go and check for a payment
  plan, a dispute or an unbilled cycle themselves, and its search box is hinted
  in four words instead of twenty-seven. Step 2 no longer says *"a move-out
  usually needs a final read"* — this is a sale, it closes nothing and takes no
  reading — and no longer shows a clerk which of our own modules answers what.
  Step 3's two explanation panels are one line each. Step 4 no longer shows a
  question the business has not answered. **What a clerk needs is untouched:**
  *"Stays with you"*, *"What this sale will not touch"*, *"Nothing is prorated
  at a sale. One period, one bill."*, and the four rows describing the property
  and its billing.

### Fixed

- **Leaving the transfer wizard no longer lands on an error page.** `Save &
  exit`, the `← Transfers` link at the top and `Back to transfers` after a
  completed sale all pointed at an address the product reads as *an account
  named "transfers"*, so every one of them showed **"This account could not be
  opened."** All three now open the Transfers list. (`DEF-CUS-5948`.)

- **Step 5 stops claiming the product has no way of sending anything.** It has
  five — and none of them has ever delivered a single message: there are 420
  messages waiting in the queue on the sample utility and not one has been sent.
  The screen now says the plain thing instead, which is that **nobody is told a
  sale happened and the clerk has to tell the buyer and the seller themselves**.
  No tick-list of letters was added, deliberately: there is no
  change-of-ownership letter in the template catalogue, nothing in the product
  can put a message into the queue, and a tick that promised a letter would be
  promising something this product has never once done. That work is
  `DEF-CUS-5949`. (`DEF-CUS-5949`.)

- **The transfer wizard has a walkthrough for the first time**, which presses
  every control on all five steps instead of reading the markup around them —
  `10-scripts/def_cus_5934_transfer_wizard_walkthrough.mjs`. Move-in, move-out
  and the clerk request walk each had one; this flow did not, which is why the
  Product Owner found everything above by hand.

### Known, and filed rather than glossed

- **Seven short new sentences on this screen read in English in every language,
  for now.** The copy ruling renamed the keys behind them and the eleven
  translation files were deliberately not touched in the same change: two other
  people were editing those files at the time, and this product's rule is that a
  translation is written in its own language rather than run through English. The
  exact sixteen keys to write and to remove are recorded as `DEF-CUS-5973`.

### Not fixed, and said plainly

- **`DEF-CUS-5934` — *"step 4 when last tick is press - uI breaks"* — stays
  open.** The tick was pressed in a real browser in every state the step has
  (four window widths, a loaded account, a missing balance, a missing deposit,
  no account at all, before and after the sale date, arriving forwards, by the
  step bar, by `Back`, after a reload, with the park panel open, ticked and
  unticked and ticked again, and after a minute and a half of sitting on the
  step) and it records the tick and leaves the screen standing every time. The
  one thing on step 4 that **did** break the screen was the way out of the
  wizard, which is fixed above. We cannot say whether that is what was hit, and
  the tenant it was reported on is not one we hold.

## [2.314.0] — 2026-09-20

### Added

- **The move-out screen now asks why a customer is leaving, and keeps the
  answer.** The screen had offered five reasons — lease ended, owner sold the
  property, downgrade or hardship, deceased, other — since the day it was
  built, and stored none of them: there was no column to put one in, so the
  wizard asked and forgot. A utility that cannot say why forty accounts closed
  last quarter cannot answer its own board. The reason is now a required choice
  beside the move-out date, it is saved with the closure, and it reads back on
  the move-out's own record page.

  **Accounts closed before today keep no reason and none was invented for
  them.** Their record says the product never asked, which is the truth. A
  closure made from now on and skipped says so differently — *not given* rather
  than *not asked* — because those are two different facts about a utility's
  own records.

### Fixed

- **A move-out you parked and came back to can now be opened again.** Parking a
  half-finished move-out saved everything you had typed, and then there was no
  way back to it from the move-out's own record: that page is found by the
  job's number, and a parked move-out had never been given one. The `Resume`
  button added the day before pointed at a page nobody could reach.

  A parked move-out is now given its number the moment it is put down — the
  same `MVO-` number the finished move-out is filed under, so the number you
  write on a sticky note is the number it ends up on. The Move-outs list prints
  it, the record page opens on it, and `Resume` picks the job back up where you
  left it. **The number is not used twice**: finishing the job keeps the number
  the draft was carrying rather than issuing a second one.

  Two smaller things on the same path: a parked move-out's record showed no
  move-out date even though one had been typed, and an unfinished move-out
  could not be matched to its account in the list.

## [2.313.2] — 2026-09-19

### Fixed

- **A clerk can now record what happens to money a departing customer still
  owes.** On the last screen of a move-out, after the deposit has been applied,
  there is sometimes a balance left over — and step 4 is where a clerk says
  whether it is collected, put on a payment plan, written off, or moved to the
  landlord's account. **That button refused every time it was pressed, on every
  account.** The screen worked the figure out correctly and then would not
  accept an answer about it: on one real account it showed `Short by $1,591.85`
  and replied *"there is no shortfall to decide"* directly underneath. The
  screen was telling the server the bill figure when it asked what the position
  was, and not telling it when it saved the answer, so the server worked the sum
  out a second time with the bill missing. Both now state the same figure, from
  one place. Nothing about how the money is worked out has changed.
- **The heading over that figure spells the money like every other figure in
  the product.** It read `What happens to 1591.85` — no dollar sign, no comma —
  directly above a line reading `$1,591.85`. It now reads
  `What happens to $1,591.85`.


## [2.313.1] — 2026-09-19

### Added

- **The Move-outs list now shows the move-outs that have not finished yet.**
  Until today it listed only move-outs that were already done, so a clerk who
  started one, stopped part-way and came back had nothing on the list to go
  back to. An unfinished move-out is now a row like any other, showing the

  `2 of 6` — beside the word `In progress`, or `Waiting` where they recorded

- Opening an unfinished row carries on from where it was left, rather than

### Changed

- **A finished move-out now reads `Completed` on the list**, which is the word
  its own record page has always used. It read `Closed` there and `completed`
  here, so one move-out had two words on two screens a clerk moves between with

### Note

- Where an unfinished move-out cannot answer a column yet, the list says so
  rather than showing a dash: it has no reference number until it completes,

- A move-out nobody has started is still not on the list. Nothing records one

- An unfinished move-out currently appears both in the panel above the table
  and as a row in it. Which of the two should stay is with the Product Owner.

## [2.313.0] — 2026-09-19

### Added

- **The move-out wizard's final-bill step now shows the bill.** Step 3 drew a
  panel saying the figure was not available; it now lists what the closing bill
  will contain — each line with its period and its amount, the export credit,
  and the net — and beneath it the whole subtraction: what is outstanding, what
  the deposit covers, and what is left over. No bill is issued by this screen;
  it prices what the bill will contain and posts nothing.
- **What happens to the deposit is stated.** The four things that can happen to
  it are named, the one that applies is marked, and the other three each say in
  a few words what they would need. Which one applies is decided by the
  subtraction, not by the clerk, so none of them is offered as a choice.
- **Step 4 shows the shortfall and what each way of settling it would need** —
  including who can do it, and that writing a debt off needs a supervisor.
- **Step 5 now says what closing this account actually does** — to the account,
  the unit, the meters and the money — what will be sent and when, and what
  closing does NOT do. Six things it still cannot work out are named one by
  one rather than left blank, because a blank and a harmless answer look the
  same on a screen.
- **Step 1 shows the plan the unit is billed on**, which is what the reviewer
  asked for and the only change to that step.
- Step 6 recaps the new money and the new consequences, so the last screen
  before the close agrees with the three before it.

### Fixed

- **The money step said an account owed nothing when it had not worked out what
  it owed.** Where the closing position could not be totalled, `Short by` still
  printed `$0.00` — on the money step, on the shortfall step, on what happens
  next and on the review. It now says the subtraction has not run, and the two
  figures that ARE known — the balance carried in and the deposit held — still
  show.
- **A clerk could choose where a departing tenant's debt goes, press the
  button, and always be refused.** Step 4 offered four ways to settle a
  shortfall on every move-out, and the save behind them failed every time
  because the account's position had not been worked out. The four now appear
  only when there is a shortfall to settle, and the step says plainly when
  there is nothing yet to decide.

## [2.312.0] — 2026-09-19

### Added

- **An unfinished move can be picked up from its own record page.** Opening an
  in-progress move-in or move-out from the register used to be a dead end: the
  page showed what had been filled in so far and offered no way onward, so the
  clerk had to go back to the parked-drafts panel to carry on. The record now
  carries a `Resume` action that reopens the wizard at the step the draft was
  parked at, with everything that was typed.
- The action appears on unfinished moves only. A completed move-in or move-out
  is unchanged and still offers doors and no actions.
- `Resume` is the same word the parked-drafts panel uses, in all eleven
  languages, because it is the same act on a second surface.

### Note

- This gives the journey its last step; it does not change what a move-out can
  settle. A move-out still reaches a money step that cannot total, because no
  final bill is produced in that flow yet. That work is separate and in hand.

## [2.311.6] — 2026-09-19

### Fixed

- **The Move-outs list was rebuilt to its drawing, and this build is the one a
  browser has actually been clicked through.** The summary strip shows three
  tiles instead of five, the two that counted things the product cannot yet
  work out are gone, and the paragraphs of explanation under the table have
  been removed. The Settlement column is one line. The reference, the account
  number and a new `Open` on every row each open the record they name.
- **The move record no longer breaks when it finishes loading.** Opening a
  move-in or a move-out showed *"Unexpected Application Error"* once the data
  arrived. It opens, on both kinds of move.

## [2.311.5] — 2026-09-19

### Added

- **A clerk can attach a document to a new service request.** Step 4 of the new
  request wizard used to offer nine tick-boxes and a sentence explaining that
  there was nowhere to keep a file. There is now: choose what the document is,
  pick the file, say what it proves, and mark whether this request needs it.
  The file is kept, shrunk on the way in where that loses nothing, and listed
  with its name, its size, who attached it and when.
- **A list of what a request holds, instead of a list of what it could hold.**
  The step draws the documents on the request — `Proof of identity`,
  `Tenancy agreement or deed` and the rest — with their file, their uploader
  and their state, and four filters: everything, the required ones, the ones
  still missing a file, and the rejected ones. `Add another document` records
  that something is expected before it arrives.
- **A document now survives the draft.** Attaching used to be held in the
  screen until the next save, so a clerk who noted three documents and left the
  wizard lost all three. What is attached is kept against the request itself,
  so it is still there after stepping on and back, and after closing the wizard
  and returning to the draft.

### Fixed

- **A date on the documents list could show the wrong day.** The uploaded-on
  date was rendered without the utility's own time zone, so a document filed
  late in the evening could read as the next day's.
- **A missing uploader showed the word "undefined".** Where nobody is recorded
  as having attached a file — a document the system itself filed, for example —
  the list now shows a dash.
- **A document whose file was never really stored no longer claims otherwise.**
  A handful of sample records name a file that does not exist, and four of them
  said they had been verified. They now read `Nothing attached`, and nothing on
  the screen offers to open them.

## [2.311.4] — 2026-09-19

### Fixed

- **A citation in the payments API pointed at the wrong defect.** A push
  script substituted a whole id family rather than one occurrence and rewrote
  an unrelated, correct reference. Both ids being real, no check could see it.
  Restored.

## [2.311.3] — 2026-09-19

### Added

- **The day's counter takings, split by how the money was handed over.** Money
  taken at a counter for an application fee has reached the books since
  2026-09-15, but the list of it could only be filtered by whether it was still
  being held — so the only questions it answered were *everything ever taken*
  and *everything still held*, and neither of those balances a cash drawer.
  `GET /counter-receipts` now takes `f.taken_on=YYYY-MM-DD`, and its totals
  carry a `by_method` split: a day on which the counter took **$25.00 cash and
  $30.00 by cheque** reads **$55.00 taken** with a **cash line of $25.00**,
  which is the only one of the three that can be counted against the notes and
  coin in the drawer. Grouped by day and method deliberately, because that is
  how the bank deposit already groups. Proved on real PostgreSQL and tied out
  against `1010 Undeposited funds`.
- **Still not reachable from any screen.** Nothing in the front end mounts this
  list — it was deferred when the counter money was first made to post and it
  is deferred still. A clerk cannot balance a till from the product today.

## [2.311.2] — 2026-09-19

### Changed

- **The first page of a new request is the page that was drawn.** *How did this
  reach us?* is now just **Channel**; the fields sit two across in the drawn
  order — Channel beside Full name, Email beside Phone, Date of birth beside
  Driver's licence, then the Social Security Number — and **Applying as is a
  dropdown** rather than a pair of buttons, which the Product Owner asked for on
  2026-09-19. Four explanatory sentences came off the step: what happens if you
  leave the name blank, what happens on a staff-raised request, and the two
  promising that the licence and the SSN are stored encrypted. **Nothing about
  the storage changed** — both are still encrypted, and still proved by a test
  that reads the raw column back; the sentences belong in the record rather than
  on a counter clerk's form.
- **The co-applicant is one tick box.** It was a heading, a badge and
  twenty-six words about who is liable for the bill.
- **The address page asks how many units are on the property.** What the
  applicant says is kept beside what the register holds, and the page says
  whether the two **agree** or **differ**.
- **The billing address box is always on screen**, greyed out while *Same as
  the service address* is ticked, so a clerk can see what clearing the tick
  will ask for.
- **The six property-type buttons are gone from the address page.** Product
  Owner: *"if premises is found then we already have all details related with
  property"*. Nothing was deleted — a request that already carries a property
  type still shows it.

### Fixed

- **Picking a building now offers its units.** A clerk who chose a property
  with six flats on record was still handed an empty box to type the flat
  number into — on every property, every time — so the unit was typed rather
  than chosen off the register. It had been that way since 2026-09-15.


## [2.311.1] — 2026-09-19

### Fixed

- **Six sample documents on a service request pointed at files that do not
  exist, and four of them said *Verified*.** All six rows carry a reference
  shaped `sample-data://cr030/…`; **none of them resolves to a stored file**,
  every size is blank, and four are marked as checked — a clerk having
  certified a document nobody can open. Asking for one of them would have shown
  *"Something went wrong on our side"* on a row the screen was displaying. It
  now says plainly that there is no file yet, and any of those rows can be
  given a real file, so none of them is stranded.
  **Still owed** (filed, not fixed here): the seeder should store real bytes or
  leave the reference blank, a document marked *Verified* with no readable file
  should not be possible, and the Documents tab still counts those six as
  attached.

## [2.311.0] — 2026-09-19

### Added

- **A clerk can attach the applicant's paperwork to a service request, and it is
  kept.** Until now the capture screen said *"We cannot take a file yet — there
  is nowhere to store it"*, and that was the plain truth: nothing in this
  product accepted a file for a request. A driving licence, a deed or a site
  plan now goes into the same document store the bills and the notices already
  use, so it is kept for seven years and cannot be altered or deleted
  afterwards, and it can be handed back as a link that dies after four hours.
  **Attaching is still not checking** — every file arrives marked *Not checked*
  and stays that way until a person opens it and says it is good.
  **A request can hold several documents of the same kind**, which is what an
  applicant for a new connection actually brings.
- **Files are made smaller on the way in, and the picture does not change.**
  Over 56 real image files, **18,076,547 bytes became 13,306,223 — 26.4% saved
  — with no pixel altered in any of them.** We deliberately do *not* reduce a
  photograph's quality the way a phone does: these are documents somebody reads
  a licence number or a property boundary off, and once a file is stored it
  cannot be replaced. **A PDF, a spreadsheet and any image under 64 KB are
  stored exactly as they arrived.** Where a file was made smaller, the record
  keeps **both** sizes, so a clerk who chose a 3.1 MB file and sees a smaller
  one on screen is told why.
- ⚠ **The button is not released yet.** The door is built, tested and tenant-
  scoped; the *Attach a file* control on step 4 of the capture wizard is still
  disabled and still shows the old sentence, because that screen was being
  rebuilt by another lane on the day this landed. The next lane on that step
  releases the control and retires the message.

## [2.310.11] — 2026-09-19

### Fixed

- **You can now set a unit's floor area while you are adding it.** `Floor area`
  was on the edit form, on the unit's own page, in the units list and in the
  spreadsheet import — everywhere except the one screen where units are created.
  A clerk could only set it by adding a unit and then immediately editing it, or
  by importing a file. It now sits directly under `Floor` on the add form, takes
  one figure that is written onto every unit the run creates, and the review step
  states it before anything is created. (`DEF-MET-5868`)

- **`Cancel` has moved to the bottom of four screens, where the rest of the
  buttons are.** On Add units, the plan wizard, the discount wizard and the
  budget-billing enrolment it sat alone in the top-right corner, away from
  `Back` and the button that finishes the job. It is now the left-hand end of the
  same footer row. The enrolment screen had *two* exits — `Cancel` at the top and
  `Back` at the bottom, both going to the same place — and now has one. **Two
  more screens are still to come**, Add property and the charge-code wizard; both
  were being changed by other people at the time and are carried separately.
  (`DEF-MET-5869`)

- **Add units has a way back to the units list again.** The screen had no back
  link at all: the only way out was `Cancel`, and the `Premises › Units` trail at
  the top of the page is not clickable on the part that says `Units` — the part
  that is clickable goes to the properties list instead. `← Units` is back in the
  page head, and it reads differently from the footer's `Back`, which still means
  only *the previous step*. (`DEF-MET-5870`)

## [2.310.10] — 2026-09-19

### Fixed

- **Putting a meter on a unit now asks which service it serves, and a meter
  cannot be fitted without an answer.** Assigning one from the shelf used to
  leave the Service column empty, and a meter with no service cannot be billed
  at all. The Assign panel now offers the services that address actually takes
  — nothing more, so it cannot offer one the system would refuse — and nothing
  is chosen for you. A bin, a backflow preventer or a battery still goes on in
  one press, because those do not measure anything. (`DEF-MET-5860`)

- **`On since` now says when the meter arrived at that unit.** It was showing
  the day the meter was first installed, which is a different day once a meter
  has been moved — and is blank altogether on anything taken from the shelf, so
  the column read as a dash on every meter anybody had just fitted.
  (`DEF-MET-5861`)

- **`Last read` now shows the reading on the dial, with the usage beside it.**
  It was showing only the usage since the previous read, so the very first read
  on a new meter — which has no previous read to measure against — appeared as
  a bare date with no figure at all. A meter now reads as its date, its
  reading, and then how much was used; a first read shows its date and its
  reading, and no usage, because there genuinely is none. (`DEF-MET-5862`)


## [2.310.9] — 2026-09-19

### Fixed

- **Pressing Continue on an unfinished tax step now says so.** The tax wizard's
  first step refused an incomplete form correctly every time and then erased its
  own message a line later, so a clerk saw nothing at all — no sentence, no
  marked box, no change — and the button simply looked broken. It had been that
  way since 11 September. The refusal now stays on screen and the empty boxes are
  marked, which is what the refusal's own wording has always promised. The other
  four Plans & Rates wizards never had this. (`DEF-RAT-5804`)

- **The tax wizard no longer tells a clerk a blank boundary reaches nobody when it
  reaches 71 of 79 properties.** Choosing *Inside city limits* and leaving the
  place box empty showed the warning *"Left blank, this reaches nobody"* directly
  above a count reading *"71 of 79 premises match"*. The warning is true for
  *In a state* — that one really does reach nobody — and it was being shown under
  every boundary. Believing it and leaving the box blank would have taxed 71
  properties. (`DEF-RAT-5805`)

- **And the count now says how it was reached.** Each property can carry its own
  recorded *City limits* answer, and where it does, that answer decides — the typed
  town name only covers properties nobody has recorded one for. That is why scoping
  a tax to Katy, a town with six properties here, reached seventy-seven, and why
  typing a town this utility has never heard of reached exactly as many as leaving
  the box empty. The number was right and unexplainable. The screen now reads
  *"71 by recorded City limits. 6 more by name."* under the count, on the first step
  and again on the review, and the sample addresses beside it name both groups
  instead of only one. **No tax changes what it charges: the rule that decides this
  has not moved.** (`DEF-RAT-5806`)

- **Three boundaries the product cannot work out yet can no longer be chosen.**
  *In a county*, *In a taxing district* and *A named list of premises* have nothing
  in the product to match against, so a tax scoped by one of them quietly reached
  nobody for ever. The screen said so in red after the choice was made and still let
  it be saved. All five are still listed; the three that cannot work are greyed out,
  and each switches itself back on the day the product can answer it. A tax already
  using one still opens and still saves.

- **The clerk is told a tax cannot be deleted, before they save one.** There is no
  way to delete a tax anywhere in the product — it is switched off and kept — and
  nothing said so until after the fact.


## [2.310.8] — 2026-09-19

### Fixed

- **The last page of a new rate no longer shows a blank price.** *Review &
  activate* asks you to check what will be stored, and for four of the seven
  rate shapes it showed nothing at all — a time-of-use rate with four priced
  windows, a demand rate carrying an energy price and a demand price, a
  seasonal rate and a capacity rate all ended on one empty line. Every shape now
  lists what it will store, a line each, named: *Summer · Off-peak, 00:00 to
  16:00 — 0.0900*. (`DEF-RAT-5826`)

- **Fixing a wrong price now leaves a mark on the rate's own history.** The
  *Fix an error* route worked and said nothing afterwards: the Audit tab showed
  two identical rows, both carrying the reason typed on the ORIGINAL filing, and
  labelled the row you had just replaced **Scheduled** — the word this screen
  uses for a change still to come. The replaced row now reads **Corrected** and
  says *"This filing was corrected."*, the new row is marked **Correction**, and
  the reason you typed is the reason shown against it. (`DEF-RAT-5827`)

- **Filing next year's rate no longer inherits this year's end date.** Opening a
  live rate to file the next one handed you the dates of the rate you are
  replacing. A 2029 filing was then refused — *"The end date has to come after
  the start date"* — about a box you never touched; worse, a change dated inside
  the old window was accepted and quietly took that window's end date as its
  own, leaving the service with no price from the following January. Both dates
  now start empty on a new version. Picking up an unfinished change you parked
  still gives you back the dates you parked. (`DEF-RAT-5833`)

- **The review no longer says a minimum is never billed.** It is: the minimum on
  a rate schedule is what tops a bill up, and has been since 10 September. The
  note has moved onto the per-size table above it, where it is true, and now
  reads *"Per-size floors are not billed yet. Billing reads the minimum bill
  below."* (`DEF-RAT-5828`)

- **A missing season price now marks the box it is about.** Leaving one blank on
  a seasonal rate was refused with *"This is required."* on a page where nothing
  was marked. The message now sits under the season's own price box, the box
  carries the required star, and it clears the moment you type. (`DEF-RAT-5830`,
  and part of `DEF-RAT-5829`)

- **A rate filed ahead of time no longer calls itself two things at once.** A
  water rate starting 1 March 2027 showed the pill **Draft** and the tile
  **IN FORCE · v1** in the same header. The tile now reads *No version in
  force*, the version is listed as **Scheduled**, and *Next change* still names
  the date. (`DEF-RAT-5831`)

- **The demand ratchet has a box to tick.** The demand editor described a
  ratchet setting and offered no way to set it — and a rate that arrived with it
  switched on could not be switched off. There is now a tick and a percentage
  beside the power-factor pair, and the paragraph describing it is gone.
  (`DEF-RAT-5832`)

### Known

- **After a rate is refused, the way forward is still the red card's Retry.**
  Fix the value and the page stops asking for it, but the footer's *Continue*
  and *Back* do not come back until you press *Retry* or *Cancel*, and the red
  card keeps repeating the message it was refused with. That footer is shared
  with five other wizards, so it is being handled separately (`DEF-RAT-5829`).

## [2.310.7] — 2026-09-19

### Fixed

- **The Coverage tab on a billing cycle now says whose accounts it is listing.**
  It lists every account in the utility that reaches **no cycle at all** — which
  is what it has always been for — but nothing on the screen said so, so the
  list read as *this* cycle's accounts and testers reported accounts they had
  never selected. The table now has a heading, **On no cycle**, and one line
  under it: *The whole utility, not this cycle. Put them on a route.* Nothing
  about the figures changed. (`DEF-MET-5854`)

- **The Premises list's one line under the title is the subtitle the design
  draws.** It read `79 premises · 130 + 1 common units · 62 vacant · 4 pending
  activation`; it now reads *Every property that takes service, and the units
  inside them.* **No count has become unreachable, and every figure is
  identical where it now lives:** the Premises footer says how many properties
  there are (79), *Status = Pending* narrows it to the 4 awaiting activation,
  and on the Units tab the footer says how many units there are (131) with

### Reported, not changed

- **"Some units show as having no assets" could not be reproduced.** Every one
  of the 83 stops on all 12 routes of the demo utility agrees with the Assets

  the Route detail asks *"is this meter's assignment still open"* where billing
  asks *"is this meter on the unit today and in service"*, so **a meter
  scheduled for removal next month disappears from the route a month early**.
  That is filed with its worked example rather than fixed, because it is not
  what was reported and the same answer feeds the Units list. To settle the

## [2.310.6] — 2026-09-19

### Fixed

- **The review step shows the price you just typed.** Editing a charge code, a
  clerk who changed the amount from 3.50 to 4.25 reached step 3 of 3 and read
  back **3.50** — on the Amount row and on the sample bill line. The save was
  always right; only the read-back was wrong, which is the worse direction: you
  either retype a change that already worked, abandon a correct one, or save
  believing you entered something else. Step 3 now reads back what is in the
  box. Nothing changed for a code being created, and a retyped percentage still
  says *As typed above* rather than showing a figure it cannot format honestly.
  (`DEF-RAT-5819`)

- **A charge code can no longer be saved in a state that stops bills.**
  *Apply automatically* means *on every bill*, and Penalty, One-time,
  Refundable and Adjustment all mean *on an event* — the billing engine refuses
  the combination. It was offered on all five types anyway, the screen did not
  change by one character when you ticked it, step 3 never mentioned it, and
  the save succeeded. A Penalty code scoped to Commercial would then have
  refused the bill of every Commercial customer and left Residential and
  Industrial untouched. The tick is now greyed out on the four types that
  cannot carry it and says why in five words; a code that already has the
  contradiction can still be un-ticked, and Continue waits until it is. Step 3
  gained a **When it applies** row, so it can never be saved unseen.
  (`DEF-RAT-5820`)

- **You can see which charge codes are limited to one customer class.** The
  list has a **Customer class** column beside Service — the two rules that
  decide whether a code reaches a customer, side by side — and the code's own
  **Applicability** tab now names the class, in the same words the rate
  schedule already uses. A code that reaches everyone says *Every customer
  class* rather than leaving the cell blank. (`DEF-RAT-5821`)

- **The charge-code screens stop implying a price is versioned.** The header
  read *"…references the version in force, so an issued bill never changes."*
  A charge code has no versions and no dates: a new amount prices the next bill
  on every plan carrying it, at once. It now says that, and the edit screen
  says it where the clerk is standing. Nothing about issued bills changed —
  those keep their price, as they always have. (`DEF-RAT-5824`)

- **Choosing *Refundable* no longer sends you to a screen that was deleted.**
  It read *"Deposit rules live on the plan."* They moved to the charge code on
  8 September, and the plan's deposits panel went with them — so a clerk who
  followed that line walked all eight steps of the plan wizard and found
  nothing. It now says where the deposit amount actually is. (`DEF-RAT-5825`)

### Known

- **The charge-codes list still cannot be FILTERED by customer class**, only
  read. The column answers the question a clerk was asking; the filter needs a
  database lookup our test database cannot run, so it is filed rather than
  half-built.

- **A charge code's Plans tab still contradicts the tile above it** — the tile
  counts 0 where the table lists five plans. That is an older report and is not
  touched here.

## [2.310.5] — 2026-09-19

### Fixed

- **A plan no longer shows a database code where its customer class should be,
  and no longer silently stops narrowing.** Three sample plans — *Sample —
  Residential*, *Sample — Commercial* and *Sample — Industrial* — each pointed
  at a customer class that had been deleted two days earlier, when every
  utility got its own list of classes instead of sharing one. Nothing said
  anything: the plan wizard rendered the 36-character code as the class, and
  because the code matched nothing the plan quietly offered every charge code

## [2.310.4] — 2026-09-19

### Fixed

- **Adding a property now opens the owner's account for real.** The last two
  things standing in the way are gone. The form asks who the owner is — whether
  they are a **person or a company**, and then the one identifier that goes with
  that answer: a Social Security number, a driving licence or a phone for a
  person, a Tax ID for a company. With a name, one identifier and an account
  type, pressing Create opens the owner's Master Account and links it to them,
  with the number coming from your own numbering settings. (`OQ-MET-12472`)

- **A company is never asked for a phone or a Social Security number, and a
  person is never asked for a Tax ID.** The boxes change with the answer, so the
  wrong one cannot be filled in by accident — a business filed under a phone
  number is a business nobody can find again.

- **Picking an owner from the list is now enough.** Before this, an owner picked
  properly but with *Managed by* left empty was refused, and only someone who
  also retyped the name into the free-text box got through. The owner's own
  contact details are used now. (`DEF-MET-5847`)

- **The *Where is it?* step stopped drawing two of everything.** Where a utility
  has a city address lookup, the step showed two headings, two address boxes and
  two postcode boxes, with nothing saying which one counted. It is one section
  now, with one address box, and the lookup offers its matches underneath it.
  A utility with no lookup sees exactly what it always saw. (`DEF-MET-5845`)

### Unchanged, deliberately

- **A property still saves with the owner boxes empty.** An address is a real
  address whether or not anybody can be billed for it. You are told before you
  press Create that no owner account will be opened, and the address is never
  lost because of it.

- **Typing a name in *Managed by* still creates nobody.** It is a name, not a
  party — the owner list is the only thing that names one.

### Known

- **The *Create master account* button on the property page is still refused.**
  It has no place to put the owner's identity, so it meets the same rule this
  release satisfied on the Add Premises form. (`DEF-CUS-5846`)

## [2.310.3] — 2026-09-19

### Fixed

- **Adding a property now opens the owner's account, and says so when it
  cannot.** The Add Premises form asked for the owner and the manager and then
  saved the address and nothing else — no Master Account, and no word about it.
  Two other ways into the product had done this correctly for weeks: New
  Connect, and the premises import. The form was the one door that never called
  the account. It calls it now, through the same door, and the property is never
  lost if the account is refused. (`DEF-MET-5844`)

- **The form asks how the owner is charged.** There is a new **Account type**
  box under the owner. It is optional, and leaving it blank means no owner
  account is opened — the review screen says so in those words before you press
  Create. Nothing guesses it: the account type decides what the bill is priced
  and reported as, and a property type is not a consumer category.

### Known

- **An owner nobody has identified still gets no account.** A signed rule says
  every address gets its owner a Master Account; another says we cannot open one
  for a party with no identifier on file, and the owner record holds none. That
  is an open question for the Product Owner (`OQ-MET-12472`), and the same gate
  stops the **Create master account** button on the property page
  (`DEF-CUS-5846`).

## [2.310.2] — 2026-09-19

### Fixed

- **Three of the seven *Applies to* choices on a discount could not be saved at
  all.** Writing a discount, the second screen asks what it comes off and offers
  seven answers. Choosing *All services*, *Specific services* or *One service*
  filled the form in, pressed Create, and answered *"Something went wrong on our
  side."* — every time, for everybody. *All services* and *Specific services* are
  the pair asked for on 10 September; they were built on the screen and in the
  code that day and the database was never widened to accept them, so they had
  been dead every day since. *One service* is older and had never worked: the
  screen sends the word `water` and the column wanted an internal id. All seven
  save now, and each one is checked by reading the stored value back rather than
  by trusting the save.
- **A discount could be edited exactly once.** The second *Save new version* on
  any discount answered *"Something went wrong on our side. Nothing was saved."*
  and the edit door on that discount then stayed shut for good. The rule behind
  it is right — one draft at a time — but there was no way to see the draft that
  was blocking, and no way to get rid of it. It now says *"This discount already
  has a draft. Finish it or discard it."*, the discount's **Audit** tab lists
  every version including the draft, and the draft's row carries **Discard
  draft**.
- **Asking for proof and naming no document was refused with a developer code.**
  Choosing *Apply and approve, with proof* and ticking nothing showed the clerk
  the literal text `rating.discounts.proof_kinds_required`, at the very last
  step, after they had walked two more screens past the one where that choice is
  made. It now reads *"Name at least one accepted document."*, in all eleven
  languages, and it stops them on the step where the choice is made.

## [2.310.1] — 2026-09-19

### Fixed

- **Adding a route now asks for an area AND a sub-area, in two boxes.** The
  screen had one box under a label that read *"Area · sub-area"*, so it named
  two things and offered one. Two boxes was already the ruling — it was made on
  8 September and applied to the property screens that day, and this screen was
  never changed. A property and a route now use the same pair, and what gets
  stored has not moved: the sub-area when one is chosen, otherwise the area.
  (`DEF-TEN-5842`)

- **The premises picker in a new route opens on the area you just chose.** It
  used to ignore it and offer every property in the utility — on a 40,000-property
  utility that is 40,000 rows to hunt through for the forty on this route. On the
  demo utility, choosing *Downtown* now opens the picker on **16** properties
  instead of **79**. The narrowing shows as a chip you can read and take off, and
  a route that picks up a stray property outside its area is still one click
  away: remove the chip, or add a second area beside it. (`DEF-TEN-5843`)

- **"Select all" now exists when adding a cycle and on the units list.** Adding
  a cycle meant ticking every route by hand, and assigning a plan to a hundred
  units meant a hundred clicks. Both controls say how many they will take —
  *Select all 12*, *Select all 131* — and they mean **everything the filters
  match**, not the fifty rows on the page. A plan still cannot be assigned until
  something is selected; the button says so instead of hiding. (`DEF-TEN-5840`)

- **The eye icon is gone from the premises list.** It looked like *open this
  property* and went to the Units tab instead. The property number in the first
  column already opens the property, so the icon was removed rather than
  repointed. Units filtered by a property are still reachable — the units list
  has its own property filter, and each property has a Units tab.
  (`DEF-MET-5841`)


## [2.310.0] — 2026-09-19

### Changed

- **The premises and units import templates only ask for what a utility can
  actually supply.** The premises template offered 31 columns and units 20, and
  fourteen of them were fields our own address-matching process writes for
  itself — headings like *"Gis parcel id was"* and *"Gis verified at"*, which
  nobody chose and which arrived automatically whenever a field was added to the
  table. Premises now offers 24 columns and units 15. The real GIS keys stay:
  *GIS parcel ID* and *GIS point ID* are what a city gives a utility, and they
  have proper headings now instead of generated ones.
- **The owner column is called *Owner name*.** The template used to carry two
  name-shaped columns — *Owner* and *Owner name (legacy)* — and only one of them
  created the owner's account, so a utility filling in the wrong one got an
  address and no owner. The legacy box is gone from the template.

### Added

- **An import can now record the owner's category, and that is what makes the
