## [2.61.0] — 2026-08-27 · a premises can be marked inside or outside the city, and the surcharge finally bites

### Added
- **Jurisdiction is settable on a premises.** It decides whether a bill carries
  the outside-city surcharge, and until now **only a CSV import could write it**
  — there was no way to set it on one building.
  ⚠ **Three states, not a tick-box: *inside* · *outside* · *not recorded*.** A
  checkbox has two, and the one it defaults to is the one that ADDS money to a
  bill. Values that look like an answer but are not one — `1`, `0`, `maybe`,
  blank — are **refused rather than read charitably**, because a lenient parser
  turns a stray spreadsheet cell into a surcharge.
- **The sample tenant now exercises the surcharge**, so a demo shows what it
  actually does. **Worked, on a real issued bill — 161 Silver Creek Rd, June,
  18 kgal:** water usage **$109.00 → $163.50**, monthly base **$8.00 → $12.00**,
  **one bill up $58.50**. Every figure is quoted from an existing rate sheet;
  none was invented for this.
  The commercial tenants move **$0.00**, on purpose — their plan states no
  factor, which is what makes the "no factor, no surcharge" promise visible
  rather than asserted.

### Fixed
- **Turning the surcharge on nearly made 21 other bills fail, one silent
  exception at a time.** Those addresses sit on the same plan and had no
  jurisdiction recorded, so each would have refused its own bill on a demo that
  still looked healthy. Caught by the lane's own guard before it shipped — the
  guard asks *is anything exposed*, not *did my rows land*.

### Known
- **Correcting a jurisdiction applies FORWARD ONLY** and touches no bill already
  issued — issued money does not change by itself. Whether six months of a wrong
  mark (**about $350**) owes the customer an adjustment is a question for the
  Product Owner, and the code says so rather than implying it.
- ⚠ **Two signed rules meet here for the first time.** Sewer is exempt from the
  surcharge and its base is $0.00, so "flat everywhere" reaches nothing — while
  the sewer charge is 40% of a water charge the surcharge has already moved:
  **$43.60 → $65.40**. Neither rule is wrong; nobody has said what they mean
  together.

## [2.60.0] — 2026-08-27 · a transfer and a disconnect can be quoted down a phone — almost

### Added
- **A transfer and a disconnect case now carry a reference number**, allocated
  inside the transaction that creates the record, so neither can exist
  unnumbered even for a moment. Both surfaces show it in a leading **Reference**
  column.

### Known — and this is the honest half
- ⚠ **Neither has a NUMBER FORMAT yet, deliberately.** The rule this product
  holds itself to is that a seeded default is taken from what the prototype
  actually draws and never invented — the connection series is `CON-26-0110`
  because those screens draw exactly that. The transfer and disconnect screens
  draw **no reference column at all**; their rows are identified by account
  number on both sides. So the column exists, the allocation works, and the
  format is refused rather than guessed.
  Until it is ruled, a new record shows **the reason it has no number**, never
  a dash and never an invented one.
- ⚠ **And the two are not the same question.** The prototype draws a
  disconnection as a **work order** — `WO-4833` — so a disconnect case may not
  need a series of its own at all. That is why one of the two carries a
  recommendation and the other deliberately does not.

**Closing either is one catalogue row and no schema change.** That is what this
release bought.

## [2.59.0] — 2026-08-27 · a district can have sub-areas, and the demo stops being thinner than a real tenant

### Added
- **Sub-areas** (your question: *"Why you dont have sub areas below"*). A seeded
  tenant's Areas list goes from **4 to 7** — North district gains **NE** and
  **NW**, East district gains **SE**. Every list and picker shows the hierarchy
  rather than flattening it, because a picker that flattens a tree silently is
  how somebody assigns a premises to the wrong district.
  ⚠ **Downtown and Industrial corridor get none, on purpose.** Without a
  district that has no children, the "no sub-areas" wording and a plain district
  path could never be seen on a seeded tenant.

### Fixed
- **The second level of areas had been unreachable except by hand, and nothing
  said so.** The seeding handler read only a code and a name and **silently
  discarded every other field**, so a parent named in the fixture produced a
  top-level row and raised nothing. The column, the refusals, the delete
  protection and the picker had all been built and were reachable only by a
  person typing on a settings screen.
- **A seeded premises had no state** — hardcoded empty on all three seeding
  paths while the tenant's own record held the answer. It takes the tenant's
  declaration now, and stays blank when they declared none.

### Known
- **Six more fields the importer accepts are still not seeded**, and each is
  left blank on purpose with a question rather than filled with something
  plausible: a building **name** (the ones on file are owners, not buildings),
  an **external reference** (it would assert a prior system nobody named),
  **floor** and **square feet** (no dimensions are specified anywhere), and two
  **staff decisions** that are not derivable. A seeded value nobody chose is
  worse than a blank, because a demo makes it look decided.

## [2.58.0] — 2026-08-26 · a single reading in a modal, bulk accept, and usage per meter

⚠ **2.56.0 through 2.58.0 were all cut in one sitting**, because four waves were
merged back-to-back before any of their bumps was taken — the per-wave rule's
first day, and the integrator (me) batched it. Each wave still gets its OWN
number so a defect names one wave, which is what the rule is for; what slipped
is the timing, and it is stated rather than smoothed over. See DEF-822.

### Added
- **One reading, one modal.** A clerk with a single reading from the counter no
  longer walks a five-stage import. (Your words: *"if it is simple then modal"*.)
  ⚠ **It writes nothing of its own** — the reading goes through the same three
  steps a 1,247-row file does, and a test posts one counter reading and asserts
  it lands carrying a batch id, which is the proof there is no second write
  path. "Simple" is **measured** from the plan's own register set, and a set
  that cannot be resolved answers *not simple* rather than assuming one register.
- **Bulk accept on the reads list**, with the selection column that was missing.
  Every row gets the acting user, the reason and its own audit entry — your
  ruling: *"an auditor asking 'who chose to estimate M-4412?' gets a name"*.
  This also closes a gap open since 11 August: three fields for who fixed a row
  and why have been in the schema, and on screen, with nothing able to write them.
  ⚠ **Only Accept is bulk, and the screen says so.** An override is a supersede
  needing its own value and reason per reading, and one reason covering forty
  readings would be untrue of thirty-nine.
- **Twelve months of usage on the meter**, one chart per register.

### Fixed
- **A meter's monthly usage was adding up registers that measure different
  things.** A demand peak landed in the energy total and TOU windows were
  counted twice. Measured on the reported case: **698 → 684 kWh**, and the
  reading count 2 → 1, so the figure is no longer credited to more evidence than
  it had. An unclassified register now **refuses** rather than defaulting in —
  which matters this week, because `generation` was added the same morning and a
  default would have added a solar device's production to every site's usage.

### Known
- **Bulk estimate is built and has no button.** Its target list is a different
  selection model, and one selection meaning two things is how a clerk estimates
  the wrong meter. Left to the wave that owns that list.
- **The meter chart computes from readings rather than reading a stored row**,
  because the stored monthly row has no per-meter grain. The rules are literally
  the same functions, a test pins the two against each other, and the payload
  and the screen both say `computed from reads` rather than implying otherwise.

## [2.57.0] — 2026-08-26 · a new tenant's sample data speaks the services it sells

### Fixed
- ⛔ **A new tenant that does not sell water received an empty estate — no
  meters, and therefore no readings.** This is what you reported on two or three
  tenants. The sample estate was **water-only**, written into the fixture in two
  places that both said so, with no branch anywhere on which services the
  utility actually sells.
  The estate is now a **shape** and the service a **parameter**. Measured, per
  tenant mix: a water utility gets a water estate; an **electric and gas**
  utility gets an **electric** estate and gas is refused **by name**; a
  solar-only utility gets a stated refusal instead of silence. 49 meters and 189
  committed readings in each case, through the real upload pipeline — nothing
  inserts a reading behind it.
- **Master and sub-meters speak the tenant's service too.** Before this, a
  submetering utility selling electricity got no master meter and not one
  sub-meter, because every row named a service it did not have.
- **Two silent zeros in the seeder.** Seeding meters where no units exist
  reported success with a count of zero, and a meter whose unit was missing was
  dropped without a word. Both now say they could not run.

### Known
- **A non-water estate has consumption and no price.** There is no signed
  electric or gas tariff, and inventing one would be inventing money. The
  readings are real; what they cost waits on a tariff.
- **One metered service per estate.** An electric-and-gas utility gets an
  electric estate and gas refused by name; two would double the ready-to-run
  billing batch the sample exists to let you press.

## [2.56.0] — 2026-08-26 · the Missing count survives the chase days, and a disputed amount stops ageing

### Fixed
- **The Missing count dropped to zero on exactly the days a clerk chases
  stragglers.** It counted only open reading windows, so a cycle whose window
  closed on the 20th read **0** from the 21st — while sixty meters were still
  unread and the bill run was five days away. It now counts until the **bill run
  consumes the period**. Worked: four unread meters, window closed the 20th —
  the chip says **4** on the 22nd and **0** on the 26th once the run completes.
  (Your words: *"Keep counting until the run consumes the period — those are the
  chase days"*.)
- **The chip printed "this count is not built" underneath a live count**, and
  had since the count became real.

### Added
- **A disputed amount stops ageing while we investigate, and the rest of the
  bill ages normally.** Your ruling: *"the disputed amount doesn't age into late
  fees while open"*. Three worked figures: a **$184.20** bill with **$47.00**
  disputed ages **$137.20**; a **$1,000.00** bill with **$400.00** disputed
  earns a **$9.00** late fee instead of $15.00; and a **$60.00** bill with
  **$40.00** disputed leaves **$20.00** ageable — under the minimum, so **no fee
  at all**, where the un-excluded bill would have earned $5.00.
  The issued invoice is not touched, voided or held. It is issued money.

### Known
- ⚠ **Nothing in the product records HOW MUCH is disputed.** Measured across the
  repo: no column, no service, nothing writes one. So the arithmetic above is
  built and tested against a supplied figure, and an open dispute with **no**
  figure **refuses** rather than picking a side — the two available guesses are
  **$137.20 apart** on that first bill. That question is with you.

## [2.55.0] — 2026-08-26 · one rail for every upload, and three write modes

### Added

- **Reads upload joins the one import rail.** It used to have a wizard of its
  own; it now runs on the same five-stage workflow as premises, units, assets
  and accounts, which is the seventh thing that rail carries. Manual entry is a
  choice of transport on that same rail, not a second screen. (Your words:
  *"We need to follow tailwind wizard that we are using - i believe we are using
  same code for various"*.)
- **Three write modes, chosen at step 1** — *Insert new only · Insert & update ·
  Replace* — because what the file MEANS decides how every later stage judges
  it. Stage 4 now **states** the choice you made rather than offering it a
  second time.
  ⚠ **Replace supersedes; it never overwrites.** A correction is a new reading
  with the old one pointed at it, so the reading a bill was issued from stays
  exactly as it was — and a replace that meets a **billed** reading is
  **refused by name**, not silently skipped. Worked case: a 2-row corrections
  file where one row names a billed reading is refused by that reading's own
  name and date, the other row posts, and the receipt says `1 posted` with the
  refusal listed beside it.
- **A second person can co-sign a read batch.** The field for it has existed and
  been shown on screen since it shipped 16 days ago, with nothing able to write
  it. It writes now.

### Fixed

- **A read batch could report `posted` while posting nothing.** ⚠ **This turned
  out to already be fixed** — the register still said otherwise. The lane
  re-measured before re-fixing and found the product correct and the record
  stale: the batch raises on a count mismatch and answers `posted_nothing` with
  the skipped rows named. **The register was the stale thing, not the product.**

### Known

- ⚠ **`Replace` and `Insert & update` currently do the same thing to readings**,
  because the ruling's own words describe the same set of rows and what
  `replace` should do to readings on file but absent from the file has no
  answer we may guess. The mode is *recorded* on every batch, so whichever way
  it is ruled applies with no data migration. Deleting readings, and
  superseding them by nothing, are marked FORBIDDEN rather than offered.
- **The co-sign does not yet BLOCK a post** where a utility turns that on. The
  door and the record exist; the toggle's home is a settings screen another
  wave owns. The payload says so out loud rather than letting a screen assume.

## [2.54.0] — 2026-08-26 · a validation check can be switched off, and a reading says when one was

**The first release under the per-wave rule** (PO ruling 2026-08-26, *"We have
to bump version when major when minor so we are able to keep track of"*). One
wave, one version — so a defect reported against this build names this wave and
nothing else.

### Added

- **You can switch off a validation check that does not fit your business, per
  utility service.** Every check ships **ON** — nothing is disabled by a default
  nobody chose — and the checkbox is on the same Settings page as its threshold.
- ⚠ **Seven checks cannot be switched off, and the screen says so rather than
  greying them out.** *Meter must exist · meter not retired · unit must exist ·
  usage cannot be negative · rollover · duplicate reading · export on a
  non-net meter.* These are not judgments about your business — a reading
  against a meter that does not exist is not a matter of policy — so they render
  as **locked rows with the reason beside them**. A greyed-out control with no
  explanation reads as "broken"; this reads as "cannot be turned off".
  Attempting it through the API is **refused by name**, and forced back on
  inside the setting itself, so a script or a fixture cannot do it either.
- **A reading records that a check was switched off — it does not simply go
  quiet.** This is the part worth knowing: a check that vanished from a reading
  would be indistinguishable from a check that PASSED. So a switched-off check
  is **replaced, not dropped**, and the reading carries `disabled` with the
  reason *"disabled by tenant setting"*.
  ⚠ **It is deliberately kept separate from "could not evaluate".** That list is
  a **chase list** — it exists so a clerk can close a gap. A check you retired
  has nothing to chase, and mixing the two is how a chase list stops being read.
- **Switching a check on or off is written to the audit trail** with its own
  action, so an auditor asking who retired a check gets a name and a date.

### Fixed

- **The whole frontend had stopped parsing, and every test in it was red** — not
  failing, *unable to start*. A comment block had lost three characters in a
  merge, and the build refused the file. ⚠ The consequence worth recording: with
  that parse error present, the type-checker checked **nothing**, and repairing
  it revealed two real type errors that had been hiding behind it. A parse error
  is not one failure among many; it silences every other check on the file.
- **A shared page was flagged as broken by an internal check while being
  correct** — two independent lanes found it the same afternoon and both were
  right.

### Known

- **One new check can still be switched off that arguably should not be.** The
  check that stops a solar inverter's *generation* being filed as a customer's
  *consumption* is the exact mirror of one of the seven locked ones — same
  shape, same severity — but the seven were locked **by name**, and it was not
  among them. It stays switchable because that is what the ruling says. Worked
  case for the decision: *a solar inverter reports 612 kWh, and a utility can
  currently switch off the check that stops that being billed as usage.*

## [2.53.0] — 2026-08-26 · Meter Reads: reads that carry how they were taken, and a bill run that shows its work

⚠ **This is the LAST release that covers more than one wave, and it covers
ten.** From the next one, the version moves on **every wave** — PO ruling
2026-08-26, *"We have to bump version when major when minor so we are able to
keep track of"* — so a defect reported against a version will name one wave
instead of eleven. Assigning ten numbers to these ten retroactively would put
build numbers on deploys that never happened, so the seam is stated here rather
than smoothed over.

### Added

- **A reading now records HOW it was taken** — Manual, Walk-by, AMI, AMR or
  Mobile — chosen when you upload and overridable on any single row. Readings
  collected before this carry whatever the old system said, translated when they
  are read and **never rewritten**, because a committed reading is a record. ⚠
  Three old words — `drive_by`, `self_read`, `field_visit` — match none of the
  five, and rather than guess, those readings say **"not stated"** until you
  tell us what they should become.
- **Your utility's own shorthand for a service is accepted.** A file that says
  `E` for electric, `W` for water or `G` for gas now loads as if it had spelled
  the service out. ⚠ Where a single letter is genuinely ambiguous — `S` if you
  sell both **sewer** and **solar** — the import **refuses to choose** and names
  both, because a silently-picked service prices the wrong charge. The same file
  loads cleanly for a utility that sells only one of them.
- **The validation rules are editable, per utility service** (Settings). Every
  rule ships with a starting value; a water threshold and an electric threshold
  are separate numbers, because 1 kgal and 50 kWh are not the same kind of
  large.
- **The bill run shows its reasoning about readings before you bill.**
  Estimated · High · Low · Days · Meter factor · Replacements · True-up — each a
  tab you can work through. ⚠ The Replacements tab says out loud that a meter
  swap is **inferred**, not recorded, so you can disagree with it.
- **Readings are taken at move-in, move-out, transfer, disconnect and new
  connect**, and each one records **which event produced it and who took it**.
  An auditor asking who recorded a closing figure gets a name.
- **A master meter's reading is reconciled against the sum of its sub-meters,
  and the gap is STORED** rather than absorbed into a bill. Worked case: a
  master reading **12,400 kWh** against **11,940 kWh** of sub-meters leaves
  **460 kWh (3.71%)** recorded against a 3% tolerance — a number somebody can be
  asked about. Device readings are collected too.
- **A demand reading carries its reset**, and a peak is never added to an energy
  total. ⚠ See *Known* below — the unit a peak is stored in is still wrong.
- **The reading detail is a page, not a side panel** (your ruling: *"i want page
  to be open for consitency - we dont open side panel"*). Old links still work.
- **A route sheet prints** from the walk order you already set.
- **The Missing count keeps counting through the days you chase stragglers.** It
  used to drop to **0** the moment a reading window closed — which is exactly
  when a clerk is chasing. Worked case: a cycle of 1,240 meters whose window
  shut on the 20th with 60 unread now still says 60 on the 22nd, and stops only
  when the bill run consumes that period.
- **Correcting a reading corrects the ones after it.** Where the next reading is
  not yet billed it is recomputed as a new superseding row; where it IS billed,
  the product recommends the correction rather than making it, because issued
  money does not change by itself.
- **Tenant setup now says which step failed, and why.** Each of the eleven setup
  jobs reports its own outcome with an error code, a failed step writes to that
  tenant's audit trail so it can be traced later (your ruling), and a single
  failure no longer costs you the rest of the setup — you can retry just that
  step.

### Fixed

- **A solar customer's real consumption never reached a bill.** A net meter
  records both what you used and what you exported; once an export row existed
  beside it, the billing read filter dropped **both**, and the account billed as
  though no reading existed. **684 kWh** of real usage, on every net meter.
- **The move-in and move-out tabs printed "no readings" over readings they had
  been served.**
- **The reads upload template shipped with its example row one column out** — a
  reading method that read `Access ok`. Two changes to the same file, each
  correct alone.
- **Two internal checks had been passing over real failures.** The
  migration-safety check had been red for days while every report said green,
  because nothing ran it; and the check that lists which record numbers are
  actually issued had drifted eight series out of date, while naming three as
  unused that are in use. Neither was visible to anyone.
- **Version 2.52.0 shipped with no changelog entry** — written by hand
  afterwards, and **a gate now refuses that**: a version literal that moves with
  no matching entry fails the build. Proven against the exact case it missed.

### Known, and stated rather than hidden

- ⚠ **A demand charge is mis-billed today.** A demand meter records a *peak rate
  of draw* (kW), not a *quantity of energy* (kWh), and the product currently
  says both — it stores the peak in the meter's kWh while pricing it per kW. A
  **412 kW** peak bills at **$154.00** where the correct charge is
  **$4,532.00**. The unit and the quantity are both wrong and are fixed
  together; the decision is with the Product Owner.
- **The sample estate a new tenant receives is water-only.** It is written into
  the fixture in two places that both say so, with no branch on which services
  the utility actually sells — so an electric-and-gas tenant receives no meters
  and therefore no readings. This is the leading explanation for sample reads
  not appearing on new tenants, and the fix is in progress.
- **The import rail is still five separate wizards.** Uploading readings, the
  write modes (insert · insert-and-update · replace), and the batch that reports
  `posted` over rows that did not land are all in flight, not shipped.

## [2.52.0] — 2026-08-26 · the import stops printing database keys at you, and a plan matches by its name

⚠ **This entry was written on 2026-08-26, after 2.52.0 had already been cut**
(DEF-806). The build number went into `package.json`, `package-lock.json` and
`pyproject.toml` in lockstep and no changelog entry went with it, which is the
one thing §7 rule 4 of the change process says a gate must refuse. Written from
the commits in the range rather than from memory.

### Added
- **A premises' available services can be set on screen** (CR-036 h). They were
  loadable by import and editable nowhere, so a wrong value could only be fixed
  by importing the file again.
- **A unit's services come from its premises** (BR-MET-119). The Product Owner
  ruled the ORDER rather than the column: **Premises → Units → Meters**. A unit
  does not carry its own list — it shows what its premises makes available, so
  the two can never disagree. ⚠ **The third link is NOT enforced**: a meter can
  still be tagged to a service the unit's premises does not offer. That cost was
  stated before it was built, not discovered afterwards.
- **The Waiting-on list folds into the six worklists** (CR-035 amendment 1)
  rather than standing as a seventh tab. Parked jobs appear where the jobs are.

### Fixed
- **The import receipt printed database keys at a clerk** (DEF-767). The PO, on
  the deployed 2.51.0 receipt: *"We get database keys on this screen"* — a
  64-character rollback uuid and a full file hash, on a screen a billing clerk
  reads. The rollback id is **deleted**, not shortened: nothing was ever
  actionable through it. ⚠ The test covering that row PASSED, because it asked
  whether six fields were PRESENT and its expected content was the uuid. A
  presence check cannot answer a legibility question.
- **The units import asked for "Plan" and matched only on CODE** (DEF-771), so a
  file naming plans the way a human names them loaded **9,881 units unplanned**.
  A plan now matches by code **or** by name, case-folded, and the column says
  which it took. Where a name matches more than one published plan the import
  **refuses to choose** and names both — it does not reject your row; the unit
  loads unplanned and flagged, exactly as before.
- **The import took 38 seconds and 38 of them were ours** (CR-036 e). Measured
  rather than guessed, on the PO's own shape — 9,881 units against 9,957
  premises: work **37.98s**, queue **0.11s**. Neither the queue nor the
  database. Units transform+validate now runs in **5.25s**, output proved
  byte-identical row by row.
- **The import now says what it knows and stops promising what it will not do**
  (DEF-750/751/752/754). The sentence that would have prevented the whole
  incident is now on the screen before you commit: *"Services available —
  mapped from SERVICES_AVAILABLE, and blank in all 9,881 rows. Nothing will be
  written to it."* **Matched is about the heading, never about the cells.**
- **Two controls for one setting** (DEF-770). The write mode was chosen at step 1
  and offered again at stage 4, with no answer about which one wins. Stage 4 now
  STATES the choice and hands you back to step 1 to change it.
- **A move-in with no counts took the whole screen down** (DEF-757), and the
  **Transfers tab whited out the screen** (DEF-781). Both found by clicking, not
  by a test.
- **The 2-second poll was shipping 4 MB** (DEF-766) on every tick of a running
  import.
- **Four services rendered as slugs and months rendered as numbers** (DEF-763,
  DEF-753), and **Jurisdiction read as a paragraph** where it should read
  *"Inside city limits"* (DEF-507).
- **The tool that recovers lost translation keys was corrupting every non-ASCII
  character it touched** (DEF-768) — every accented and non-Latin locale.

### Known, and stated rather than hidden
- **Park is inert on five of the six wizards** (DEF-746) while BR-SHL-048 says
  every wizard parks, and **a park reminder is stored and delivered nowhere**
  (DEF-758). CR-035 is recorded as NOT fully done for exactly this reason; a
  green tick over it would have been false.
- **The import screen still promises a skip that does not fire** (DEF-750). The
  `Insert new only` skip is assigned in one place and read in none, so a
  re-import reaches every row while the screen says otherwise. Open.
- **A saved column set never gains a column added after it was saved**
  (DEF-784). Invisible to every check we own, because the failing case needs a
  user WITH history: every test and every fresh browser starts from no
  preference and gets the full set. This is the one mechanism by which a column
  can still be missing on a live tenant.

## [2.51.0] — 2026-08-26 · a half-finished job can be parked, and the import stops misleading you

### Added
- **Park now works on every wizard** (CR-035). The Product Owner: *"in practical
  life all these requests do not close in a day, hence users generally park
  them."* A move-in, move-out, transfer, disconnect or new connect can be set
  aside with **what you are waiting for**, a note and a reminder date, and picked
  up later at the step you left — with everything you had typed still in it.
  A **Waiting on** list shows every parked job, its reason, its reminder and
  **how long it has been sitting**.
  **A parked job changes nothing** (BR-SHL-048, PO ruling: *"until move-in
  executed, no records updates"*). Park a move-in for Unit 12 on 26 August and
  come back on 2 September: in between, Unit 12 still reads **Vacant**, no
  account exists, nothing is billed differently. A parked draft is a saved form
  and appears in your Waiting-on list and nowhere else.
  ⚠ **The cost, stated rather than hidden:** a parked move-OUT is invisible to
  the rest of the product, so that account **keeps billing** until the job is
  finished. The reminder date and the visible age are what stop a draft sitting
  forever.
  Everything it does is re-checked when you resume — what was true when you
  parked may not be true a week later.

### Fixed
- **The `Fix here` button on a rejected import row did nothing** (CR-036 b).
  It did work — it just took over a second to respond on a 9,881-row file, so
  the second click closed what the first had opened. The list is paginated now
  (**189ms instead of 3.6s**) and the control no longer closes what it opened.
- **The validate screen contradicted itself and read as total failure**
  (CR-036 f). Mid-run it showed `ROWS CHECKED 0 · ERRORS 0` beside a bar reading
  *16% complete*; a count that has not been computed is now an **em-dash**. On a
  finished run it showed `PASSED CLEAN 0 · WARNINGS 9881`, which reads as
  *nothing succeeded* when in fact **nothing was blocked** — so `Passed clean`
  is retired and a **`Will load`** count takes its place. It is exact, not an
  estimate.
- **The write mode is chosen at step 1** (CR-036 g), not at the final confirm.
  PO: *"this is important decision how you will process the data."* It decides
  what the file MEANS — a load, a correction or a replacement — and steps 2 and
  3 were already judging your file against an assumption nobody had asked you to
  make. Step 3 now names it: *"Checked as 'Insert & update', the choice made at
  step 1."* You can still change it at the dry run.

## [2.50.2] — 2026-08-26 · a clerk can find an account, and every Accounts tab offers the thing it lists

### Fixed
- **The transfer wizard asked a clerk to type an internal id** (DEF-732). The
  Product Owner opened it, typed **`AC-2026-00025`** — the account number every
  list, KPI tile and detail header in this product prints — and was told *"That
  account could not be read"*. Nothing was broken at any line: `GET /accounts/{id}`
  correctly failed to find a uuid that was never a uuid, and the field's own help
  text admitted what it wanted (*"The account id. There is no search-as-you-type
  behind this box yet"*). The screen asked the wrong question, got a correct
  answer, and showed a message that read like a system fault — which made step 1
  impossible to complete and the whole transfer flow unreachable in practice.
  **The box is now a search.** Type the account number, the customer's name or
  the service address, pick the account from the matches, and step 1 completes —
  through the search this product has published since W2 (`GET /accounts?q=`,
  BR-CUS-053), not a new endpoint. **A pasted account id still resolves**, so
  nothing that used to work stopped working.
  **The identical field on the disconnect wizard is fixed with it** — the same
  box, the same help text, and the thing behind it cuts a customer's service.
  Those two are the only screens in the product that take an account by hand;
  the other four wizards receive it from the account they were opened from.
  ⚠ **"No account matches that" and "that account could not be read" are now
  different sentences**, because they are different facts and a clerk can act on
  only one of them. A term that finds nothing says so; the fault sentence is left
  for a real fault.
- **Four Accounts tabs listed work with no way to start any** (DEF-729, DEF-730).
  The Product Owner walked the deployed build and found the same hole four
  times: *"new request - no button to add new request"*, *"new connect - no
  button"*, *"Move in - no button to add Movein"*, *"Move out - no button"*.
  **The page's one primary slot now carries the active tab's create action** —
  `+ New request`, `+ New connect`, `+ New transfer`, `Start a disconnect` —
  which is what the design draws, and it relabels rather than multiplying, so
  one screen still has exactly one primary. New connect rows also gained the
  eye that opens them.
  **Move-in and move-out stay disabled and the reason is real:** both wizards
  are built, but a move-in creates the next occupant of *a particular account's*
  unit, and no account is chosen in this header. The live control is on the
  account's own page, and the disabled button says so.
  ⚠ One of these was **the product contradicting itself**: the new-connect
  button was greyed out saying *"the new-connect wizard is not built yet"* on a
  build where it was built and routed.
- **The move-in and move-out lists explained themselves in our words, not the
  clerk's** (DEF-731 — the Product Owner quoted the screen back to us). Under
  the table a clerk read *"`services.move_out` writes `closed_at` …
  `MOVE_OUT_FIELDS` will not even accept a date to park"*. It now reads: *"A
  move-out that has not gone through yet is not kept anywhere, so this list
  shows only the ones already closed. An account whose move-out is still being
  arranged is open and still billing, and it is not listed here."* Twenty-two
  such sentences were rewritten, and five of them stopped being red — an
  absence is not an error, and only three red strips remain, for the three real
  failures.

### Changed — internal, no user-visible behaviour
- **Four quality gates could not see the code they were reading** (DEF-741).
  They stripped block comments before line comments, so a `//` line spelling a
  path with a star in it opened a comment that ran to the next `*/` below —
  3,608 bytes of real code invisible across eight files, reported as PASS. Fixed
  and proved: a planted violation drew zero hits from the shipped gate and a
  named failure from the fixed one. Gate output on the real tree is unchanged,
  so nothing was hiding that mattered today.

## [2.50.1] — 2026-08-26 · a bill carrying a late fee can be sent

### Fixed
- **A bill with a late fee on it could not be sent at all** (DEF-719, closing
  the last half of DEF-201, open since 17 August). A clerk applied a late fee on
  the bill run's exception step, the draft assembled and looked correct, and the
  bill then died at release with *"a fee line ('Late fee') names no charge
  code"* — and no clerk could fix it on a screen, because the line named nothing
  to point anywhere. It now names the utility's own **LATE** charge code, and
  the fee books to whatever account that code points at (BR-BIL-075, PO ruling
  2026-08-26: *"A · The late fee uses a tenant charge code — like NSF and
  reconnect already do"*).
  **Worked, on the reference bill:** electricity $82.08 + base $18.50 = $100.58,
  late fee **$8.13**, tax $8.30 (charged on the $100.58 only — a fee is never
  taxed), **total $117.01**, with the $8.13 credited to *4200 Late-fee revenue*
  — or to **4210**, or anywhere else the utility points their LATE code, which
  is the whole reason this shape was chosen over hard-wiring 4200.
  ⚠ **The charge code says WHERE the fee goes and never WHAT IT IS.** The
  amount stays the signed late-fee rule — `max($5.00, 1.5% × overdue portion)` —
  so a utility that puts a flat amount on their LATE code is still charged
  $8.13, not that amount. Changing that figure needs a finance re-sign.
  ⚠ **One thing a utility must do before this works for them:** point the LATE
  code at an account (Taxes & fees → charge codes → GL account). The code is
  created for every utility; the account is not chosen for them, and until it is
  the bill says so by name and the rest of the run still goes out.

## [2.50.0] — 2026-08-26 · what a discount asks of a customer, and the month a staff screen opens on

### Added
- **The unit Plan tab now shows what a customer must SATISFY to get each
  discount the plan offers**, not only that one exists (CR-034 §7, PO 2026-08-26:
  *"We should show all discount plan offer and what condition are required to
  avail that discount ; when account is attached it will avail those
  discounts"*). Per discount: who qualifies, how it is granted, which documents
  are accepted and whether the reduction waits for them, how it is kept
  (recertification and what happens on lapse), what it reduces, the most it can
  take off, how low it may drive a bill, and whether it can be held beside
  another. Worked, on Silver Creek's SENIOR: *Age 65+ · the customer applies and
  staff approve · Government ID or Birth certificate · nothing comes off a bill
  until the proof is on file · recertified every 12 months with 60 days' notice ·
  at most $20.00 off one bill · the bill cannot go below $0.00 · not alongside
  another assistance discount*.
  **Every figure is a stored value forwarded from rating; nothing is computed.**
- **And the screen says that nothing CHECKS those conditions.** The eligibility
  rule is stored as authored and no code evaluates it, so each condition carries
  *"Nothing in this product checks this condition. Staff confirm it when the
  account is enrolled."* A clerk who believed the software was refusing
  unqualified customers would stop checking, and it refuses nobody.

### Changed
- **The staff Plan tab now opens on the CURRENT MONTH** rather than *as of
  today* (PO 2026-08-26: *"B Default to this month"*). ⚠ **The move-in wizard is
  deliberately unchanged** and still answers *as of today* with no period: on the
  25th a month-END date resolves a rate version effective the 28th, which is the
  right answer for staff asking about this month and the wrong one to show a
  customer who is signing up. The endpoint invents no period either way.
- The discounts on this screen now resolve on the same service date as the plan
  and the rate schedules above them, instead of on the day the screen is open.

## [2.49.1] — 2026-08-26 · the danger tier reaches the confirm dialogs

### Fixed
- **Every destructive confirm in the product committed through a button styled
  exactly like Save** (DEF-718) — delete, retire, archive, deactivate, roll
  back, remove, across **30 dialogs**. B14's danger tier had no way to reach
  `ConfirmDialog`'s confirm button, so, as with DEF-712 the night before, the
  rule was *unfollowable* rather than unfollowed.
  **It is a classification, not a sweep:** 21 confirms now carry the tier, 3
  compute it (one dialog serves *deactivate* and *reactivate*, *archive* and
  *publish*, *disable* and *enable*), and **6 keep the ordinary primary on
  purpose** — a bulk apply, a send, two rate-change confirms, a forward-only
  counter reset and a currency change. A warning colour on every dialog is a
  warning colour nobody reads.
- **The retire wizard's commit — "Retire M-4204 ✓" — was the standard primary**,
  where *retire* is the danger rule's own second example.

## [2.49.0] — 2026-08-26 · the fee line, the danger tier, and what a unit is priced on

### Fixed
- **A tenant that configured any recurring or auto-apply charge code could not
  issue ANY bill** (DEF-714) — every bill in the run, not just the one carrying
  the fee. Live since the 22 Aug ruling that put recurring charges on the bill.
  The charge id was being dropped at **seven** hops; each now carries it.
  Worked: a $12.00 monthly service fee books to **4210**, and tax stays
  **$8.30, not $9.29**, because a fee is not taxed.
  **DEF-201 was the same defect, open since 17 Aug with this exact fix written
  in its own prevention column.** Closed by the same change.
- **A disconnection committed through a button styled exactly like Save**
  (DEF-712). B14's danger tier had no way to reach a wizard's commit, so the
  rule was *unfollowable* rather than unfollowed.
- **S90 told a clerk a cut account was "still accruing base charges"**
  (DEF-716) — made false by the 25 Aug ruling that base stops at the cut.
- **2.48.0 bumped one version literal of four** (DEF-720). The backend and the
  lockfile still read 2.47.0, so the product could not say which build it was.
- One rule id claimed by two different rules, neither registered (DEF-711).

### Added
- **The unit's Plan tab now shows what the unit is actually priced on**
  (CR-034) — for a stated period: plan and version, services, rate schedule per
  service, minimum charges, charge codes with their amounts, discounts, taxes,
  and the contract section citing CR-020 as paused.
  **Ask about 1–31 July and every rate shown is the one in force on 31 July.**
  A mid-period plan change shows **both** stretches rather than picking one.
  Nothing on this screen is computed — every figure is a stored value.
- A sixth account status, **`Disconnected`** (BR-CUS-107), seeded and
  backfilled to existing tenants.

### Known issues
- **Nothing assigns the new `Disconnected` status yet**, so a cut account still
  reads *"Marked disconnect / billable"* (DEF-701). Assigning it today would
  make the cut customer's address read vacant to another move-in, and would
  drop the whole account from billing so the usage consumed **before** the cut
  would never be billed. Blocked on **OQ-386**.
- **A bill carrying an applied late fee still cannot be issued** (DEF-719) —
  awaiting a ruling on where it books.
- **A cut customer can be reconnected $75.00 short** (DEF-708).
- **30 destructive confirm dialogs are still on the primary tier** (DEF-718).
- A cut customer can be flipped back to Active through the API, around the
  reconnect flow (DEF-721).

## [2.48.0] — 2026-08-25 · CR-030 W5–W7 · the worklists, the wizards, and two money rulings

⚠ **The changelog's last entry was `2.40.3` while `package.json` read `2.47.0`.**
Seven releases shipped without an entry — the exact step the change process says
is "many times not followed correctly", which is why a gate refuses a CR marked
done with no version. This entry covers the span.

### Added
- **Every Accounts tab has a body.** The strip went from two built tabs to eight:
  Accounts · Requests · New connects · Move-ins · Move-outs · Transfers ·
  Disconnects · Imports.
- **New Connect**: the nine-step wizard (S87) and the connection detail (S88),
  with `GET /connections/{id}` and three write doors behind them.
- **Transfer and disconnect wizards** (`TRF-02`, `DSC-02`), five steps each.
- **The work-order templates page** ships deliberately blank and says why —
  Work is out of scope, and a page that states its own absence beats both a
  dead link and a screen filed in the wrong module.
- **J26 activated**; J27/J28/J29 written as handoff contracts, not yet activated.

### Changed — money, and both are PO rulings of 2026-08-25
- **Base charges STOP at the cut** (BR-CUS-103). A plan with an $18.50 standing
  charge, cut 15 June: June serves 15/30 → **$9.25**, July → **$0.00**. Before
  this, a cut customer paid $18.50 a month for a service that was off.
- **The reconnection fee is owed AT THE CUT** (BR-CUS-104), so arrears plus the
  fee must clear before reconnection. ⚠ **Not yet posted — see Known issues.**
- **A service request's age accents at seven days** (BR-CUS-106), closing a
  decision the design could only bound between 6 and 11.

### Known issues
- **A tenant that configures any recurring or auto-apply charge code cannot
  issue any bill** (DEF-714). Fee lines are assembled and then refused at issue.
- **A cut customer can be reconnected $75.00 short** (DEF-708) — the fee is
  recorded on the case and reaches no ledger, so the gate cannot see it.
- **A cut account still reads "Marked disconnect / billable"** (DEF-701): no
  account status means "off", and naming its class is still an open ruling.

## [2.40.3] — 2026-08-23 · CR-029 · the seven rulings built

### Added
- Bill runs get a real number series — RUN-0001 onward, forward-only; a refused run burns no number. Existing runs stay unnumbered.
- Cycles anchored on the 29th–31st now generate: the window clamps to the month's last day (28 Feb, 29 Feb in a leap year) and returns to its anchor the following month.
- A cycle whose days-to-complete exceeds its own repeat now WARNS instead of refusing; if the operator overrides, the overlapping windows are generated for real.

### Changed
- When a cycle's first-run date disagrees with its start day, the FIRST RUN anchors the schedule. The screens show the effective day and name the saved one beside it ("15 (saved 1)") rather than printing a day the engine ignores.
- A run with no typed bill date falls back to the cycle's bill day in the month AFTER the period ends — bill day 5, period 1–31 Aug, 21 days to pay → bills 5 Sep, due 26 Sep. Still a default a clerk may override.

### Removed
- `cycles.bill_date` — the sixth and last legacy cycle column.
- The reader on a closed read window: the column, the payload keys and the argument. The route's read history no longer shows or stores who walked it. `routes.assigned_to` and the Reads tab's existing display are unaffected.

### Notes
- Areas are geography only: a route is created and edited in exactly one place, the routes registry (BR-MET-103).
- OQ-345 opened by the overlap ruling: when two windows are open, which one a reading belongs to is not yet decided; the ambiguous case refuses rather than guessing.

## [2.40.2] — 2026-08-23 · CR-029 wave W5 · the close

### Added
- The cycle wizard's Schedule step is the RULED one at last: **Start day · Days
  to complete · Bill day · Due days**, and the frequency picker offers all
  **eight** business words (Daily · Weekly · Fortnightly · Monthly · Bimonthly ·
  Quarterly · Semiannual · Annual). It had shipped writing the superseded
  day-of-month pair and offering three lowercase CR-006 values, so a utility
  that bills weekly could not say so.
- The cycles export carries frequency, start day and days-to-complete beside the
  window, so the file can be used to reconstruct the schedule it describes.

### Changed
- **One naming grammar, end to end (D5).** The sample-records plant minted
  `SCW-M` / `SCW-R1` for every tenant that took sample data — a second grammar
  beside `CY-001` / `RT-001`, and on the demo tenant the SCW row was the one
  holding every account. It allocates from the number series now, carries the
  three ruled schedule fields and a real service set, and stops writing three
  deprecated columns.
- **Five deprecated cycle columns are dropped** (`window_start`, `window_end`,
  `read_day_from`, `read_day_to`, `due_day`). The read window is derived for
  every cycle; the due fact is `due_days`. `bill_date` STAYS — billing reads it
  as a fallback and nothing rules what replaces it.
- `GET /routes` and `GET /cycles` answer the paged envelope to every caller; the
  transitional bare-array branch is retired on both sides.
- Five backend refusals speak in their own sentences instead of a borrowed key.

### Fixed
- **The Cycles sub-tab lost six of its nine columns** for anyone who landed on
  Routes first and clicked across — which is everyone. The two tables shared one
  React component and therefore one column-visibility state, so the switch left
  the intersection: Cycle # · Name · Actions. Found in a browser and by nothing
  else.

### Notes
- The dashboard's transitional day-of-month fallback is gone with the columns. A
  cycle with no first-run date is now SKIPPED rather than counted down to, and
  `closed — bill run pending` is unreachable: BR-REP-027's four cycle states are
  two plus `not configured`.
- Three amendments are owed to signed rules and are reported, not taken:
  BR-REP-027 (the four states), BR-MET-009 (the window clause), and a new open
  question — what bill date a run inherits from a cycle that holds a bill DAY.

## [2.40.1] — 2026-08-23 · CR-029 waves W0–W3 · the calendar ticks

### Added
- The period engine: a cycle derives its next windows from start day + frequency + days-to-complete, computed on demand — no cron, no stored rows. The bill-run wizard offers the next period and never forces it.
- Read windows became closable records (window · read-on · reader · collected · expected · skips · result), idempotent per route and period.
- Route detail (SET-06D) and cycle detail (SET-07D) exist for the first time, five tabs each, with per-premises drag-to-reorder and a printable route sheet.
- Both landings rebuilt as Routes | Cycles sub-tabs; both wizards are addressable URLs, so a refresh no longer loses a four-step flow.
- `DataTable` gained expandable rows (kit capability FE-02, B13 amended).

### Changed
- Routes serve a service SET; walking order is per premises; exclusions carry a reason; a run may override the cycle's due-days default.
- The dashboard countdown counts to the next cycle date. The "last completed cycle" claim is REMOVED rather than guessed — the default window falls to the last 30 days.

### Notes
- Three schedule situations deliberately produce nothing rather than a guess, each awaiting a ruling: OQ-339 (a 31st in February), OQ-340 (first run disagreeing with start day), OQ-341 (days-to-complete longer than the period).
- Tailwind: the two un-migrated Routes & Cycles screens went from 16 bespoke classes to 0; no stylesheet was touched.

## [2.40.0] — 2026-08-23 · CR-029 opens · Routes & Cycles

### Added
- CR-029 captured with the PO's words verbatim: the upgraded prototype's route and cycle surfaces become the reference for these screens (r10 is history here), and thirteen decisions are ruled (G0, D1–D13).
- Design record `04-docs/02-decisions/17-cr029-routes-cycles-design.md` (B17): per-screen specs, the dynamism audit, the gap list, and the six-wave plan.

### Changed
- Routes and cycles are grouping only, hardened: a cycle captures start day · frequency (eight one-word business names) · days to complete, and the reading window is derived, never stored.

### Notes
- Four places where the PO's rulings supersede the upgraded prototype's own copy are stamped in the CR record (D6 reader out of scope · D9 bill/due days stay on the cycle as run-overridable defaults · D12 no balance column · D13 no account-level cycle assignment).

- Inventory: uninstalled stock by type with counts and costs, drilling to the

- Lifecycle: certifications falling due, warranty cover by group, the age &
